Lore/Cosmology/The-Emerald-Dream.title: The Emerald Dream
Lore/Cosmology/The-Emerald-Dream.content:
The Emerald Dream
Azeroth as it would have been if no thinking creature had ever touched it. A vast, verdant mirror-world overlaid on the waking one, shaped by Ysera and the Green Dragonflight, and the source of all druidic power.
How It Works

Druids enter through the Emerald Enchantment — a sleep that can last centuries
The Cenarion Circle maintains Barrow Dens at Moonglade and Teldrassil where sleepers’ bodies lie
Time runs strangely. A night elf may sleep a thousand years and wake having missed everything.
Green dragons guard the portals — Ashenvale, Feralas, the Hinterlands, Duskwood

Malfurion
Malfurion Stormrage, the first druid and the Alliance’s greatest asset, is in there. His body sleeps; his spirit is trapped. Tyrande Whisperwind has been waiting four years. Fandral Staghelm presides over the Cenarion Circle in his absence, and does not seem in a hurry to get him back.
Related
Ysera · Cenarion Circle · Malfurion Stormrage · Wailing Caverns · Moonglade · The Old Gods · Fandral Staghelm

Lore/Cosmology/The-Holy-Light.title: The Holy Light
Lore/Cosmology/The-Holy-Light.content:
The Holy Light
Not a god. A philosophy — and one that, inexplicably and reliably, works.
The Three Virtues

Respect — all things have worth
Tenacity — persist despite adversity
Compassion — the two above, turned outward

The Church of the Holy Light teaches that by holding these truths, a person aligns themselves with the fundamental benevolence of creation, and creation answers. It heals. It burns undead. It has never once explained itself.
Institutions

The Church of the Holy Light — Stormwind Cathedral, Northshire Abbey, the human heartland
The Order of the Silver Hand — the paladin order founded by Uther the Lightbringer in the Second War. Shattered. Arthas disbanded it; Uther is dead; its survivors are scattered between the Argent Dawn and the Scarlet Crusade.
Dwarven faith — Ironforge adopted the Light through Alliance contact; Dwarves make devout, pragmatic paladins

The Shadow
The Light’s opposite is not evil — it is the Void, drawn on by shadow priests and warlocks. Forsaken and troll priests wield it openly. Human priests are taught both and warned about one.


                  
                  The Forsaken problem 
                  
                

Forsaken priests can channel the Light, and it hurts them to do it. Undead flesh recoils from it. A Forsaken priest who heals an ally is choosing agony. This is excellent characterization and worth surfacing.


Related
Uther the Lightbringer · Order of the Silver Hand · Scarlet Crusade · Argent Dawn · Tirion Fordring · Arthas Menethil

Lore/Cosmology/The-Twisting-Nether.title: The Twisting Nether
Lore/Cosmology/The-Twisting-Nether.content:
The Twisting Nether
The chaotic void between worlds — a churning purple immaterium of raw magic where demons are born, where they return when killed, and across which the Burning Legion sails its endless crusade.
Key Facts

Demons do not truly die on Azeroth. Kill one and its essence returns to the Nether to re-form. Permanent destruction requires killing them in the Nether — which is why Illidan Stormrage and others obsess over reaching it.
Warlocks draw summoned demons through the Nether. Every summoning punches a small hole in reality.
Portals — the Dark Portal is a stable Nether-tunnel between Azeroth and Draenor
Draenor was shattered by Ner’zhul opening too many portals at once; its remnant, Outland, now hangs in the Nether

Related
The Burning Legion · Dark Portal · Blasted Lands · Classes of Azeroth · Ner’zhul

Lore/History/A-Short-History-of-Azeroth.title: A Short History of Azeroth
Lore/History/A-Short-History-of-Azeroth.content:
A Short History of Azeroth


                  
                  What this is 
                  
                

The history your character already knows, in the order they would have learned it. No secrets, no twists — just the background any reasonably informed person in Year 29 would have picked up from stories, schooling, or being there.
Read it once before session zero. You do not need to memorise it. Nobody is going to quiz you.




                  
                  How the years are counted 
                  
                

Everyone dates from the day the Dark Portal opened and the orcs came through. That was Year 0. It is now Year 29.
Before that, dates get vague and people say things like “three centuries back” or “before the Sundering.” The further back you go, the less anyone agrees.



Three Kinds of History
A person in Year 29 holds the past at three different distances, and knows it very differently at each one.





















DistanceWhat It Feels LikeMyth — ten thousand years agoStories. Half-believed. Only the night elves claim to remember it, and they were there.The grandparents’ wars — 30 to 1,000 years agoDocumented, argued over, still politically live. Your grandfather fought in some of it.What you lived through — the last six yearsRaw. Everyone has a personal version and most of them are still angry.

Part One · Myth


                  
                  The honest summary 
                  
                

Nobody knows how much of this is true. The night elves say they were there. Everyone else finds that hard to argue with and slightly irritating.


The World Was Made
The stories say titans — enormous beings of metal and light — came to an unfinished world, put it in order, and left. They built vaults and cities underground and then went away and never came back.
You can go and look at the vaults. Uldaman in the Badlands is one, and dwarven expeditions are digging it out right now. This part is not really in dispute. What the titans actually wanted, and whether they are coming back, absolutely is.
The Well and the War
Ten thousand years ago there was one continent and a lake of raw magic at the centre of it called the Well of Eternity. The night elf empire grew up around it and grew powerful and, most people agree, unbearable.
Their queen and her court dug too deep into that power and opened a door. Through it came the Burning Legion — a demonic army whose entire purpose is unmaking worlds.
The war that followed is called The War of the Ancients. The night elves won, barely, at a cost that reset the map.
The Sundering
The Well exploded. The single continent broke apart into the ones that exist now — the Eastern Kingdoms in the east, Kalimdor in the west, and a great deal of ocean in between where the middle used to be.
That event is called The Sundering, and it is the dividing line. Everything before it is myth. Everything after it is history.
The surviving night elves withdrew into the forests, swore off the magic that had caused it, and did not speak to anyone else for ten thousand years.

Part Two · The Grandparents’ Wars
Trolls Were Here First
Before anyone else, the continents belonged to troll empires — enormous, old, and now mostly ruins. Almost every city standing today is built on top of something a troll built first.
Roughly two and a half thousand years ago, humans and the exiled high elves fought the trolls back together in The Troll Wars. That alliance produced the human kingdom of Arathor, and the high elves taught humans arcane magic as payment.
Every troll alive knows this history and is, without exception, still furious about it.
Seven Human Kingdoms
Arathor eventually split into seven states — Stormwind, Lordaeron, Gilneas, Alterac, Stromgarde, Kul Tiras, and Dalaran. They spent centuries squabbling with each other in the ordinary way of neighbours.
The Portal Opens — Year 0
On the world of Draenor, the orcs were shamanic clan-people. Then the Burning Legion got to them, fed them demon blood, and turned them into an army.
A portal opened between the worlds. The orcs came through it into the swamps south of Stormwind.
The First and Second Wars
The First War (Years 0–5) — the orcs destroyed Stormwind. Refugees fled north by sea.
The Second War (Years 6–8) — the northern kingdoms formed the first Alliance and, with the high elves and dwarves, drove the orcs back. Lordaeron’s forces broke the Horde. The Knights of the Silver Hand were founded in this war and it is the thing they are proudest of.
The Invasion of Draenor (Years 17–18) — an Alliance expedition went through the Portal to finish the job. Draenor came apart while they were on it. Most of them never came home.
The Camps
The orcs who surrendered were put in internment camps and kept there for the better part of twenty years.


                  
                  Nobody agrees about this 
                  
                

The Alliance memory: we could not release a demon-controlled army back into the world, we fed and housed them, and it was more mercy than they showed at Stormwind.
The Horde memory: a generation was born behind a fence. Our language was not taught. Our shamans died in there. Whatever our fathers did, we did not do it, and we were still in the camp.
Both of these are true at once. This argument is not settled and it comes up constantly.



Part Three · What You Lived Through
Thrall
A young orc named Thrall was raised in captivity as a human noble’s gladiator, escaped, found the last free clan, and learned the shamanism his people had lost. He emptied the camps.
Then — and this is the part the Alliance did not expect — he took his people west, across the sea, away from the war entirely.
The Plague — Years 23–25
Something started killing people in northern Lordaeron. The dead got back up.
Prince Arthas of Lordaeron, the crown prince and the Silver Hand’s finest paladin, went north to stop it. What happened to him up there is argued about. What is not argued about is what he did when he came back: he killed his own father on the throne and handed the kingdom to the dead.
The northern kingdom is gone. Not conquered — emptied. Its survivors are refugees and its capital is a tomb.


                  
                  This is the wound 
                  
                

If you want to understand why anyone in this world behaves the way they do, it is usually this. Almost every adult human, dwarf, and high elf alive has lost someone to the plague or to what followed.


Hyjal — Year 25
The Burning Legion came back, properly, with the plague as its opening move.
Three peoples who had every reason to hate each other — orcs, humans, and night elves — met on the slopes of Mount Hyjal and fought together. Thrall’s Horde, Jaina Proudmoore’s human survivors, and Tyrande Whisperwind’s kaldorei.
They won. The night elves spent ten thousand years of immortality to do it, burning their World Tree to destroy the Legion’s commander.


                  
                  Nobody agrees about this either 
                  
                

On the road to Hyjal, the orc chieftain Grom Hellscream and his clan cut down a great swathe of Ashenvale and killed Cenarius, the demigod who taught the night elves everything they know.
The night elf memory: they murdered a god and desecrated a forest, and then asked us to fight beside them.
The orc memory: Grom broke the demon blood curse for our entire people and died doing it. He was the first orc to drink it and the last to be freed of it.
Both true. Four years later, the night elves are in the Alliance and the Warsong clan is still logging Ashenvale.



Part Four · Right Now
The Four Years After
Everyone went home and nobody agreed what came next. That is where the campaign starts.

The night elves joined the Alliance — recently, narrowly, and they are not sure about it.
The orcs have a homeland for the first time: Durotar, a red desert nobody else wanted, with Orgrimmar built out of raw timber four years ago.
The Tauren and the Darkspear trolls joined the Horde, having been saved from extinction by it.
The Forsaken joined too — undead who broke free of the Scourge and got their own minds back. Nobody is comfortable about this, including the Horde.
Stormwind stands, ruled by a ten-year-old king and a regent, and it is broke.
Ironforge is fine, is rich, and is quietly paying for most of the Alliance.
Dalaran is a crater and its surviving mages teach in back rooms.
Gnomeregan fell and the gnomes are refugees in Ironforge.

The Thing About Right Now
There is no war and there is no peace.
Thrall and Jaina Proudmoore are both genuinely trying to keep it that way. Almost nobody on either side believes the other side is trying. Meanwhile the Ashenvale logging, the Stonetalon mines, and the Hillsbrad Foothills border go on being fought over by people who are officially not at war.
And every one of the disasters above left something behind that is still out there — a plague that never fully burned out, a clan that never accepted the peace, an order that lost its way.


                  
                  The one thing to take from all this 
                  
                

Everyone in this world has just survived something. Nobody is at their best. The institutions are broken, the heroes have scattered, and the people who should be in charge are dead, missing, or ten years old.
That is the gap you walk into at level one.



If You Remember Five Things

The Dark Portal opened 29 years ago and started everything. Orcs are not from here.
The orcs were demon-controlled and are not any more. One of them died to break it.
Lordaeron was destroyed by its own prince, four years ago, and the survivors are everywhere.
Everyone fought together at Hyjal and won, and then immediately stopped speaking.
The night elves gave up immortality to make that work, and are still working out what that means.


Going Deeper
The detail behind all of this, if you want it:

Timeline of Azeroth — the full chronology, dated
The State of the World — where every region stands right now
Peoples MOC — each people’s own version of this history, in much more depth
The Alliance · The Horde — how the two sides actually work
Player Primer — Azeroth in Year 29 — the short version, if this was too much

Related
History MOC · Timeline of Azeroth · Player Primer — Azeroth in Year 29 · Canon Boundary — What Exists at Launch

Lore/History/The-First-War.title: The First War
Lore/History/The-First-War.content:
The First War



                  
                  Years 0–5 ADP 
                  
                

The orcish Horde came through the Dark Portal into the Swamp of Sorrows and destroyed the Kingdom of Stormwind.
What Happened

Medivh, possessed by Sargeras, opens the Dark Portal in collaboration with the warlock Gul’dan.
The orcs — already corrupted by Mannoroth’s blood and dying of it on Draenor — invade a world they were promised.
King Llane Wrynn is assassinated by Garona Halforcen under Gul’dan’s compulsion.
Stormwind Keep falls. Anduin Lothar leads the human refugees by sea north to Lordaeron.

Why It Still Matters
The orcs’ arrival was never their own idea — they were a weapon, aimed by a demon-possessed human wizard. This is the single most important fact in Alliance–Horde relations and almost nobody on the Alliance side believes it. Stormwind City was rebuilt after this war, and that reconstruction creates the Defias Brotherhood.
Related
Medivh · Gul’dan · Orcs · Dark Portal · Stormwind City · The Second War

Lore/History/The-Four-Years-After.title: The Four Years After
Lore/History/The-Four-Years-After.content:
The Four Years After


                  
                  Years 25–29 ADP 
                  
                

The reconstruction. New nations built on new continents by people who had lost their old ones — and a peace that is only holding because everyone is too tired to break it.
What Happened

Durotar is claimed. Thrall settles his people on barren red rock nobody else wanted, and raises Orgrimmar.
The Tauren unite. Cairne Bloodhoof drives the centaur from Mulgore with orcish help and founds Thunder Bluff. The tauren join the Horde out of debt and conviction.
The Darkspear Trolls settle in Durotar under Vol’jin, having lost the Echo Isles to the madman Zalazane.
Teldrassil is grown. Fandral Staghelm raises a second World Tree. Darnassus is built in its branches.
The night elves join the Alliance — a decision Tyrande makes largely alone, with Malfurion lost in The Emerald Dream.
The Battle of Theramore (Yr 26). Admiral Daelin Proudmoore arrives from Kul Tiras and attacks the Horde in defiance of his daughter. Jaina Proudmoore stands aside and lets the orcs kill him to preserve the peace. She has not been forgiven by anyone.
Gnomeregan falls. Troggs break into the lower levels and a radiation purge is authorised to drive them out. It fails to kill the troggs and kills most of the gnomes. Gelbin Mekkatorque leads the survivors into Ironforge.
Ragnaros is summoned. The Dark Iron Dwarves draw the Firelord into Molten Core beneath Blackrock Mountain.
The cold war calcifies. Ashenvale and Hillsbrad Foothills become permanent low-grade battlefronts.

Why It Still Matters
This is the present. Every institution the players interact with is four years old or four years broken. Nothing has settled. Nothing is traditional. Every alliance is provisional and every border is an argument.
Related
The State of the World · Timeline of Azeroth · Thrall · Jaina Proudmoore · Teldrassil · Gnomeregan · Ragnaros

Lore/History/The-Guardians-of-Tirisfal.title: The Guardians of Tirisfal
Lore/History/The-Guardians-of-Tirisfal.content:
The Guardians of Tirisfal


                  
                  ~2,600 BDP to Year 3 ADP 
                  
                

A secret order that invested the combined power of the world’s greatest mages into a single champion each generation, to fight the Burning Legion unseen. It ended in the worst possible way.
What Happened

The Council of Tirisfal is founded after the Troll Wars, drawing on human, elf, and dragon members.
Aegwynn is chosen Guardian and holds the office for nearly 900 years, defying the Council’s authority.
She destroys an avatar of Sargeras in Northrend — and entombs it, unaware that Sargeras allowed it, and that his spirit has hidden inside her.
Aegwynn conceives a son, Medivh, and passes the Guardian’s power to him at birth. Sargeras passes with it.
Medivh awakens possessed, contacts Gul’dan on Draenor, and opens the Dark Portal.
Medivh is slain at Karazhan by Anduin Lothar, Khadgar, and Garona Halforcen in Year 3.

Why It Still Matters
Every war of the last thirty years traces back to this order’s single point of failure. Karazhan stands abandoned and sealed in Deadwind Pass at launch — a tower full of a dead Guardian’s secrets that nobody has dared enter. Aegwynn is alive, in hiding, and elderly.
Related
Medivh · Aegwynn · Karazhan · The First War · Kirin Tor · Sargeras

Lore/History/The-Interbellum.title: The Interbellum
Lore/History/The-Interbellum.content:
The Interbellum


                  
                  Years 8–23 ADP 
                  
                

Fifteen years of exhausted, ugly peace. The Alliance won and did not know what to do next.
What Happened

Defeated orcs are herded into internment camps across Lordaeron, where they sink into a listless lethargy — the withdrawal of a people cut off from demonic blood.
Thrall is born in captivity and raised by Aedelas Blackmoore at Durnholde Keep as a gladiator and a tool.
The Alliance fractures. Gilneas walls itself off behind the Greymane Wall. Stromgarde and Kul Tiras drift. The high elves withdraw to Quel’Thalas.
Stormwind is rebuilt — and the Stonemasons’ Guild, who did the work, are never paid. Their leader Edwin VanCleef takes them underground as the Defias Brotherhood.
Year 20: Thrall escapes, finds the Frostwolf clan and Drek’Thar, and learns shamanism — the first orc in generations to touch the elements.
Year 21: Thrall frees the camps, liberates Grom Hellscream, and inherits the Doomhammer. The New Horde is born.

Why It Still Matters
This is where the campaign’s grudges are manufactured. The Defias, the Syndicate, Gilneas’s isolation, the high elves’ departure, and Thrall’s entire worldview all come out of these fifteen years. The Alliance’s biggest internal problems are self-inflicted debts from this period.
Related
Thrall · Defias Brotherhood · Edwin VanCleef · Orcs · Grom Hellscream · Hillsbrad Foothills

Lore/History/The-Invasion-of-Draenor.title: The Invasion of Draenor
Lore/History/The-Invasion-of-Draenor.content:
The Invasion of Draenor


                  
                  Years 17–18 ADP 
                  
                

The Alliance Expedition went back through a reopened Dark Portal to end the orcish threat at its source. Draenor did not survive.
What Happened

The shaman Ner’zhul reopens the Dark Portal to seek new worlds to conquer.
An Alliance Expedition under Turalyon and Khadgar pursues him through.
Ner’zhul opens multiple portals at once. The competing rifts tear Draenor apart.
Khadgar seals the portal from the Draenor side. The Expedition is stranded.
Ner’zhul flees into the Twisting Nether, where Kil’jaeden captures him, flays his spirit, and remakes him as The Lich King.

Why It Still Matters
Draenor’s shattered remnant becomes Outland — unreachable at launch. The Expedition (Turalyon, Alleria Windrunner, Danath Trollbane, Kurdran Wildhammer) is missing, presumed dead, which is a live mystery in 2004 and a fine plot hook. And the Lich King is created here — meaning the Second War produced the Third.
Related
Ner’zhul · The Lich King · Dark Portal · Khadgar · Blasted Lands · The Twisting Nether

Lore/History/The-Second-War.title: The Second War
Lore/History/The-Second-War.content:
The Second War



                  
                  Years 6–8 ADP 
                  
                

The Horde pushed north into Lordaeron. Seven human kingdoms, the dwarves, the gnomes, and the high elves formed the Alliance of Lordaeron and stopped them.
What Happened

Anduin Lothar unites the human kingdoms under King Terenas Menethil. Ironforge, Gnomeregan, and Quel’Thalas join.
The Horde, now led by Orgrim Doomhammer, enslaves the Red Dragonflight using the Demon Soul — Alexstrasza is chained in Grim Batol.
Lord Perenolde of Alterac betrays the Alliance, opening a pass to the Horde. Alterac is later dissolved in disgrace.
Quel’Thalas is burned. The high elves never forgive the Alliance’s slow response.
Uther the Lightbringer founds the Order of the Silver Hand — the first paladins.
Lothar dies at Blackrock Spire. Turalyon takes command and breaks the Horde.
Khadgar destroys the Dark Portal.

Why It Still Matters
Alterac’s treason creates the Syndicate. The enslaved dragons create the Dragonmaw and the mystery of Grim Batol. The high elves’ bitterness leads most of them to leave the Alliance. And the surviving orcs are put in internment camps — where Thrall is born.
Related
The Interbellum · Orgrim Doomhammer · Uther the Lightbringer · Alterac Mountains · Syndicate · Grim Batol · Alexstrasza

Lore/History/The-Sundering.title: The Sundering
Lore/History/The-Sundering.content:
The Sundering


                  
                  ~10,000 years before the Dark Portal 
                  
                

The Well of Eternity collapsed in on itself and took the continent with it. A single landmass became the world we know.
What Happened

The Well implodes. The resulting cataclysm shatters Kalimdor into the continents of today.
Eighty percent of the night elf population dies. The site of the Well becomes the Maelstrom.
Queen Azshara and her drowned court are transformed by an Old God’s bargain into the Naga.
Illidan Stormrage secretly poured stolen Well-water onto Mount Hyjal, creating a second Well. Malfurion imprisons him beneath Hyjal for ten thousand years.
The Dragon Aspects grow Nordrassil, the first World Tree, over the new Well — granting the night elves immortality and a duty to guard it.

Why It Still Matters
The geography of the entire campaign is Sundering debris. So is night elf immortality — which was spent at Mount Hyjal four years ago, meaning every night elf PC is experiencing mortality for the first time in ten millennia. That is not a footnote. That is a personality.
Related
The War of the Ancients · Nordrassil · Naga · Illidan Stormrage · Night Elves · Queen Azshara

Lore/History/The-Third-War.title: The Third War
Lore/History/The-Third-War.content:
The Third War



                  
                  Years 23–25 ADP 
                  
                

The Scourge destroyed Lordaeron and Quel’Thalas from the inside, the Burning Legion returned, and the world was saved by an alliance nobody wanted, on a mountain nobody could defend.
What Happened

A plague spreads through northern Lordaeron, turning the dead into Scourge. Prince Arthas Menethil investigates with Jaina Proudmoore and Uther the Lightbringer.
Arthas culls Stratholme — slaughtering his own infected citizens before they can turn. Uther refuses. Arthas disbands the Order of the Silver Hand on the spot.
Arthas sails to Northrend, burns his own ships, and takes up the runeblade Frostmourne. It takes his soul.
Arthas returns and murders his father, King Terenas. Lordaeron falls.
Arthas cuts the Dead Scar through Quel’Thalas and defiles the Sunwell to raise Kel’Thuzad as a lich, who summons Archimonde.
Archimonde destroys Dalaran.
Medivh, returned as a prophet, warns the leaders to flee west. Only Jaina Proudmoore and Thrall listen.
In Kalimdor, Grom Hellscream drinks demon blood again to kill Mannoroth — and in dying, breaks the orcs’ blood curse forever.
The Battle of Mount Hyjal: humans, orcs, and night elves stand together. Nordrassil’s power is detonated to destroy Archimonde. The night elves lose their immortality.
Aftermath: Illidan Stormrage flees to Outland. Sylvanas Windrunner frees herself and founds the Forsaken. Kael’thas Sunstrider leads the Blood Elves away. Arthas merges with Ner’zhul to become the whole Lich King.

Why It Still Matters
Everything in the present tense is Third War wreckage. The Plaguelands, the Forsaken, Theramore, Durotar, Teldrassil, the broken Silver Hand, the Scarlet Crusade, the fragile Alliance–Horde non-aggression — all of it. Four years ago. Everyone alive remembers it.
Related
Arthas Menethil · The Lich King · Mount Hyjal · Scourge · Sylvanas Windrunner · Thrall · Jaina Proudmoore · The Four Years After

Lore/History/The-Troll-Wars.title: The Troll Wars
Lore/History/The-Troll-Wars.content:
The Troll Wars


                  
                  ~2,700 years before the Dark Portal 
                  
                

The Amani troll empire moved to exterminate the high elves of Quel’Thalas. The elves, badly outnumbered, went to the humans of Arathor for help.
What Happened

The exiled Highborne — now High Elves — had founded Quel’Thalas atop a troll holy site. The Amani took offense, correctly.
Arathor sends its armies. In exchange, the elves teach one hundred humans the arcane arts.
Combined human steel and elven magic breaks the Amani at the gates of Quel’Thalas.

Why It Still Matters
This is the founding alliance of human and elf, and the origin of human magic — which leads directly to Dalaran, the Kirin Tor, the Guardians of Tirisfal, and Medivh opening the Dark Portal. It also leaves the Amani with a grudge that is still burning at launch in the Hinterlands and Eastern Plaguelands.
Related
High Elves · Humans · Trolls · Quel’Thalas · Kirin Tor

Lore/History/The-War-of-the-Ancients.title: The War of the Ancients
Lore/History/The-War-of-the-Ancients.content:
The War of the Ancients


                  
                  ~10,000 years before the Dark Portal 
                  
                

Queen Azshara and her Highborne, drunk on the Well of Eternity, opened a portal for Sargeras. The Burning Legion poured into a world that had never seen war.
What Happened

The Highborne’s reckless spellcraft draws Sargeras’s attention across the Twisting Nether.
Azshara agrees to unmake the world in exchange for godhood. Her court begins widening the portal.
Malfurion Stormrage, taught by Cenarius, leads a resistance of night elves, Dragons, Furbolg, and earthen.
Illidan Stormrage — jealous of his brother, in love with Tyrande Whisperwind — betrays the resistance to Sargeras, and is scarred and given his demonic sight.
Neltharion forges the Demon Soul, drains the other four flights, and turns on everyone. He becomes Deathwing.
The resistance destroys the Well of Eternity to close the portal.

Why It Still Matters
Everything after is aftershock. The Sundering, the Naga, the exile of the Highborne, the founding of Quel’Thalas, the broken Dragon Aspects, Deathwing’s existence, and the night elves’ ten-thousand-year isolation all begin here. It is also the Legion’s first failure — and they do not forget.
Related
The Sundering · Queen Azshara · Illidan Stormrage · Malfurion Stormrage · Deathwing · Night Elves · Arcane Magic and the Well of Eternity

Lore/History/The-War-of-the-Shifting-San.filePath: Lore/History/The War of the Shifting Sands.md
Lore/History/The-War-of-the-Shifting-San.title: The War of the Shifting Sands
Lore/History/The-War-of-the-Shifting-San.content:
The War of the Shifting Sands


                  
                  ~1,000 years before the Dark Portal 
                  
                

The qiraji erupted from Ahn’Qiraj and nearly took Kalimdor. It ended not in victory but in a wall.
What Happened

The insectoid qiraji, servants of the Old God C’Thun, pour out of the buried city of Ahn’Qiraj into Silithus and beyond.
The Night Elves under Fandral Staghelm fight them to a standstill at terrible cost. Staghelm’s son Valstann is killed in front of him.
The Bronze Dragonflight under Anachronos intervenes. Dragons die.
Unable to destroy the enemy, the dragons and night elves raise the Scarab Wall and seal the gates of Ahn’Qiraj. Anachronos leaves the Scepter of the Shifting Sands as the only key — then shatters it.

Why It Still Matters
The war was never won. It was paused. At launch the wall still stands, the qiraji are still inside, and the Twilight’s Hammer are excavating in Silithus trying to help them out. Fandral Staghelm’s grief over Valstann is the crack in the Cenarion Circle’s leadership.
Related
Ahn’Qiraj · C’Thun · Silithus · Fandral Staghelm · Bronze Dragonflight · Twilight’s Hammer

Lore/History/Timeline-of-Azeroth.title: Timeline of Azeroth
Lore/History/Timeline-of-Azeroth.content:
Timeline of Azeroth


                  
                  Dating convention 
                  
                

Years are counted from the opening of the Dark Portal — the standard Warcraft reckoning. ADP = After the Dark Portal, BDP = Before.



The Ancient Age

























WhenEventBefore timeThe Old Gods rule a chaotic Azeroth through the Elemental Lords—The Titans arrive, defeat the Old Gods, imprison them, and order the world—The titan-forged are made: Earthen, giants, mechagnomes, vrykul—The five Dragon Aspects are empowered; the Titans depart
The Kaldorei Empire

































WhenEvent~15,000 BDPNight elves settle around the Well of Eternity; the Kaldorei empire rises~10,000 BDPQueen Azshara and the Highborne contact Sargeras~10,000 BDPThe War of the Ancients — the Legion invades~10,000 BDPThe Sundering — Kalimdor shatters. Azshara’s court becomes the Naga. Illidan Stormrage creates a second Well and is imprisoned. Nordrassil is grown.~7,300 BDPThe Highborne are exiled for practicing arcane magic~6,800 BDPThe exiles found Quel’Thalas and create the Sunwell
The Age of Empires





































WhenEvent~2,800 BDPHumans found the empire of Arathor~2,700 BDPThe Troll Wars — Arathor and the high elves defeat the Amani. The elves teach a hundred humans magic in payment.~2,600 BDPThe Guardians of Tirisfal are founded to secretly police the Legion~1,200 BDPArathor fragments into seven human kingdoms~1,000 BDPThe War of the Shifting Sands — the qiraji erupt from Ahn’Qiraj. Fandral Staghelm and the Bronze Dragonflight seal the Scarab Wall. Staghelm’s son Valstann dies.~45 BDPAegwynn defeats an avatar of Sargeras in Northrend — and is unknowingly infected by him~25 BDPMedivh is born, already carrying Sargeras’s spirit
The Wars of the Portal





















































YearEvent0Medivh, possessed, opens the Dark Portal. The First War begins.3Medivh is slain at Karazhan by Lothar, Khadgar, and Garona5Stormwind falls. Refugees flee north to Lordaeron.6The Alliance of Lordaeron is formed. The Second War begins.6Quel’Thalas is burned by the Horde and the traitor Alterac8The Horde is broken at Blackrock Spire. The Dark Portal is destroyed.8–17The Interbellum — orcs interned in camps, sinking into lethargy. Alterac is dissolved for treason.~10Thrall is born; raised in captivity by Aedelas Blackmoore at Durnholde17–18The Invasion of Draenor — Ner’zhul tears Draenor apart. It becomes Outland.20Thrall escapes Durnholde, finds the Frostwolf clan, learns shamanism from Drek’Thar21Thrall frees Grom Hellscream and Orgrim Doomhammer; the New Horde is founded
The Third War

























































YearEvent23The Plague of Undeath appears in Lordaeron. Arthas Menethil investigates.24Arthas culls Stratholme, sails to Northrend, and takes up Frostmourne24Arthas murders King Terenas. Lordaeron falls to the Scourge.24Quel’Thalas is destroyed; the Sunwell is defiled to raise Kel’Thuzad24Archimonde destroys Dalaran24Jaina Proudmoore, warned by Medivh, leads the exodus to Kalimdor24Grom Hellscream slays Mannoroth at Demon Fall Canyon — the orcs are freed of the blood curse25The Battle of Mount Hyjal — Nordrassil is sacrificed to destroy Archimonde. The night elves lose their immortality.25Illidan Stormrage is released, consumes the Skull of Gul’dan, flees to Outland25Sylvanas Windrunner breaks free of the Lich King’s control and founds the Forsaken25Kael’thas Sunstrider leads the Blood Elves through the Dark Portal25Arthas returns to Northrend and merges with Ner’zhul — The Lich King is whole
The Four Years After

































YearEvent25–29Orgrimmar is built in Durotar. Thunder Bluff is founded in Mulgore.25–29Fandral Staghelm grows Teldrassil. Darnassus is built.26The Battle of Theramore — Admiral Daelin Proudmoore attacks the Horde and dies. His daughter Jaina Proudmoore lets it happen.26–29The night elves join the Alliance. Gnomeregan falls.29The Dark Iron summon Ragnaros into Molten Core29⟶ THE CAMPAIGN BEGINS

Lore/Peoples/Blood-Elves.title: Blood Elves
Lore/Peoples/Blood-Elves.content:
Blood Elves



                  
                  In a sentence 
                  
                

The high elves who chose survival over dignity, took a new name, and left. They are not here.


After the fall of Quel’Thalas, Kael’thas Sunstrider renamed his people sin’dorei — children of blood — in memory of the dead, and led them in search of a cure for their arcane withdrawal. They went through the Dark Portal into Outland, where they have fallen in with Illidan Stormrage.

Lore/Peoples/Centaur.title: Centaur
Lore/Peoples/Centaur.content:
Centaur



                  
                  In a sentence 
                  
                

Born of a demigod’s terrible mistake, and at war with everyone including themselves.


The centaur are the offspring of Zaetar, son of Cenarius, and Princess Theradras, an earth elemental princess and daughter of Therazane. Their birth killed their father. Cenarius disowned them.
They spread across Desolace, Thousand Needles, and the Barrens, and hunted the Tauren to the brink until Thrall’s orcs intervened.
The Clans
Five khanates, perpetually at war with each other. At launch the two accessible ones are:

Gelkis Clan (Desolace) — will deal with outsiders who kill Magram
Magram Clan (Desolace) — will deal with outsiders who kill Gelkis

Also present: the Kolkar (Barrens, Desolace), the Galak (Thousand Needles), the Maraudine (Maraudon).
Theradras herself lies at the heart of Maraudon, mourning Zaetar and corrupting the earth around her.
Related

Lore/Peoples/Dark-Iron-Dwarves.title: Dark Iron Dwarves
Lore/Peoples/Dark-Iron-Dwarves.content:
Dark Iron Dwarves



                  
                  In a sentence 
                  
                

The clan that lost the civil war, summoned a fire god out of spite, and has been his property ever since.


One of the three dwarven clans of the War of the Three Hammers. Defeated and exiled, the Dark Iron under the sorcerer-thane Thaurissan retreated to Blackrock Mountain and summoned Ragnaros the Firelord to win their war for them.
Ragnaros came. He obliterated their city, raised Blackrock Mountain in the process, and enslaved them all.
They consider this a reasonable trade.
At Launch

Emperor Dagran Thaurissan rules the Dark Iron from the Imperial Seat in Blackrock Depths
He has abducted and married Princess Moira Bronzebeard, Magni Bronzebeard’s only daughter
The Shadowforge city sprawls beneath the mountain; Molten Core lies below it
They are actively working to widen the summoning that binds Ragnaros
Dark Iron agents operate in Searing Gorge, Burning Steppes, Wetlands (Dun Modr), and Redridge Mountains

Lore/Peoples/Darkspear-Trolls.title: Darkspear Trolls
Lore/Peoples/Darkspear-Trolls.content:
Darkspear Trolls



                  
                  In a sentence 
                  
                

A small, displaced tribe who owe the Horde everything, and who are the only trolls on Azeroth that anybody trusts.


Playable: Yes · Faction: Horde · Homeland: Durotar / the Echo Isles · Capital: (guests in Orgrimmar) · Leader: Vol’jin
Where They Stand
The Darkspear were a dwindling jungle tribe on the Broken Isles, being eaten alive by Murlocs and a sea witch (Zar’jira), when Thrall’s fleet ran aground nearby. The orcs saved them; the trolls’ witch doctor Sen’jin died in the fighting. His son Vol’jin brought the survivors into the Horde and has led them since.
They were given the Echo Isles off Durotar — and then lost them to Zalazane, a Darkspear witch doctor who went mad, seized the islands, and enslaved his own tribesmen with voodoo. The Darkspear now live in Sen’jin Village on the Durotar coast and as guests in Orgrimmar’s Valley of Spirits.
How They Got Here
Trolls ruled everything, once. The Gurubashi and Amani empires covered both continents, and every city standing today is built on troll ruins. The Troll Wars broke the Amani; internal collapse broke the Gurubashi. Every troll alive knows this and is furious about it.
The Darkspear were exiles even then. Driven out of Stranglethorn Vale by the Gurubashi, they fled to the Broken Isles and dwindled there for generations — a tribe of a few hundred, losing ground to murlocs and to a naga sea witch.
Then the orcs ran aground. Thrall’s fleet, crossing to Kalimdor, was wrecked near the isles. The Darkspear helped them and the orcs helped back. Sen’jin, the tribe’s witch doctor and chieftain, was captured and killed — but not before telling Thrall where to find his people.
Vol’jin brought them into the Horde. A tribe of a few hundred joined a nation of thousands, and did it as full members rather than as clients. Thrall gave them the Echo Isles.
Then Zalazane took the isles. One of their own witch doctors, driven mad, turned voodoo on his own tribe and enslaved the ones who could not flee. The Darkspear have been homeless again for less than four years.
Who Leads Them
Vol’jin, chieftain and shadow hunter — young for the role, sharply intelligent, and the most politically astute person in Orgrimmar. He is Thrall’s closest confidant and the one adviser who will tell him a plan is stupid.
Beneath him:

The witch doctors and shadow hunters, who hold spiritual authority and are consulted on everything
The elders, few in number, who remember Stranglethorn Vale

The tribe is small enough that everyone knows everyone. There is no bureaucracy. Decisions get made around a fire in an evening.
Where They Fit
The Darkspear are the Horde’s smallest member and its sharpest. They contribute headhunters, scouts, witch doctors, and — crucially — Vol’jin, who functions as Thrall’s political conscience the way Cairne functions as his moral one.
They are also guests, formally, in a city that is not theirs, and they feel it. The Valley of Spirits is a good district and it is still not home.
Other trolls consider them traitors. The Darkspear made a choice no other troll tribe has made — to join outsiders rather than fight them — and the Amani, Gurubashi, and Sandfury regard them as having sold the troll birthright for a berth in an orc city.
Voodoo
Darkspear spirituality is loa-worship and shadow magic — spirits bargained with rather than gods worshipped. It sits uneasily beside orcish shamanism and tauren ancestor-faith, and Thrall has decided not to ask too many questions.
The loa are not benevolent and are not expected to be. You bring an offering, you make a case, and you accept the terms. Zalazane is what happens when someone stops accepting the terms.
The Thing They Gave Up
Troll cultures across Azeroth practised ritual cannibalism — eating a defeated enemy to take their strength. The Gurubashi and Amani still do. The Darkspear did too, once.
They gave it up. Thrall forbade it as a condition of joining the Horde, and Vol’jin agreed on behalf of the tribe. That was not a small concession: it meant abandoning a practice tied up with victory, mourning, and what it meant to be a troll at all.


                  
                  It is a taboo now, and the tribe enforces it 
                  
                

This is not something Darkspear do quietly and everyone politely ignores. It is banned, it is shameful, and a Darkspear caught at it is in serious trouble with their own people first.
A handful of individuals are rumoured to have kept the habit in secret. That is a scandal, not a custom — closer to a disgraced elder than to a cultural quirk, and other Darkspear are angrier about it than any orc would be.


Other trolls regard the renunciation as one more proof that the Darkspear sold their birthright. The Darkspear regard it as the price of having a future.


                  
                  At the table 
                  
                

Play it as something your character does not do and finds shameful, not as a dark joke about troll appetites. If it comes up at all, it should come up as an accusation from a hostile troll tribe — which is exactly how a Darkspear would most often encounter it.


What They Just Survived

Near-extinction on the Broken Isles, within the last five years
Sen’jin’s death, which is recent enough that his son still leads by it
Losing the Echo Isles to one of their own

What They Are Fighting Now






























WhereWhoWhyThe Echo IslesZalazaneTheir home, held by a madman, with their own people enslaved inside itDurotar coastMurlocs, nagaConstant, and the reason Sen’jin Village keeps a watchStranglethorn ValeGurubashiThe old grudge. The Darkspear were exiled from there and have not forgotten.Within the HordeNobody, openlyBeing the smallest member of a coalition is its own slow fight
What They Want
Go home. Retake the Echo Isles, free the enthralled, and stop being guests. This is unanimous and it is urgent.
Vol’jin wants the Horde to survive Thrall. He can see that the coalition is held together by one man’s personal authority, and he thinks about what happens after more than anyone else does.
The elders want the tribe to grow. A few hundred people is not a nation, and the Darkspear are one bad season from being a footnote.
Character Traits

Regenerative — trolls heal from wounds that would kill anyone else. Severed limbs regrow, slowly.
Wry and fatalistic — the Darkspear have a sense of humour about their circumstances
Cannibalism is renounced, not practised — an old troll custom the tribe formally gave up to join the Horde. See below.
Loyal absolutely to Vol’jin and Thrall — this is a tribe that knows what it owes

How They Talk
Warm, teasing, and fatalistic. The Darkspear joke constantly, including about death, and outsiders often mistake this for not taking things seriously.





































PhraseWhen”Stay away from da voodoo.”Half warning, half joke. Said to outsiders who ask too many questions.”Da loa be watchin’.”A blessing and a caution at once. Nobody says it entirely comfortably.”Mon.”Universal address — friend, stranger, superior. Not casual disrespect.”Dis ain’t gonna work.”Said before doing it anyway”We been worse.”The tribe’s whole outlook in three words”Ya got somethin’ worth tradin’?”Opening a negotiation. The Darkspear will trade for almost anything.”Sen’jin would’a laughed.”Highest praise for a plan. Also said at funerals.


                  
                  On the accent, at the table 
                  
                

Troll speech has a distinct rhythm — dropped consonants, da for the, ya for you. You do not have to perform it, and a player who would rather speak plainly is not doing it wrong.
If you do use it, keep it warm rather than comic. The Darkspear are the wittiest people in the Horde, not the funniest-sounding.


What They Make of the Others


                  
                  Not symmetrical, on purpose 
                  
                

How a people sees its neighbours rarely matches how those neighbours see them. The gaps are where the roleplay is.


Humans — The old enemy, and the insult is that they have forgotten why. Two centuries of war with Arathor is a footnote in their histories and a scar in ours.
Dwarves — They fight Frostmane in the mountains and Witherbark in the hills and they do not ask which tribe you are. Being hated by association is an old feeling.
Night Elves — They came from us. Every troll knows it, no kaldorei will say it, and watching one change the subject is a small pleasure the Darkspear allow themselves.
Gnomes — They want to see a limb grow back. They are not subtle about wanting to see it. They are not going to see it.
Orcs — They pulled a dying tribe off a rock and gave us a coast. Sen’jin died in that fight. Everything since is detail.
Forsaken — Dead things that argue. The loa have opinions about that which the witch doctors decline to translate.
Tauren — The only people in the Horde who never once made us feel like guests. That is not a small thing when you are living in somebody else’s city.
Playing One
A Darkspear PC has the tightest, most personal starting motivation in the Horde: go home. Zalazane holds the Echo Isles and some of their family are still there, enthralled.
Four shapes worth taking:

Headhunter or scout — you move through jungle the way other people move through a corridor, and the Horde has noticed
Witch doctor’s student — you are learning to bargain with things that do not have your interests at heart. Zalazane learned the same way.
Enslaved and escaped — you were on the Echo Isles when Zalazane took them, and you got out. Others did not, and you know their names.
Born in Orgrimmar — the Valley of Spirits is the only home you have known, and the elders’ grief for an island you cannot remember is slightly abstract to you

Questions worth answering at session zero: Who did you leave on the Isles? What have you promised a loa, and have you paid it? Do you owe Thrall personally, or just in principle?
Related
Vol’jin · Durotar · Orgrimmar · Trolls · Thrall · Stranglethorn Vale · The Troll Wars · A Short History of Azeroth

Lore/Peoples/Dwarves.title: Dwarves
Lore/Peoples/Dwarves.content:
Dwarves



                  
                  In a sentence 
                  
                

Miners, drinkers, and unexpectedly the species with the most disturbing origin story on the continent.


Playable: Yes · Faction: Alliance · Homeland: Dun Morogh · Capital: Ironforge · Leader: King Magni Bronzebeard
Where They Stand
Ironforge is the Alliance’s most functional institution — a mountain-city under Dun Morogh that has fed, armed, and sheltered every ally who asked. It currently shelters the entire gnomish nation in Tinker Town, and does not complain about it.
The Three Hammers
Dwarven unity ended in a civil war three centuries ago. Three clans, three claims:

























ClanWhereStatusBronzebeardIronforgeWon. Rule the mountain.Wildhammer ClanAerie Peak, The HinterlandsExiled north. Gryphon-riders. Alliance-friendly but not Alliance-subject.Dark Iron DwarvesBlackrock MountainExiled, summoned Ragnaros, now enslaved to him. Enemies.
The war began over the succession when the old king died leaving three sons. It ended with two clans driven out and a grudge that has now outlived everyone who started it. Nobody living remembers the actual argument. Everybody remembers the outcome.
How They Got Here
They woke up in Uldaman. Or that is the oldest story — that the dwarves came out of the deep places and built Ironforge, and that there were mechanisms down there they did not build.
They kept to the mountain for most of recorded history, trading iron and steel and staying out of human wars.
The Three Hammers broke them three centuries ago and scattered two thirds of the people.
The Second War brought them out. Dwarven steel armed the Alliance, dwarven gryphon-riders — Wildhammers, notably, not Bronzebeards — fought in the sky, and Ironforge discovered it liked being useful.
Then archaeology became a national obsession. The Explorers’ League formed to answer one question: where did we come from? They have been digging ever since, and the answers coming out of Uldaman are not what anybody expected.
Who Leads Them
King Magni Bronzebeard — a working king. He is in the forge most days, he knows his smiths by name, and he is the most personally liked head of state in the Alliance.
Under him sits a council of thanes and guildmasters, and it has real teeth. A dwarven king who ignores his guilds finds the work slows down.
Two institutions matter as much as the crown:

The Explorers’ League — funds expeditions worldwide, answers to nobody in practice, and is currently the most influential body in Ironforge
The Senate — the clan assembly, slow and procedural and where the Wildhammer question keeps failing to get resolved

Clan comes before crown. A Wildhammer’s first duty is to Aerie Peak, and Magni knows better than to test it.
Where They Fit
They pay for things. Ironforge’s mines and forges make it the only Alliance member with a functioning treasury, and a great deal of what looks like Alliance solidarity is actually dwarven money quietly covering a shortfall in Stormwind.
They also house the gnomes, arm the humans, and are the only Alliance people the night elves find genuinely easy to deal with — dwarves want to dig things up and kaldorei want things left buried, but at least the argument is honest.
What They Just Survived

The Third War — Ironforge sent troops north and got fewer back
The fall of Gnomeregan, next door, which put an entire refugee nation inside their mountain overnight
Three centuries of the Three Hammers, which is still the defining fact of dwarven politics

What They Are Fighting Now



































WhereWhoWhyBlackrock MountainDark Iron DwarvesKin-war, three centuries old, now with an elemental lord behind itSearing Gorge, Burning SteppesDark Iron, Blackrock orcsThe southern frontier, and it is losing groundDun MoroghFrostmane trolls, troggsLocal, constant, and the troggs came out of GnomereganUldaman, BadlandsWhatever is in the vaultsNot a war. Not exactly safe either.The HinterlandsWitherbark trollsWildhammer business, which Ironforge is careful not to call its own
What They Want
Magni wants his people whole. Reconciliation with the Wildhammers is achievable and he is working on it quietly. The Dark Iron are past that, and he has stopped pretending otherwise.
The Explorers’ League wants the truth about where dwarves came from, and is going to get it whether or not anyone is ready.
Ordinary dwarves want the work to go well and the ale to hold out — and, increasingly, want somebody to explain what the League keeps finding.
Character Traits

Archaeological obsession — the Explorers’ League digs everywhere, invited or not
Clan loyalty over national loyalty — a Wildhammer’s first duty is to Aerie Peak
Hard-drinking, hard-working, genuinely warm — dwarves like people
Devout — dwarven paladins are pragmatic rather than pious

How They Talk
Blunt, warm, and full of stone and craft metaphors. Dwarves swear casually and apologise rarely.





































PhraseWhen”By me beard.”Surprise. Also “beard and hammer” for something serious.”Stone remembers.”Said of grudges, oaths, and history. The nearest thing dwarves have to scripture.”To the deep.”A toast. Answered with “and back up again” — because not everyone does.”Ye’ll no’ dig it up wi’ yer hands.”Do the job properly, or bring the right tools”Mind yer head.”Practical caution, and a running joke about how everyone else is built wrong”That’s a Bronzebeard answer.”A ruling you dislike but will accept”Khaz Modan endures.”The formal one. Said at funerals and when signing things.
What They Make of the Others


                  
                  Not symmetrical, on purpose 
                  
                

How a people sees its neighbours rarely matches how those neighbours see them. The gaps are where the roleplay is.


Humans — Reliable, decent, and permanently in a hurry. Dwarves are fond of them the way you are fond of a nephew who keeps almost getting it right. The habit of promising money that has not been raised yet is noted, repeatedly.
Gnomes — Guests who have been here four years and are not being asked to leave. Ironforge gave them a district without a debate, and would give them another. The noise is a small price.
Night Elves — Infuriating. They have watched ten thousand years of history and will not discuss any of it, and they treat a dig site like a desecration. Dwarves want to know where everyone came from; the kaldorei appear to already know and to have decided it is none of your business.
Orcs — An honest enemy, which counts for something. Dwarves fought them in the last war without losing a homeland to it, so the grudge is cooler than Stormwind’s — professional rather than personal.
Forsaken — Wrong in a way dwarves take literally. Stone endures, flesh does not, and dead things stay down. A Forsaken is a category error walking about.
Tauren — Would get on famously and have barely had the chance. Patient, craft-minded, unhurried people who honour their ancestors — that is a dwarf’s description of a dwarf. The faction line is a genuine shame.
Darkspear Trolls — The Frostmane are at the gates of Dun Morogh and the Witherbark hold the Hinterlands, and nobody in Ironforge asks which tribe. That is unfair to the Darkspear and it is not going to change soon.
Playing One
Dwarf PCs get built-in purpose: the Explorers’ League will fund an expedition anywhere, which solves the “why is this character travelling” problem in one sentence.
Four shapes worth taking:

Bronzebeard regular — Ironforge-born, mountain-proud, and quietly bothered by what the League keeps hauling home
Wildhammer — gryphon country, shaman-friendly, and only conditionally Alliance. Your loyalty runs to Aerie Peak first and you will say so.
Explorers’ League field hand — you carry the shovels and the crossbow, and you have seen three things you have not reported
Dark Iron defector — hard, and needs real justification. You left Blackrock Mountain and nobody on either side trusts you. Excellent if the player wants a hill to climb.

Questions worth answering at session zero: Which clan, and what does your family think of the other two? What have you dug up that you did not hand in? Do you drink, and is it a problem?
Related
Ironforge · Magni Bronzebeard · Uldaman · Dark Iron Dwarves · Wildhammer Clan · Explorers’ League · A Short History of Azeroth

Lore/Peoples/Forsaken.title: Forsaken
Lore/Peoples/Forsaken.content:
Forsaken



                  
                  In a sentence 
                  
                

Undead who broke the The Lich King’s hold and got their minds back — and have discovered that having your mind back is not the same as having your life back.


Playable: Yes · Faction: Horde · Homeland: Tirisfal Glades · Capital: Undercity · Leader: Banshee Queen Sylvanas Windrunner
Where They Stand
When Arthas’s power over the Scourge weakened after The Third War, Sylvanas Windrunner — the ranger-general he had murdered and raised as a banshee — seized her own free will and took a large portion of the undead with her.
They call themselves the Forsaken: not Scourge, not alive, not anyone’s.
They hold Tirisfal Glades and built Undercity in the catacombs beneath the ruins of Lordaeron’s Capital City — directly under the throne room where Arthas killed his father.
How They Got Here
They were alive. Almost every Forsaken was a citizen of Lordaeron — farmers, soldiers, clergy, apothecaries. A handful were high elves of Quel’Thalas. Sylvanas was its ranger-general.
The plague took them. Grain, distributed through the northern villages, that killed you and then stood you back up. Most Forsaken died in their own homes, in their own beds, surrounded by their own families, and then got up and killed them.
They served. For a period nobody likes to specify, they were Scourge — aware, in some cases, and unable to stop. This is the part no Forsaken discusses.
Then the grip loosened. After The Third War, as Arthas’s power waned, Sylvanas broke free and pulled thousands with her.
Then they had to decide what they were. They took the name Forsaken, took the ruins of their own kingdom, and went looking for allies — because a nation of walking corpses surrounded by enemies does not survive alone. Thrall took them in over the tauren’s objection, and they have been the Horde’s most awkward member ever since.
Who Leads Them
Banshee Queen Sylvanas Windrunner — absolute, unelected, and unchallenged. There is no council, no assembly, and no succession plan. What Sylvanas decides is what happens.
Under her:

The Deathstalkers — intelligence and assassination, and the largest single branch of the Forsaken state
The Dark Rangers — elven women raised as she was, personally loyal to her rather than to the Forsaken
The apothecaries — chemists and alchemists, a visible and respectable branch of the Forsaken state.

Where They Fit
Badly, and everyone knows it.

Hated by the Alliance, who see them as Scourge with better manners and are not entirely wrong
Tolerated by the Horde — Thrall accepted them out of pragmatism. Cairne Bloodhoof objected and was overruled. The tauren still object.
At war with the Scourge, permanently and existentially
At war with the Scarlet Crusade, who consider them the enemy — which is also not entirely wrong

The Horde is a flag of convenience. The Forsaken joined for military cover and access, contribute intelligence and alchemy, and would leave the moment the arithmetic changed. Both parties understand this.
What They Are
The Forsaken do not eat, sleep, breathe, or age. They rot slowly and can be repaired. Their bodies are wrong and they know it. Some remember their living families and cannot approach them. Some are trying very hard to remain the person they were. Some have stopped trying.
The Light burns them. Not metaphorically — healing magic that mends a living body damages an undead one, and the faith most of them were raised in is now physically hostile. Forsaken who still pray do it knowing that.
What They Just Survived

Dying, and the specifics of it, which most of them remember
Being Scourge, which is worse
The war for Tirisfal Glades against both the Scourge and the Scarlet Crusade

What They Are Fighting Now






























WhereWhoWhyWestern Plaguelands, Eastern PlaguelandsScourgeExistential. Losing means going back, and going back is the only real fear they have.Tirisfal GladesScarlet CrusadeFanatics who kill undead on sight and increasingly kill the living tooSilverpine Forest, Hillsbrad FoothillsAlliance, worgen, Dalaran remnantsA slow southward push toward Southshore that nobody has formally declaredEverywhereTheir own reputationEvery Forsaken diplomat starts the conversation twenty points down
What They Want
Sylvanas wants Arthas dead. Everything else is instrumental to that, including the Horde, including the Apothecaries, including the Forsaken themselves. She has never pretended otherwise.
The Forsaken want to be permanent. They do not reproduce. Every Forsaken is a survivor of a specific catastrophe, and when they are gone there will be no more. A nation with no future tense makes decisions differently.
Individuals want smaller things — to see a daughter from a distance, to finish a piece of work, to find out who they were before the plague took the memory. These are the ones worth playing.
Character Traits

Grim, dry, unsentimental humour — it is the only functional coping mechanism
Free will is sacred — nothing terrifies a Forsaken like the idea of being controlled again
Pragmatic to the point of atrocity — they have nothing left to lose and it shows
Not evil, and not good — the Forsaken are the campaign’s best moral grey zone

How They Talk
Dry, clipped, and darkly funny. Forsaken humour is a load-bearing structure. They keep Lordaeron’s courtesies and use them sardonically, because the alternative is having no manners at all.





































PhraseWhen”The Dark Lady watches over you.”The standard blessing. Deliberately parallels Light be with you, and the parallel is the point.”Still standing.”A greeting and its own answer. How are you? — Still standing.”Death be with you.”Said to Alliance prisoners. Not a threat exactly.”I was somebody.”Bitter, common, and said in taverns. Sometimes followed by a name and sometimes not.”Rot in peace.”A genuine farewell to the destroyed. There is no Forsaken word for a good death.”Before.”Life. “Before, I was a baker.” Never says when I was alive.”Ask the Apothecaries.”Do not ask me. Nobody says this cheerfully.
What They Make of the Others


                  
                  Not symmetrical, on purpose 
                  
                

How a people sees its neighbours rarely matches how those neighbours see them. The gaps are where the roleplay is.


Humans — We were them. That is not sentiment, it is a fact of biography, and it is precisely why they cannot look at us. A Forsaken watching a Southshore farmer is watching a life that was on offer.
Dwarves — They would put us down on principle and sleep soundly. There is a cold respect in that — at least they are honest about it.
Night Elves — They find us an offence against the natural order and they are not wrong. The Forsaken have simply concluded that the natural order had its chance.
Gnomes — They look at us the way an engineer looks at a bridge that should have fallen. One of them will ask a question one day and get a very short answer.
Orcs — They took us in when there was nowhere else, and they did it knowing exactly what we are. That is not friendship. It is the only thing anyone has ever done for us.
Tauren — Cairne argued against us to Thrall’s face and lost, and he has never pretended otherwise since. The Forsaken respect him more than they respect most of their allies.
Darkspear Trolls — They do not stare. In four years of the Horde, that is the single kindest thing anyone has done.
Playing One
A Forsaken PC can play the horror straight, and the campaign is better if they do. This is the character who has to decide, on screen, whether the person they used to be is worth preserving.
Four shapes worth taking:

The one with a family — somebody in Southshore or Hillsbrad Foothills thinks you are dead and buried. You know exactly which house. You have stood outside it.
The one still holding on — you keep your old trade, your old manners, your old name. Other Forsaken find this either admirable or pathetic and will tell you which.
The one who let go — you have decided the person who died is a stranger, and you are free in a way the others are not. This is not villainy. It is a real answer.
The one with a gap — you do not remember who you were. Somebody does, and they are alive.

Questions worth answering at session zero: What did you do before? Do you remember dying? Is there anyone alive who would recognise your face — and do you want them to?


                  
                  The Light question 
                  
                

A Forsaken Priest is one of the strongest characters available: the faith you were raised in now physically hurts you, and you use it anyway. See Classes of Azeroth.


Related
Sylvanas Windrunner · Undercity · Tirisfal Glades · Scourge · Scarlet Crusade · The Third War · The Holy Light · A Short History of Azeroth

Lore/Peoples/Furbolg.title: Furbolg
Lore/Peoples/Furbolg.content:
Furbolg



                  
                  In a sentence 
                  
                

Peaceful ursine shamanists who were the night elves’ oldest allies — and most of whom have now gone violently insane.


Furbolg tribes have lived alongside the Night Elves since before The Sundering and fought beside them in The War of the Ancients.
Then The Third War happened, and demonic corruption spread through their tribes like a disease.

Lore/Peoples/Gnolls.title: Gnolls
Lore/Peoples/Gnolls.content:
Gnolls



                  
                  In a sentence 
                  
                

Hyena-men. Everywhere. Always stealing something.


Scavenging pack-hunters found across both continents, organized into clans of varying competence. They are the default low-level threat in Alliance territory and are more dangerous in numbers than any individual gnoll suggests.
Riverpaw (Elwynn Forest, Westfall) · Redridge (Redridge Mountains) · Mosshide (Wetlands) · Woodpaw (Feralas) · Shadowhide (Redridge Mountains) · Palemane (Mulgore) · Rot Hide (Silverpine Forest — plagued, working for the Scourge)


                  
                  The Rot Hide exception 
                  
                

Rot Hide gnolls in Silverpine have been deliberately infected with the plague of undeath by Scourge necromancers. They are the one gnoll group with a plot attached.


Related
Elwynn Forest · Westfall · Redridge Mountains · Silverpine Forest · Scourge

Lore/Peoples/Gnomes.title: Gnomes
Lore/Peoples/Gnomes.content:
Gnomes



                  
                  In a sentence 
                  
                

A nation of refugees who lost their entire country to a betrayal and an engineering decision, and who remain relentlessly, offensively cheerful about it.


Playable: Yes · Faction: Alliance · Homeland: Dun Morogh (Gnomeregan, lost) · Capital: (exiled to Ironforge) · Leader: High Tinker Gelbin Mekkatorque
Where They Stand
They have no home. Gnomeregan — the great subterranean techno-city beneath Dun Morogh — fell four years ago, and the story is worse than an invasion.
The survivors live in Tinker Town in Ironforge, guests of King Magni Bronzebeard, and are working on getting their city back.
How They Got Here
Nobody is entirely sure where gnomes came from, including gnomes, and they have historically been too busy to investigate. The Explorers’ League has opinions. Gnomish scholars find the question less interesting than the machinery.
They built Gnomeregan and spent centuries in it — a sealed, self-governing, aggressively inventive city-state that traded with Ironforge and largely ignored the surface.
The Second War brought them out. Gnomish siege engines, submarines, and demolition work went to the Alliance, and gnomes discovered they enjoyed being indispensable.
Then the troggs came up. Dwarven and gnomish digging had gone deep, and something came back through the tunnels.
Then the radiation. In a single decision, the gnomes lost their city, four fifths of their people, and their confidence — and gained a refugee nation, a permanent grudge, and a project.
Who Leads Them
High Tinker Gelbin Mekkatorque — elected, not born to it, and re-elected since the disaster by people who could reasonably have thrown him out. That vote is the most interesting fact about gnomish politics.
Around him sits an advisory council of senior tinkers, whose authority comes from what they have built rather than from any office. A gnome with a working prototype outranks a gnome with a title.
Gnomish governance is genuinely, unusually meritocratic and consultative — proposals, review, iteration. It is also slow, which is why the plan to retake Gnomeregan has been in review for four years.
Where They Fit
Gnomes are the Alliance’s engineers, and its guests. Every siege engine, every mechanical lift in Ironforge, every piece of clever infrastructure in Stormwind has gnomish fingerprints on it, and gnomes are cheerfully aware that this is the reason they are welcome.
They have no territory, no army worth the name, and no vote that anyone is obliged to count. What they have is usefulness, and they work at it — partly from gratitude, and partly because a people with no country cannot afford to be optional.
What They Just Survived

The fall of Gnomeregan — eighty percent dead, in one decision, four years ago
The irradiation, which is ongoing: leper gnomes are survivors, not enemies, and the distinction gets lost
Becoming refugees in a mountain that was never built for them

What They Are Fighting Now

























WhereWhoWhyGnomereganTroggs, leper gnomes, and the mad king in the middleTheir entire country, held by the thing that took itDun MoroghTroggs, Frostmane trollsSurface skirmishing around the sealed entranceEverywhereGoblin engineersNot a war. A rivalry, conducted through sabotage, patents, and open contempt.
What They Want
Retake Gnomeregan. That is the whole national project and everyone is signed up to it. What is disputed is how — decontaminate and reclaim, or seal it forever and build somewhere new. Mekkatorque wants it back. A quiet minority thinks the city is a grave and should be treated as one.
Deal with the leper gnomes, who are their own irradiated relatives and are treated, mostly, as a problem rather than as casualties. This is the gnomes’ moral blind spot and it is not being discussed.
Stop being guests. Politely, gratefully, and with increasing urgency.
Character Traits

Irrepressible — a gnome’s optimism is a survival adaptation and it is load-bearing
Precise — they measure things nobody asked them to measure
Engineering, always — even gnome mages and warlocks tinker
Quietly grieving — every adult gnome lost most of their family. They do not talk about it.

How They Talk
Fast, technical, and relentlessly upbeat in a way that is doing a lot of work. Gnomes reach for engineering vocabulary for everything, including feelings.





































PhraseWhen”Within tolerance.”It is fine. Also: I am fine. Used about injuries, grief, and structural failures alike.”That’s a rounding error.”Do not worry about it. Frequently said about things that are not, in fact, rounding errors.”Measure twice, detonate once.”Proverbial. Somebody says it before every plan.”It worked in the model.”Said at the wreckage, without embarrassment”Before the Fall.”The war is the Second War. The Fall is Gnomeregan, always, and needs no clarification.”Give it here.”A gnome taking your broken thing. You will get it back improved and slightly alarming.”Cog and spring!”Mild oath. Roughly good grief.


                  
                  The cheerfulness is the tell 
                  
                

A gnome describing the loss of their family in the same tone they use for a gearbox failure is not coping well. They are coping loudly, which is not the same thing. Playing that gap is where the character lives.


What They Make of the Others


                  
                  Not symmetrical, on purpose 
                  
                

How a people sees its neighbours rarely matches how those neighbours see them. The gaps are where the roleplay is.


Humans — Kind, generous, and imprecise to a degree that causes gnomes physical discomfort. A human will say a bridge is ‘about forty feet’ and mean it as helpful.
Dwarves — Landlords, hosts, friends, and the reason there are still gnomes. The debt is enormous and freely acknowledged, and Ironforge has never once mentioned it.
Night Elves — They disapprove and will not say of what. Gnomes have tried adjusting several variables and have made no progress, which is the most frustrating experimental result available.
Orcs — Never fought them, never lost anything to them, and are therefore the only Alliance people who can be straightforwardly curious about orcish metalwork.
Forsaken — Fascinating and appalling in the same breath. Every gnome has privately wondered what is actually keeping one upright, and every gnome knows better than to say so.
Tauren — Have not met one. Deeply want to. The engineering questions raised by a nine-foot bipedal frame are, to a gnome, an unopened present.
Darkspear Trolls — Regenerative tissue is the single most interesting biological problem on the continent, and gnomes are aware that asking a troll to hold still while you measure is a poor opening.
Playing One
Gnome PCs have an unimpeachable motivation: retake Gnomeregan. Mekkatorque will personally back an expedition, which means a patron, funding, and a reason to be anywhere.
Four shapes worth taking:

Survivor — you were in the city when the radiation came. You got out. You have opinions about who did not, and about the man who gave the order.
Born after — you have never seen Gnomeregan and are slightly tired of hearing about it. Your home is Ironforge and you would say so if it did not upset the elders.
Tinker on assignment — the council sent you out to gather something, and you are not entirely clear whether the assignment was real or a kindness
Rogue or sapper — locks, traps, and demolition, all learned in a city that no longer exists

Questions worth answering at session zero: Who did you lose, and do you say their name? What are you building right now? Is there a leper gnome you knew?
Related
Gnomeregan · Gelbin Mekkatorque · Ironforge · Professions and Crafting · Dun Morogh · A Short History of Azeroth

Lore/Peoples/Goblins.title: Goblins
Lore/Peoples/Goblins.content:
Goblins



                  
                  In a sentence 
                  
                

Neutral by policy, mercenary by nature, and the only people on Azeroth to whom the Alliance–Horde war is primarily a market opportunity.


Once slaves of the Ogres on the Isle of Kezan, the goblins were transformed by exposure to kaja’mite ore, which made them brilliant, greedy, and permanently overexcited.
The Steamwheedle Cartel enforces strict neutrality in its port towns — Booty Bay, Gadgetzan, Everlook, Ratchet — where Alliance and Horde drink at the same bar under threat of the Cartel’s very serious bruisers. Violence in a goblin town is bad for business, and goblins deal with bad-for-business decisively.
Not all goblins are Steamwheedle. The Venture Company strip-mines Kalimdor with no regard for anything. The Bilgewater and other cartels freelance. The Blackwater Raiders run Booty Bay’s docks.
Doing Business With Them
Goblins are Azeroth’s logistics. They sell transport, explosives, information, and each other, and they will do it for anyone with coin regardless of banner — which makes a goblin contract one of the few things an Alliance and a Horde traveller can both hold at once.
Related
Steamwheedle Cartel · Venture Company · Booty Bay · Gadgetzan · Professions and Crafting · Travel and Downtime

Lore/Peoples/Harpies.title: Harpies
Lore/Peoples/Harpies.content:
Harpies


                  
                  In a sentence 
                  
                

Winged, screaming, and the only people in Kalimdor that even the centaur avoid.


All-female avian humanoids, universally hostile, nesting in the highlands of Kalimdor. Their origin is disputed — night elf legend blames a curse; they are not answering questions.
Bloodfury (Stonetalon Mountains) · Witchwing (The Barrens) · Dustwind (Thousand Needles) · Frayfeather (Feralas) · Wildmane (Feralas) · Screeching (Desolace)
