Places/Capitals/Darnassus.title: Darnassus
Places/Capitals/Darnassus.content:
Darnassus



                  
                  Arrival 
                  
                

There is no ground. The whole city is built in the branches of a tree the size of a mountain range, lit silver, and the only sound is water and wind through leaves.


Faction: Alliance · Ruler: High Priestess Tyrande Whisperwind
The night elf capital, grown into the branches of Teldrassil — a city four years old belonging to a people ten thousand years old.
Tyrande Whisperwind rules essentially alone. Malfurion Stormrage is lost in The Emerald Dream. Fandral Staghelm leads the Cenarion Circle from the Cenarion Enclave and disagrees with her on nearly everything.


                  
                  A capital in mourning 
                  
                

The night elves lost their immortality four years ago and have not culturally processed it. Darnassus is beautiful and it is quiet in a way that isn’t peace.


What It Feels Like
Quiet enough to be unnerving. There is no market noise, no hammering, no shouting. Kaldorei speak softly in public and find raised voices genuinely shocking. Visitors from Ironforge describe the silence as the hardest adjustment.
Grown, not built. Nothing here was quarried. The walkways are living wood, the walls are bark, and the whole city moves very slightly in the wind. Rain arrives as a fine drift through the canopy rather than a downpour.
Silver light, always. Moonlight is the working light, supplemented by moonwells. Full daylight never quite reaches the upper terraces.
Watchful. Sentinels are everywhere, they are all women, they are all armed, and they will track a stranger’s progress across the city without troubling to hide it.
Districts and Sites





































PlaceWhat’s ThereTemple of the MoonTyrande’s seat. Sisters of Elune. The great moonwell.Cenarion EnclaveFandral Staghelm and the druidsWarrior’s TerraceSentinelsCraftsmen’s TerraceTrade and professionsTradesmen’s TerraceAuction house, bankThe Temple GardensWhere the moonwells areRut’theran VillageAt the roots — ferry to Auberdine and Stormwind
Walking It
You arrive at Rut’theran Village, at the roots, and take the portal up. That transition is deliberate: the village is a working harbour, ordinary and a little shabby, and then you step through and the city is silver.
The Temple of the Moon dominates everything — the largest structure and the actual seat of power, since Tyrande rules as High Priestess rather than as a queen. The great moonwell inside is public and pilgrims drink from it.
The Cenarion Enclave sits apart across a bridge, which says something about the relationship. The druids keep their own hours and their own counsel.
The terraces are where ordinary life happens, and they are the least busy commercial district of any capital.
Who You Meet

Sentinels, armoured, unhurried, and watching. The city’s police, army, and border force.
Priestesses of Elune in silver, running the temple and most of the civil administration
Druids, rarer than you would expect — many are still asleep in the barrow dens
The newly awakened — druids out of the Dens who missed The Third War entirely and are visibly disoriented
Very few children. This is the detail visitors notice last and think about longest.
Tauren druids, occasionally, on Cenarion business, treated with genuine warmth

Customs and Manners

Greet properly. “Ishnu-alah” — well fortune to you. The reply is “Ishnu-dal-dieb.” Kaldorei will not translate and will notice if you learn it.
Speak quietly. Volume reads as aggression.
Do not hurry anyone. A kaldorei asked for an immediate answer will simply not give one.
Never draw on arcane magic here. Not illegal exactly — the Sentinels will simply stop you, and the room will go cold. This is policy, not superstition. See Night Elves.
Do not cut living wood. Not even a twig. Not even for a fire.
Do not ask about age. It was a neutral question for ten thousand years and is now the most painful subject in the city.
Moonwells are not decorative. Drinking is permitted; washing in one is a desecration.

Food and Drink
Kaldorei eating is light, seasonal, and largely vegetarian — not from doctrine but because a people who lived forever never developed an appetite for excess.

Moonberry juice, sweet and faintly luminous, served everywhere and to everyone
Silverleaf tea, bitter, taken at moonrise
Fruit, nuts, mushrooms and river fish, prepared simply and beautifully
Sweetblossom bread, dense and honeyed, the one thing visitors reliably ask for again
Elven wine — old, expensive, and poured in small quantities. Getting visibly drunk is a serious embarrassment.

There is no tavern culture. The nearest thing is a communal table on the Craftsmen’s Terrace where food is shared without much being said. Dwarves find this baffling and slightly sad.
What You Can Buy
Small selection, extremely high quality, and no arcane goods whatsoever.

































TradeWhereLeatherworkingCraftsmen’s Terrace. Best in the world — kaldorei leatherwork is unmatched.Herbalism, alchemyCraftsmen’s Terrace, with instruction that treats plants as peopleTailoringFine, light, and expensiveSkinning, first aidWidely taughtEnchantingYes — nature-flavoured, and the practitioners resent the categoryEngineering, arcane goodsNo. Do not ask.
See Professions and Crafting.
Groups Worth Knowing

The Sisters of Elune — priesthood and civil service in one. Tyrande’s institution.
The Sentinels — the army, and the most experienced light infantry in the world
Cenarion Circle — druids, headquartered at the Enclave, and the one body with warm Tauren ties across the faction line
The Wardens — jailers. Mostly absent, chasing an escapee, and their absence is felt.
The Barrow Den keepers — a small order tending sleeping druids who have not woken. Grim, patient work.

Downtime Here
Darnassus is the Alliance’s best city for nature trades and quiet study, and its worst for shopping. See Travel and Downtime.

































ActivityWhat Darnassus OffersCraftLeatherworking and alchemy at the highest level available anywhereResearchTemple archives, ten thousand years deep — if a priestess vouches for youTrainDruid, hunter, priest, rogue, warrior. No mages, no paladins.Curry favourThe Cenarion Circle takes outsiders seriously if you have done something for a forestCarouseBarely applicable. A shared table and a long silence. Roll once on Rumor Tables, not twice.Tend a relationshipThe best city in the game for it — kaldorei measure trust in years and notice effort
Things To Do In A Session

Attend moonrise at the Temple — the whole city stops, and it is genuinely moving
Talk to someone newly awakened from a barrow den, and hear them ask what year it is
Sit in on a Cenarion argument about Teldrassil and hear how carefully nobody says what they think
Take the ferry from Rut’theran and watch the city recede — the best way to appreciate its scale
Try to buy something arcane and learn exactly how a polite refusal can feel like a slammed door

Related
Tyrande Whisperwind · Night Elves · Teldrassil · Fandral Staghelm · Malfurion Stormrage · Cenarion Circle · The Alliance · Elune · Travel and Downtime

Places/Capitals/Ironforge.title: Ironforge
Places/Capitals/Ironforge.content:
Ironforge



                  
                  Arrival 
                  
                

The gate is a hole in a mountain and beyond it the air is hot and smells of coal. The whole city is one vast circular hall around a lake of molten metal, and it never gets dark.


Faction: Alliance · Ruler: King Magni Bronzebeard
The most functional institution in the Alliance. Magni Bronzebeard rules a mountain that has fed, armed, and sheltered every ally who asked — including an entire displaced nation.
The Great Forge at the centre is a lake of molten metal and the source of most Alliance steel. The Deeprun Tram runs from here to Stormwind City beneath the sea, which is a genuine engineering marvel that dwarves and gnomes built together and mention constantly.


                  
                  Moira 
                  
                

His only daughter, Princess Moira Bronzebeard, was abducted by Dagran Thaurissan of the Dark Iron Dwarves and is in Blackrock Depths. Magni wants her back and has said so publicly, repeatedly.


What It Feels Like
Warm, bright, and never quiet. There is no night here. The Forge burns constantly, so the light and the hammering never stop, and dwarves find the concept of a curfew funny. Visitors sleep badly for the first two days and then sleep better than they have in months.
Prosperous, and unembarrassed about it. Ironforge is the only Alliance capital with a working treasury. Nothing is falling down. The bridges are maintained. This is a city that pays its people.
Genuinely welcoming. Dwarves like company. A stranger who sits at a bar will be talked at within five minutes, and the conversation will be about work.
Districts and Sites









































PlaceWhat’s ThereThe Great ForgeThe molten heart of the cityThe CommonsAuction house, bank, tradeTinker TownThe Gnomeregan Exiles. An entire nation in one neighbourhood.Hall of ExplorersExplorers’ League. The library. The Titan artefacts.The Military WardBarracks, trainersThe Mystic WardMages and the Hall of MysteriesHigh SeatMagni’s throneDeeprun TramTo Stormwind. Under the sea. Two hours.
Walking It
Everything is a ring around the Forge, so you cannot get lost — you can only go clockwise or anticlockwise. Dwarves give directions that way and find maps unnecessary.
Tinker Town is the loudest and strangest quarter: gnomish scale, gnomish noise, machinery in the streets, and the constant low hum of things running. The dwarves gave the gnomes a whole district and have never once suggested a timeline for leaving.
The Hall of Explorers is the best library on the continent and the only one with a live excavation department. It is also where the Explorers’ League recruits, loudly, from anyone who looks capable.
Who You Meet

Smiths and miners, off shift, still sooty, drinking early because their shift ended at dawn
Gnomes, everywhere, in numbers that surprise first-time visitors
Explorers’ League scholars trying to fund something
Wildhammer visitors from Aerie Peak — gryphon-riders, tattooed, treated warmly and not quite as citizens
Mountaineers back from Dun Morogh patrol, complaining about troggs
Human and night elf envoys, looking slightly overheated

Customs and Manners

Your trade is your introduction. A dwarf asks what you do before your name. Answering vaguely is odd.
Buy the round. Refusing a drink is fine; refusing to reciprocate is not.
Clan matters. Ask a dwarf’s clan, not their nation. Bronzebeard, Wildhammer — and be careful how you ask about the third.
Do not say “Dark Iron” idly. It is a live war and somebody in the room has lost family to it.
Craftsmanship is sacred. Insulting a piece of work insults the person who made it, and dwarves take this seriously enough to fight about.
Nobody hurries. A dwarf who has been asked to rush a job will do it slower, on principle.

Food and Drink
Ironforge eats heavily and often, and drinks more than any city in the world.

Roast boar and mutton, spiced hard, served in slabs
Rock-hard travel bread that softens in stew and is genuinely good after two days on the road
Mountain trout from Loch Modan, and cave mushrooms grown in the lower tunnels
Cheese, aged in the cold levels, exported at absurd prices to Stormwind
Stout — dark, thick, and the city’s principal export after steel. Thunderbrew is the name everyone knows.
Gnomish liqueurs in Tinker Town, brightly coloured, unwisely strong, occasionally luminous

Taverns. Stonefire Tavern in the Military Ward, loud and good. Bruuk’s Corner by the Forge, where the smiths go. Tinker Town has a small place run by gnomes where the drinks are measured to the millilitre.
What You Can Buy
The best forge-work in the world, and the widest engineering selection anywhere.

































TradeWhereBlacksmithing, miningThe Great Forge. Best in the world, and they know it.EngineeringTinker Town — the gnomish branch, and the only place to learn it properlyMining and prospectingThe Forge district, with instructors who have actually dugAlchemy, enchantingMystic WardLeatherworking, tailoringThe CommonsGuns and ammunitionIronforge invented them. Nowhere better.
See Professions and Crafting.
Groups Worth Knowing

Explorers’ League — will fund an expedition anywhere on the strength of one good argument. The single best patron for a low-level party in the Alliance.
The Senate — the clan assembly. Slow, procedural, and where the Wildhammer question keeps failing to resolve.
Gnomeregan Exiles — a full government-in-exile in one district, with a very specific war aim
The Mountaineers — Dun Morogh’s standing patrol. Hire out as guides.
Wildhammer Clan envoys — sympathetic, not subject, and worth cultivating separately

Downtime Here
Ironforge is the Alliance’s best crafting and research city, and the friendliest place to spend a week. See Travel and Downtime.

































ActivityWhat Ironforge OffersCraftBest in the Alliance for smithing, engineering and miningResearchThe Hall of Explorers. Unmatched for anything titan, ancient, or underground.TrainAll classes but druid. Paladin training here is practical rather than devotional.Curry favourThe Explorers’ League is the easiest faction in the game to impress — bring them something oldCarouseStonefire or Bruuk’s. Roll twice on Rumor Tables.Work a tradeCaravan escort to Menethil, mountaineer contracts, trogg bounties
Things To Do In A Session

Take a commission at the Hall of Explorers — the fastest way to get a party moving with a patron and a budget
Sit through a Senate session and watch three centuries of grudge conducted in procedural language
Visit Tinker Town and be shown an invention that should not work
Drink with off-shift smiths and learn what the Forge is actually producing lately, and for whom
Ride the Tram to Stormwind and feel the difference in the two cities immediately

Related
Magni Bronzebeard · Dwarves · Gnomes · Explorers’ League · Uldaman · Dun Morogh · Dark Iron Dwarves · Wildhammer Clan · Gnomeregan Exiles · The Alliance · Travel and Downtime

Places/Capitals/Orgrimmar.title: Orgrimmar
Places/Capitals/Orgrimmar.content:
Orgrimmar



                  
                  Arrival 
                  
                

Timber palisades and iron spikes built into a red canyon, smoke from a hundred forges, and drums. It smells of hot metal and dust and it was not here five years ago.


Faction: Horde · Ruler: Warchief Thrall
The Horde capital, raised in Durotar by a people who spent a generation in internment camps and will not be caged again.
It is raw. Nothing here is old. Nothing is decorative. Thrall holds court in Grommash Hold, named for Grom Hellscream, who died freeing the orcs from the blood curse.
Also: Ragefire Chasm opens directly beneath the city. The Cleft’s own people stay out of the lower passages, and the reasons they give do not agree with each other.
What It Feels Like
Under construction, everywhere. Scaffolding, fresh timber, half-finished walls. The city is being built while you stand in it, and orcs are visibly proud of that rather than embarrassed.
Hot and dry. Durotar is red rock and dust. The canyon holds the heat. Water is rationed in a way no other capital rations anything, and wasting it is a serious offence.
Loud, direct, and easier than it looks. Newcomers expect hostility and get bluntness instead. An orc who dislikes you says so, which visitors from Stormwind find alarming and then restful.
Drums. Not constant — but the Valley of Honor keeps a rhythm going during training hours, and you feel it through the ground.
Districts and Sites





































PlaceWhat’s ThereValley of StrengthThe main gate. Auction house, bank, zeppelin tower.Valley of WisdomGrommash Hold. Thrall’s seat.Valley of HonorWarriors, the arena, the forgeValley of SpiritsDarkspear Trolls quarterThe DragTrade, leatherworking, the road between valleysCleft of ShadowWarlocks. Rogues. Entrance to Ragefire Chasm.Ragefire ChasmThe fissure under the Cleft. Warm, and it smells wrong. Nobody patrols it.
Walking It
The Valley of Strength is the front door and the marketplace, and the zeppelin tower dominates it. Everything arrives here.
The Drag is a covered road cut between the valleys — shaded, cool, and the only comfortable place to stand at midday, so it is where deals actually get done.
The Valley of Honor is where the city is loudest: the forge, the arena, and open training grounds where anyone can be challenged and often is.
The Valley of Spirits is the Darkspear quarter and feels like a different city — stilted huts, different cooking smells, drums in a different rhythm.
The Cleft of Shadow is dark, low, and everybody knows what happens there. Nobody says it out loud.
Who You Meet

Grunts on the gate, bored and observant
Smiths and armourers, working in the open because there is nowhere to work indoors
Shaman, more visible here than any priest is in Stormwind, and consulted on practical matters
Darkspear everywhere, in a quarter they were given and still call temporary
Kor’kron — Thrall’s own guard, newer than the walls, very serious about it
Tauren visitors from Thunder Bluff, usually on Cenarion or diplomatic business
Goblins running freight through the zeppelin tower, neutral and charging accordingly

Customs and Manners

Say what you mean. Orcish conversation is direct to a degree other peoples read as rudeness. Softening a request makes it unclear, and unclear is worse than blunt.
Strength is greeted, not boasted about. Claiming a deed you cannot back is the fastest way to be challenged.
Challenges are real and usually not lethal. In the Valley of Honor a challenge is training. Elsewhere it is serious.
Do not waste water. The single strongest taboo in the city.
Never mock the camps. A generation was born behind a fence. Jokes about it end conversations and sometimes friendships.
Honour the dead by name. Grommash Hold is named for a man who died four years ago. Say his name properly.
Fel magic is banned and practised. Everyone knows. Saying so loudly in the Valley of Wisdom is a political act.

Food and Drink
Orcish cooking is fire, meat, and not much else — a cuisine built by people who were recently nomadic and are now learning to farm hard ground.

Roasted boar, raptor and scorpid, spiced heavily, cooked over open flame
Hard flatbread, cooked on stones, and the staple everyone eats
Dried and salted meat, still the backbone of the diet — a camp habit that stuck
Cactus apple, sour, plentiful, and the only fresh thing that grows well in Durotar
Thunder ale and grog, strong and rough
Troll cooking in the Valley of Spirits — fish, jungle spice, and much better than the orcish food, which orcs will admit after a drink

Taverns. The inn in the Valley of Strength is functional. The Broken Tusk is where you actually go — mercenaries, caravan crews, and goblins looking for hands.
What You Can Buy
Practical goods, excellent leather and metal, and no arcane market to speak of.

































TradeWhereBlacksmithing, miningValley of Honor. Rough, strong, unbeautiful work.Leatherworking, skinningThe Drag. Excellent — Durotar has a lot of dead beasts.Alchemy, herbalismThe Drag, and troll practitioners in the Valley of SpiritsTailoringLimited. Cloth is imported and expensive.EngineeringGoblin branch only, through the zeppelin tower tradersPoisons and shadow goodsCleft of Shadow. Ask carefully.
See Professions and Crafting.
Groups Worth Knowing

The Kor’kron — Thrall’s guard. Small, new, and increasingly the instrument of his authority.
The shaman circles — rebuilt from near-nothing in four years, and consulted on water, weather and war
The Warsong — Grom’s old clan, mostly in Ashenvale, and their veterans in the city are unrepentant
Darkspear Tribe — Vol’jin’s people in the Valley of Spirits, and the sharpest political operators in the Horde
Steamwheedle Cartel goblins — neutral freight and information, at a price
Burning Blade — a fel cult, present, denied, and recruiting

Downtime Here
Orgrimmar is the Horde’s training hub and the best place on either continent to find work. See Travel and Downtime.

































ActivityWhat Orgrimmar OffersTrainEvery Horde class. Shaman training here is the real thing.CraftSmithing and leatherworking are strong; tailoring and engineering are notWork a tradeThe best in the world. Caravan guard, arena bouts, goblin contracts, bounties in The Barrens.Curry favourProve something. Orgrimmar rewards deeds far faster than words. Reputation as a Mechanic.CarouseThe Broken Tusk. Roll twice on Rumor Tables.ResearchWeakest of the capitals. Four years old, and almost nothing is written down.
Things To Do In A Session

Fight in the Valley of Honor — a challenge, not a death match, and the fastest way to be taken seriously
Watch Thrall hold court at Grommash Hold and see a young warchief manage people twice his age
Take a goblin freight contract at the zeppelin tower and find out what you have agreed to carry
Eat in the Valley of Spirits and let a Darkspear explain, kindly, why orcish cooking is bad
Stand at the mouth of Ragefire Chasm and notice how little anyone wants to discuss it

Related
Thrall · Orcs · Durotar · The Horde · Vol’jin · Darkspear Trolls · Burning Blade · Ragefire Chasm · Grom Hellscream · Travel and Downtime

Places/Capitals/Stormwind-City.title: Stormwind City
Places/Capitals/Stormwind-City.content:
Stormwind City


                  
                  Arrival 
                  
                

White stone and blue banners, canals under arched bridges, and a cathedral you can see from every district. Gulls over the harbour road. Somebody is always shouting about the price of bread.


Faction: Alliance · Ruler: King Anduin Wrynn, regent Bolvar Fordragon
The Alliance’s greatest city, rebuilt from rubble after The First War by stonemasons who were never paid.
What It Feels Like
Grand, and slightly threadbare. The masonry is magnificent and the maintenance budget is not. Scaffolding stands on the Cathedral’s north face and has for two years. The canals are clean in the Trade District and less so behind the Dwarven District.
Crowded with people who arrived recently. Half the city is refugees — Lordaeron families four years on, Westfall farmers who gave up, Dalaran survivors who teach in back rooms. Accents from four dead kingdoms. Everyone is polite about it and nobody is comfortable.
Loud in the morning, tense in the evening. The guard presence in the Trade District is heavy and visibly thinner everywhere else.
The Political Situation

King Anduin Wrynn is about ten and frightened
His father Varian Wrynn is missing, and nobody in the palace will say more than that
Bolvar Fordragon governs honestly and is being managed
The nobility are contemptuous of the outer provinces and the outer provinces have noticed
Westfall, Duskwood, and Redridge Mountains have all been effectively abandoned

Districts and Sites









































PlaceWhat’s ThereTrade DistrictAuction house, bank, the main squareOld TownSI:7. Rogues. The Pig and Whistle.Cathedral SquareStormwind Cathedral. Church of the Holy Light. Archbishop Benedictus.Mage QuarterThe Wizard’s Sanctum. Portals. Warlocks in the Slaughtered Lamb’s cellar.Dwarven DistrictIronforge expatriates. The Deeprun Tram terminus.The ParkNight elf quarter. Small, quiet, resented by nobody and visited by few.The StockadeThe prison. Currently rioting. The crown is not discussing it.Stormwind KeepThe throne room. The council.
Walking It
From the front gate the road runs through Valley of Heroes — statues of the Second War’s dead, and the only place in the city where humans, dwarves and elves stand as equals in stone. It puts visitors in the right frame of mind, which is the point.
The Trade District is the loudest square in the Eastern Kingdoms. The Canals ring everything and every district touches one, which is how goods actually move; the bridges are where you meet people.
Old Town is the oldest surviving stonework and knows it. Narrow, dark by four in the afternoon, and the guard patrols are noticeably lighter.
The Mage Quarter smells faintly of ozone. The Park is the quietest place in the city — the kaldorei quarter, a handful of residents, moonlight-coloured stone, and a small shrine nobody else visits.
Who You Meet

Guards in blue tabards, underpaid and mostly decent. Nine copper a day, and they will mention it.
Refugees, everywhere, doing work below what they trained for. A Lordaeron surgeon runs a fish stall on the canal.
Clergy in white and gold, more visible than the crown. The Church feeds people the crown does not.
Petitioners on the Keep steps, queuing to be told the treasury is empty
Dwarven engineers from the Tram works, permanently covered in grease and permanently pleased with themselves
Nobles’ retainers running errands nobody explains

Customs and Manners

The Light is public. Strangers say “Light be with you” on parting. Refusing to answer it is not rude exactly, but it is noticed.
Rank is spoken. Address a knight as ser, a priest as father or sister. Getting it wrong marks you as provincial.
Do not discuss Lordaeron carelessly. Half the room lost somebody. “That’s a Lordaeron problem” used to be a shrug and now it starts fights.
Fel magic is a crime. Warlocks exist in the Slaughtered Lamb’s cellar and everyone pretends otherwise. Casting it openly means the Stockade.
Tipping is not a custom. Paying a craftsman late is the deepest possible insult here, for reasons the whole city understands.

Food and Drink
Human cooking is hearty and unambitious. Bread, stew, river fish, root vegetables, mutton on a good day.

Canal pike and eel, sold fried from carts. Cheap, decent, universal.
Westfall bread — the loaf everyone grew up on. Getting scarce and expensive, because Westfall is not shipping grain. This is the single most common conversation in the city.
Elwynn cider and ale, ordinary and everywhere
Dwarven stout, imported through the Tram, expensive, and a status drink
Ironforge cheese and smoked boar, likewise imported

Taverns. The Pig and Whistle in Old Town — where SI:7 people drink and nobody says so. The Blue Recluse in the Mage Quarter, quiet, tolerant of odd conversation. The Gilded Rose in the Trade District, for people with money.
What You Can Buy
The best general market in the Alliance, and the widest selection of trainers anywhere.

































TradeWhereBlacksmithing, armour, weaponsOld Town and the Dwarven DistrictAlchemy, herbsMage QuarterTailoring, enchantingMage Quarter and Trade DistrictLeatherworkingThe Trade District’s back lanesEngineeringDwarven District only, and it is gnomish workPoisonsOld Town. Not on a shelf. See Ravenholdt.
See Professions and Crafting for how trades work here.
Groups Worth Knowing

The Church of the Holy Light — runs the Cathedral, the orphanage, and most of the actual charity. More trusted than the crown.
Order of the Silver Hand — headquartered at the Cathedral, leaderless since Uther, and arguing with itself
SI:7 — Old Town. Officially does not exist. Hires quietly.
The trade guilds — furriers, smiths, brewers. Real political weight, and they remember what happened to the masons.
The Kirin Tor in exile — a handful of Dalaran survivors teaching in the Mage Quarter without any authority to certify anyone

Downtime Here
Stormwind is the best training and research city in the Alliance. See Travel and Downtime.

































ActivityWhat Stormwind OffersTrainEvery class trainer except shaman and druid. The default reason to come.ResearchThe Cathedral library, the Wizard’s Sanctum, and the Royal Archive if you have a name to dropCraftEvery primary trade, best selection in the AllianceCurry favourThe Church, the guilds, and SI:7 all take on outsiders. Reputation as a Mechanic.CarouseThe Pig and Whistle. Roll twice on Rumor Tables.Work a tradeCaravan guard south, harbour work, and bounties on the Westfall road
Things To Do In A Session

Attend a service at the Cathedral and watch who is present and who is conspicuously not
Queue at the Keep with the petitioners and hear six real grievances in an hour
Take the Deeprun Tram to Ironforge — two hours under the sea, and a genuinely good conversation scene
Visit the Park and find the one night elf who will talk to you
Ask about the Stockade riot and notice how quickly people change the subject

Related
Kingdom of Stormwind · Anduin Wrynn · Bolvar Fordragon · Varian Wrynn · Elwynn Forest · The Stockade · Stormwind Cathedral · Humans · The Alliance · Travel and Downtime

Places/Capitals/Thunder-Bluff.title: Thunder Bluff
Places/Capitals/Thunder-Bluff.content:
Thunder Bluff



                  
                  Arrival 
                  
                

Four mesas rising out of golden plain, connected by rope bridges hundreds of feet above the ground. Totems, wind chimes, and drying hides. It is the quietest capital in the world.


Faction: Horde · Ruler: High Chieftain Cairne Bloodhoof
The tauren capital in Mulgore, four years old and already the most peaceful place on either continent.
Cairne Bloodhoof is the only leader in the world on speaking terms with almost everyone — Thrall’s mentor, respected by Jaina Proudmoore, honoured by night elf druids, and the Horde’s most consistent internal critic.
What It Feels Like
Open, high, and windy. No walls anywhere. Thunder Bluff has never been attacked and is not built as though it expects to be, which is either serene or naive depending on who you ask.
Slow. Nobody hurries. Conversations have long pauses in them that are not awkward to anyone but visitors. A request answered “I will consider it” genuinely means days.
Unarmed, mostly. Weapons are carried but rarely worn in the upper rises. Coming to Elder Rise armed is not forbidden, just noticed.
The bridges. Rope and plank, hundreds of feet up, no railings, swaying in the wind. Tauren cross them carrying furniture. Everyone else edges across sideways and pretends not to.
Districts and Sites

































PlaceWhat’s ThereElder RiseCairne’s tent. The elders. The seat of government.Spirit RiseShamans, spirit healers, the Cenarion taurenHunter RiseHunters, the Hunter’s HallThe Middle RiseAuction house, bank, innPools of VisionSacred waterThe rope bridgesHundreds of feet up. No railings. Tauren find this unremarkable.
Walking It
You arrive by lift from the plain below — a wooden platform on ropes, operated by hand, that visitors ride once and remember.
The Middle Rise is the practical mesa: trade, the inn, and where most business happens. It is the only crowded place in the city.
Elder Rise is where government occurs, which mostly means elders sitting under an open awning listening for a long time before anyone speaks. Petitioners are heard in the order they arrived, regardless of rank.
Spirit Rise holds the shaman and the druids and is where the Cenarion Circle’s tauren work. It is the quietest mesa on a quiet mountain.
The Pools of Vision are sacred and public. People come to think.
Who You Meet

Elders, everywhere, and genuinely listened to rather than humoured
Hunters back from Mulgore with kills, going straight to the drying racks
Shaman and spiritwalkers, consulted on weather, water, illness and disputes
Druids, the first generation their people have ever produced, most of them very young for the role
Night elf druids on Cenarion business — the only place in the world where an Alliance and Horde member work together routinely and nobody comments
Refugees and travellers of every people. Thunder Bluff turns nobody away, which is policy.
Grimtotem, occasionally, being coldly polite

Customs and Manners

Do not interrupt. The single most important rule. A pause is not an invitation; tauren leave space in speech deliberately.
Greet with “Aho.” It covers hello, agreement, and I hear you. Enormously flexible and always appropriate.
Elders speak first and last. Cutting across one is a serious offence, and visitors do it constantly.
Waste is obscene. Take what you need, use all of it, and do not leave food. This applies to guests.
Weapons down on Elder Rise. Not a law. Just do it.
Never lie about a hunt. Exaggerating a kill is the local equivalent of forgery.
Ask before entering a tent. Doors are hides. Privacy is a courtesy rather than a lock, and it is absolutely expected.

Food and Drink
Tauren cooking is communal, generous, and slow. Meals are shared from a common pot and eaten sitting down. Nobody eats alone if it can be helped.

Roasted plainstrider and kodo, slow-cooked over embers for most of a day
Mulgore grain, ground into flatbread and porridge, the staple
Dried meat and pemmican — a nomad diet that outlived the nomadism
Sweet corn and root vegetables from the first farms anyone has planted in generations
Spirit water from the Pools, taken ceremonially and in very small amounts
Fermented kodo milk, sour, strong, and an acquired taste that visitors rarely acquire

There is no drinking culture in the Orgrimmar sense. There is a fire, and a pot, and a great many hours.
What You Can Buy
Modest, excellent, and honestly priced. Nobody haggles hard here and trying it marks you.

































TradeWhereLeatherworking, skinningHunter Rise. Superb — tauren waste nothing off a kill.Herbalism, alchemySpirit Rise, taught as medicine rather than chemistryCooking, first aidThe best instruction anywhere, and freely givenBlacksmithing, miningPresent but basic. Buy metalwork in Orgrimmar.Tailoring, enchantingLimitedEngineeringNone. Tauren find the whole discipline slightly rude.
See Professions and Crafting.
Groups Worth Knowing

The elders’ council — the actual government, and the most accessible leadership on either side. Anyone may petition.
Cenarion Circle — tauren and night elf druids working as partners. The one warm cross-faction channel in the world.
The spiritwalkers — speak with ancestors, hold authority no chieftain can overrule
The Bloodhoof tribe — Cairne’s own, and the closest thing to a ruling house
Other tribes — Runetotem, Skychaser, Ragetotem, Winterhoof, Wildmane. Not subjects. Allies with opinions.
The Grimtotem — present, cold, and not hiding their contempt

Downtime Here
Thunder Bluff is the best place in the world to recover, learn nature trades, and talk to somebody properly. See Travel and Downtime.

































ActivityWhat Thunder Bluff OffersTend a relationshipThe best city in the game for it. Time spent is visibly valued.CraftLeatherworking, alchemy, cooking and first aid at the highest levelTrainDruid, shaman, hunter, warrior, priest. No warlocks, no rogues.Curry favourThe Cenarion Circle and the elders both reward patience over deedsResearchOral, not written. Ask an elder and be prepared to sit for a long time.CarouseNot really available. A fire, a pot, and hours. Roll once on Rumor Tables and make it a good one.
Things To Do In A Session

Petition the elders about anything and experience being genuinely, unhurriedly heard
Sit at a communal meal and let a stranger feed you, which is the whole culture in one scene
Cross a rope bridge in the wind — a free, memorable, entirely non-combat challenge
Watch a tauren druid and a night elf druid work together and think about what that means four years after Ashenvale
Visit the Pools of Vision and be offered a vision you did not ask for

Related

Places/Capitals/Undercity.title: Undercity
Places/Capitals/Undercity.content:
Undercity


                  
                  Arrival 
                  
                

You descend through the ruins of a throne room, past a bloodstain nobody has cleaned, into a circular city of green light and running sewage. The dead do not need air, and it shows.


Faction: Horde · Ruler: Banshee Queen Sylvanas Windrunner
The Forsaken capital, built in the catacombs beneath the ruins of Lordaeron’s Capital City.
Sylvanas Windrunner chose this site deliberately: the entrance passes directly through the throne room where Arthas Menethil murdered his father, King Terenas. She makes everyone walk through it.
What It Feels Like
Wrong, and deliberately so. Green light from apothecary lamps, a constant low drip, and the smell — visitors describe it as a cellar that has been closed too long. The Forsaken have not fixed any of this because none of it inconveniences them.
Orderly. This is the surprise. The streets are clean-swept, the districts are logical, the record-keeping is meticulous. A people with no appetites and no need for sleep get a great deal done.
Quiet in an unusual way. No eating, no children, no snoring, no crowds outside working hours. What you hear instead is work: presses, scratching pens, the apothecaries’ equipment.
Watchful without being hostile. Living visitors are stared at. Not with menace — with something closer to curiosity, and occasionally with envy that nobody admits to.
Districts and Sites









































PlaceWhat’s ThereThe Ruins of LordaeronAbove. The throne room. The bloodstain.The Trade QuarterAuction house, bankThe War QuarterWarriors, the Forsaken militaryThe Magic QuarterMages, warlocksThe ApothecariumThe alchemists’ halls. Sealed to visitors.The Rogues’ QuarterRogues, poisonsThe Royal QuarterSylvanas’s throne.Zeppelin towerTo Orgrimmar and Grom’gol
Walking It
You come down through the ruins first, and the route is theatre. Broken banners, a collapsed hall, and the stain on the throne room floor that has been left exactly as it was. Nobody hurries you through it.
Below, the city is a wheel — an outer ring canal with the quarters arranged around it and the Royal Quarter at the hub. It is the most rationally planned capital in the world, because it was designed all at once by people who did not have to compromise with anyone living there first.
The canal carries sewage and run-off. It is not pleasant and it is not hidden.
The Apothecarium is sealed to visitors and the guards on it are not conversational.
Who You Meet

Forsaken, in every state of preservation from nearly-lifelike to frankly alarming, dressed with more care than you would expect
Deathstalkers — intelligence work, unmarked, and they will already know why you are here
Dark Rangers — elven women, Sylvanas’s personal loyalists, and the most unsettling people in the city
Apothecaries in stained coats, hurrying, disinclined to chat
Orc and troll envoys, visibly uncomfortable, keeping visits short
Living traders — a small, hardy population who make excellent money and have made their peace
Almost no Tauren. They come when they must and leave the same day.

Customs and Manners

Do not ask how they died. The single hard rule. Some will tell you. Being asked is an intrusion.
Do not offer food or drink. A kindness elsewhere, a pointed joke here.
Free will is sacred. Any suggestion that a Forsaken could be commanded, compelled or charmed will end the conversation and possibly the relationship.
Do not heal a Forsaken with the Light without asking. It hurts them. Doing it uninvited is closer to assault than to charity.
Black humour is the register. Grim jokes about their own condition are normal and expected. Pity is not, and lands very badly.
“The Dark Lady watches over you” is the standard blessing. Returning it is polite and costs you nothing.
Do not linger near the Apothecarium. Nobody will explain why. Everyone will notice.

Food and Drink
The Forsaken do not eat. This is the fact that reorganises the whole city, and visitors take a day to absorb it.

There is no restaurant culture, no tavern culture, and no market smell. The inn exists for living guests and Horde envoys and is oddly formal about it.
What the markets sell instead is reagents, chemicals, preservatives, poisons, cloth, and information. The Trade Quarter is a supply depot, not a food market.
For living visitors: salted rations, hard bread, and imported ale, all sold at a markup and all slightly stale. The Forsaken find this funny.
Embalming supplies and preservative wine are on open sale, and are the city’s genuine luxury goods. A well-preserved Forsaken has spent money.

What You Can Buy
The best alchemy and poison market in the world, and very little else.





































TradeWhereAlchemyUnmatched anywhere. The instruction is superb and slightly chilling.PoisonsOpenly sold. No other capital does this.HerbalismExcellent — corpse-flower and grave-moss varieties nobody else stocksEnchanting, tailoringMagic Quarter. Shadow-work is a speciality.First aidTaught here, which visitors find unexpectedly ironicBlacksmithing, engineeringBasic. Buy elsewhere.CookingTaught, badly, by people who have not eaten in years
See Professions and Crafting.
Groups Worth Knowing

The Deathstalkers — intelligence and assassination, the largest arm of the Forsaken state, and always recruiting
The Dark Rangers — personally loyal to Sylvanas rather than to the Forsaken as a people. That distinction matters.
The apothecaries’ guild — chemists and alchemists, respectable, well-funded, and sealed off
The Magic Quarter circles — Forsaken who were Kirin Tor apprentices in life and remember the whole curriculum
The living traders’ compact — a dozen families who supply the city and have negotiated genuinely good terms

Downtime Here
Undercity is the world’s best alchemy city and its worst carousing city. See Travel and Downtime.

































ActivityWhat Undercity OffersCraftAlchemy and poisons at a level nowhere else touchesResearchExcellent, and unnervingly well-organised. The Forsaken write everything down.TrainWarrior, rogue, mage, warlock, priest. No shaman, no druid, no hunter.Curry favourThe Deathstalkers pay for information and ask no questions about where it came fromWork a tradeCourier and escort runs to Silverpine Forest and the Plaguelands. Dangerous, well paid.CarouseEffectively unavailable. Nobody drinks. Roll once on Rumor Tables and make it grim.
Things To Do In A Session

Walk the throne room on the way in and let a Forsaken tell you, flatly, what happened there
Buy poison openly and notice that no other city in the world would allow it
Ask a Forsaken what they did before — the one question they will usually answer, and the one that opens them
Watch a living trader haggle with someone who does not need anything they sell
Try to visit the Apothecarium and be turned away politely, twice

Related
Sylvanas Windrunner · Forsaken · Tirisfal Glades · The Horde · Arthas Menethil · Scourge · Travel and Downtime

Places/Eastern-Kingdoms/Alterac-Mountain.title: Alterac Mountains
Places/Eastern-Kingdoms/Alterac-Mountain.content:
Alterac Mountains


                  
                  Arrival 
                  
                

Snow, ruins, and a violet dome on the horizon that nothing has been able to enter for four years.


Continent: Eastern Kingdoms · Levels: 30–40 (tabletop 8–10) · Held by: Syndicate, Crushridge ogres — no legitimate authority
A kingdom that was dissolved. Lord Perenolde betrayed the Alliance during The Second War and Alterac was struck from the map. Its nobility became the Syndicate, now led by his son Aliden Perenolde, and they hold the ruins of their own capital as bandits.
Crushridge ogres hold the rest. Ravenholdt Manor — the rogues’ guild — operates from a house in the hills that officially isn’t there.


                  
                  The ruins of Dalaran 
                  
                

The shattered remains of Dalaran lie under a great violet dome of magical energy, raised by surviving Kirin Tor after Archimonde destroyed the city. Nobody gets in. Nobody has explained what the dome is for. It is one of the best pieces of unexplained scenery in the game.




                  
                  Sight, sound, smell 
                  
                

Sight — Snow on black rock, a burned-out capital nobody has claimed, and bandit camps with better equipment than they should have.
Sound — Wind through ruins. Ogres somewhere above the treeline. Nothing that sounds like a settlement, because there isn’t one.
Smell — Cold stone, pine, and woodsmoke from fires whose owners do not want to be found.

Places/Eastern-Kingdoms/Alterac-Valley.title: Alterac Valley
Places/Eastern-Kingdoms/Alterac-Valley.content:
Alterac Valley


                  
                  In a sentence 
                  
                

A frozen valley in the far north where the Frostwolf orcs and the Stormpike dwarves are fighting over mining rights and a great deal of pride.


A contested valley between Alterac Mountains and the northern highlands, where the Frostwolf clan (Drek’Thar — Thrall’s own mentor) and the Stormpike Guard dwarven expedition are in open conflict.


                  
                  Sight, sound, smell 
                  
                

Sight — A high glacial valley between snowfields, with two fortified camps facing each other across ground that has been fought over long enough to be bare.
Sound — Wind off the ice. Horns from both ends of the valley. Ice cracking, which stops arguments until it is identified.
Smell — Cold stone, woodsmoke, and iron.

Alterac Mountains · Thrall · Orcs · Dwarves · Canon Boundary — What Exists at Launch

Places/Eastern-Kingdoms/Arathi-Highlands.title: Arathi Highlands
Places/Eastern-Kingdoms/Arathi-Highlands.content:
Arathi Highlands


                  
                  Arrival 
                  
                

Rolling green uplands scattered with standing stones, and a walled city on the western cliffs that is losing a siege it has been losing for years.


Continent: Eastern Kingdoms · Levels: 30–40 (tabletop 8–10) · Held by: Contested — Syndicate, ogres, and two dying garrisons
The birthplace of human civilization. Arathor was founded here, and Stromgarde Keep is the last of the seven kingdoms still holding its own ground — barely.
Prince Galen Trollbane commands a garrison fighting the Syndicate for the ruins of his own city and the Boulderfist ogres for everything else. Stromgarde has effectively left the Alliance; it was not invited back after The Second War and it has stopped asking.
Refuge Pointe (Alliance) and Hammerfall (Horde) glare at each other across the middle of the zone. Hammerfall’s orcs are Dragonmaw remnants — the clan that chained Alexstrasza at Grim Batol — now reformed under Thrall, which not everyone believes.


                  
                  Sight, sound, smell 
                  
                

Sight — Wide gold grassland, the broken towers of Stromgarde, and standing stones older than any kingdom that ever claimed them.
Sound — Wind with nothing to break it. Ogre drums from Boulderfist. Trollish horns in the hills at night.
Smell — Dry grass, horse, and old smoke from a city that has been burning slowly for twenty years.

Places/Eastern-Kingdoms/Badlands.title: Badlands
Places/Eastern-Kingdoms/Badlands.content:
Badlands


                  
                  Arrival 
                  
                

Red rock canyons and a wind that never stops. Half-buried in the cliffs is a doorway, and it was not made by anyone who is still alive.


Continent: Eastern Kingdoms · Levels: 36–45 (tabletop 10–12) · Held by: Contested — Alliance dig, Horde outpost, and something older


                  
                  Dungeon 
                  
                

Uldaman (41–51 / tabletop 12–13)


Arid canyon country whose real significance is underground.
Also here: Kargath (Horde), Lethlor Ravine full of black dragon whelps, and troggs — the failed, degenerate titan-forged — pouring out of every hole.


                  
                  Sight, sound, smell 
                  
                

Sight — Red canyon and dust, dig sites terraced into cliff faces, and bones the size of buildings weathering out of the rock.
Sound — Wind and grit. Blasting from the League camps. Troggs in the scree, and further off, something very large moving without hurry.
Smell — Hot dust, dry bone, and blackpowder.

Places/Eastern-Kingdoms/Blasted-Lands.title: Blasted Lands
Places/Eastern-Kingdoms/Blasted-Lands.content:
Blasted Lands


                  
                  Arrival 
                  
                

The ground is red and cracked and nothing grows. In the centre of it stands an arch of black stone, forty feet high, and the air inside it hums.


Continent: Eastern Kingdoms · Levels: 45–55 (tabletop 13–15) · Held by: Nobody. Nethergarde Keep holds a corner.
Thirty years ago this was Black Morass. Then Medivh opened the Dark Portal and the land died in a radius.
The Portal stands dormant — a stone arch with no light in it, watched from Nethergarde Keep by a garrison the Kirin Tor posted a generation ago and never rotated out. They have been waiting for something to come through for thirty years. Nothing has.
Demonic remnants infest the Tainted Scar: Razelikh the Defiler and his lieutenants, the Shadowsworn, and Lord Kazzak — a pit lord who is simply there, and who is beyond any reasonable party.


                  
                  Sight, sound, smell 
                  
                

Sight — Cracked red earth to the horizon, floating stone, and the Portal’s frame standing in the middle of it, lit and empty.
Sound — Wind with grit in it. Nothing living. Near the Portal, a low tone you feel in your teeth rather than hear.
Smell — Scorched rock and a dry, chemical burnt smell that is not smoke and does not fade.


Points of Interest

Places/Eastern-Kingdoms/Booty-Bay.title: Booty Bay
Places/Eastern-Kingdoms/Booty-Bay.content:
Booty Bay


                  
                  In a sentence 
                  
                

A pirate town built into a cove on stilts and scaffolding, where an orc and a human can share a table because the alternative is being thrown off a pier.


The Steamwheedle Cartel’s crown jewel, at the southern tip of Stranglethorn Vale. Run by Baron Revilgaz.
One rule: no fighting in town. The Bruisers enforce it without discussion, regardless of faction, rank, or provocation.
Sites: the Salty Sailor Tavern · the docks (ships to Ratchet and Menethil) · the auction house · the Gurubashi Arena just north, where goblins run free-for-all pit fights · Bloodsail Buccaneers in the waters south


                  
                  Sight, sound, smell 
                  
                

Sight — A town built in tiers down a cliff face into a sheltered cove, painted every colour goblins could source, with a gallows on the dock.
Sound — Gulls, rigging, auctioneers, three arguments at once in four languages, and the harbour cannon being test-fired.
Smell — Fish, tar, gunpowder, cooking grease, and money.


Related
Steamwheedle Cartel · Stranglethorn Vale · Goblins · Bloodsail Buccaneers · Travel and Downtime · Reputation as a Mechanic

Places/Eastern-Kingdoms/Burning-Steppes.title: Burning Steppes
Places/Eastern-Kingdoms/Burning-Steppes.content:
Burning Steppes


                  
                  Arrival 
                  
                

Ash falls like snow. The ground is warm through your boots. And filling the northern sky is a mountain with a hole in it, glowing.


Continent: Eastern Kingdoms · Levels: 50–58 (tabletop 15–17) · Held by: Dark Horde, Black Dragonflight, Dark Iron Dwarves
The land in Blackrock Mountain’s shadow, and one of the most dangerous zones on the continent because three separate hostile powers are using it at once.

Dark Horde orcs under Rend Blackhand hold the Spire
Black Dragonflight whelps and drakes range across the zone; Nefarian is inside the mountain
Dark Iron Dwarves control Blackrock Pass and the depths

Two tiny outposts cling on: Morgan’s Vigil (Alliance) and Flame Crest (Horde). Neither can do anything about any of it.


                  
                  Sight, sound, smell 
                  
                

Sight — Black rock, open fire-vents, and the mountain filling the northern sky like a thundercloud that has decided to stay.
Sound — Vents venting. Dragonkin overhead. Blackrock drums, which are constant enough that you stop hearing them and then notice they stopped.
Smell — Ash and sulphur, and under it a hot animal smell that visitors take a while to place.

Places/Eastern-Kingdoms/Dalaran.title: Dalaran
Places/Eastern-Kingdoms/Dalaran.content:
Dalaran


                  
                  In a sentence 
                  
                

A crater under a violet dome the size of a hill. Nothing goes in. Nothing comes out. Nobody will explain what the dome is for.


The magocratic city-state of the Kirin Tor, ruled by the Council of Six, and for centuries the world’s foremost centre of arcane learning and the secret home of the Guardians of Tirisfal.
Archimonde destroyed it during The Third War — pulled it down in a single act.
What remains is rubble in the Alterac Mountains, sealed under a great dome of violet energy raised by surviving mages. They are trying to rebuild. Progress is not visible.


                  
                  Sight, sound, smell 
                  
                

Sight — A shallow crater ringed by rubble, and over it a violet dome you can see from a day’s ride, humming faintly and enclosing nothing anyone can reach.
Sound — The dome, which makes a low tone people stop hearing after an hour and dream about afterwards. Otherwise wind over broken stone.
Smell — Cold ash, wet masonry, and a sharp ozone tang close to the barrier.


Related
Kirin Tor · Alterac Mountains · Archimonde · The Third War · Jaina Proudmoore · Khadgar · Guardians of Tirisfal

Places/Eastern-Kingdoms/Dark-Portal.title: Dark Portal
Places/Eastern-Kingdoms/Dark-Portal.content:
Dark Portal


                  
                  In a sentence 
                  
                

An arch of black stone forty feet high standing in a dead red waste, with nothing in it, humming.


Built by Medivh under Sargeras’s possession and Gul’dan on Draenor, opening in Year 0 and starting The First War.


                  
                  Sight, sound, smell 
                  
                

Sight — A stone frame the height of a keep standing in cracked red waste, lit from within, with the bones of two wars scattered around its feet.
Sound — A low tone felt in the teeth rather than heard, steady, never varying. Wind with grit in it.
Smell — Scorched rock and a dry burnt-metal smell that does not fade with distance.


Its History





























WhenWhatYear 0Opened. The orcish Horde invades.Year 8Destroyed by Khadgar at the end of The Second WarYear 17Reopened by Ner’zhul; the Alliance Expedition follows him throughYear 18Sealed from the Draenor side. Draenor shatters into Outland.NowDormant. Watched from Nethergarde Keep. Nothing has come through in years.

Places/Eastern-Kingdoms/Deadwind-Pass.title: Deadwind Pass
Places/Eastern-Kingdoms/Deadwind-Pass.content:
Deadwind Pass


                  
                  Arrival 
                  
                

A narrow canyon between two zones, entirely empty. No town, no camp, no quest-giver. Just a road, a ruined bridge, and a tower.


Continent: Eastern Kingdoms · Levels: 55–60 (tabletop 17–18) · Held by: Nobody. Nothing. Deliberately.
The emptiest zone in the game, and the most effective.
There is nothing here — no settlement, no faction, no reason to stop. Deadwind Pass exists to be the road between Duskwood and Swamp of Sorrows, and to have Karazhan in it.


                  
                  Sight, sound, smell 
                  
                

Sight — A gorge road with no settlement on it, ruined bridges, and a tower on the ridge that is visible from everywhere and approached by no one.
Sound — Wind funnelled through rock. Ravens. No traffic — this is a trade road with no trade on it.
Smell — Cold stone and dry rot. Nothing cooking, anywhere, because nobody lives here.

Places/Eastern-Kingdoms/Dun-Morogh.title: Dun Morogh
Places/Eastern-Kingdoms/Dun-Morogh.content:
Dun Morogh


                  
                  Arrival 
                  
                

Snow, pine, and the smell of forge-smoke on the wind. Then the mountain opens and there is a city inside it, and it is warm.


Continent: Eastern Kingdoms · Levels: 1–12 (tabletop 1–3) · Held by: Ironforge


                  
                  Dungeon 
                  
                

Gnomeregan (29–38 / tabletop 8–9)


The dwarven homeland, and one of the safest places in the world — with one enormous exception underneath it.
Also here: the Frostmane trolls, starving and displaced, holding Shimmer Ridge and Frostmane Hold. They were here before the dwarves.


                  
                  Sight, sound, smell 
                  
                

Sight — Snowfield and black pine, the Ironforge gate cut into the mountain, and steam venting from vents in the rock.
Sound — Wind. Boar in the drifts. Blasting from the quarry, and the constant low note of the mountain’s forges through the stone.
Smell — Cold air, pine, coal smoke, and hot metal near the gate.


Points of Interest

Places/Eastern-Kingdoms/Duskwood.title: Duskwood
Places/Eastern-Kingdoms/Duskwood.content:
Duskwood


                  
                  Arrival 
                  
                

There is no sun here. Not clouds — the light simply does not arrive. The trees are black, the road is the only safe ground, and something in the treeline is keeping pace with you.


Continent: Eastern Kingdoms · Levels: 20–30 (tabletop 5–7) · Held by: Nominally Stormwind. In practice, nothing living.
It was called Brightwood once. Then The Third War and a badly-handled summoning turned it into this.
The dead do not stay buried at Raven Hill. Worgen — the Nightbane — hunt the deep woods, released by a spell nobody will admit to casting. Ogres hold Vul’Gol. And the Kingdom of Stormwind, again, has sent nobody.
Darkshire survives on the Night Watch: exhausted volunteers who patrol until they can’t and are led by a commander who is very obviously past breaking.


                  
                  The gothic horror zone 
                  
                

Duskwood runs on personal tragedy rather than politics. Stalvan Mistmantle, the tutor whose obsession destroyed a family. Morbent Fel, the necromancer at the cemetery. Abercrombie, the hermit assembling a body out of parts. Mor’Ladim, a father raised as an undead monster looking for his daughter’s grave. Each is a self-contained short story and they are among the best-written quests in vanilla.




                  
                  Sight, sound, smell 
                  
                

Sight — Permanent dusk under a canopy that never thins, lanterns burning at midday, and headstones outnumbering houses in Darkshire.
Sound — No birds. Wolves that call and are answered from the wrong direction. The Night Watch’s bell, rung more nights than not.
Smell — Wet leaf-mould, cold stone, and tallow from the lanterns. Under it, faintly, something turned.

Places/Eastern-Kingdoms/Eastern-Plaguela.title: Eastern Plaguelands
Places/Eastern-Kingdoms/Eastern-Plaguela.content:
Eastern Plaguelands


                  
                  Arrival 
                  
                

The sky is red. Not sunset — permanently, structurally red. In the middle of a dead country there is one small chapel with the lights on, and it has never fallen.


Continent: Eastern Kingdoms · Levels: 53–60 (tabletop 16–18) · Held by: Scourge; Argent Dawn at Light’s Hope


                  
                  Dungeon 
                  
                

Stratholme (58–60 / tabletop 18)


The Scourge’s heartland on this continent, and the hardest zone in the Eastern Kingdoms.
Stratholme — the city Arthas Menethil culled with his own hands — is now split between Baron Rivendare’s undead and the Scarlet Crusade’s Bastion, both of whom hold half a burning ruin and neither of whom will leave.
Light’s Hope Chapel is the Argent Dawn’s seat: a small consecrated building the Scourge has attacked repeatedly and never taken. It is neutral ground for anyone who is bleeding.
Tirion Fordring lives alone in a hut in the eastern hills, exiled from the Order of the Silver Hand years ago for sparing an orc’s life, drinking, and refusing to be the man everyone needs him to be.


                  
                  Sight, sound, smell 
                  
                

Sight — Red-orange sky over dead ground, plague cauldrons steaming at crossroads, and Stratholme’s walls intact and lit.
Sound — Cauldrons bubbling. Bone-wagons on the roads. Somewhere always a bell, or something imitating one.
Smell — Rot, chemical sweetness from the cauldrons, and a cold mineral smell around the Scourge camps.


Points of Interest

Places/Eastern-Kingdoms/Elwynn-Forest.title: Elwynn Forest
Places/Eastern-Kingdoms/Elwynn-Forest.content:
Elwynn Forest


                  
                  Arrival 
                  
                

Oak and open farmland, a river you can hear before you see it, and the towers of Stormwind on the western horizon. It is the most peaceful place in the Eastern Kingdoms and it is one bad harvest from not being.


Continent: Eastern Kingdoms · Levels: 1–10 (tabletop 1–3) · Held by: Kingdom of Stormwind
Stormwind’s heartland, rebuilt after The First War and comfortable enough that its problems look small. They are not small — they are early.
Kobolds have taken the mines. Gnolls raid the logging camps from the Eastvale. And Defias Brotherhood agents move openly through Westbrook, recruiting from farms that can’t make their tithe, because the road west to Westfall is not guarded anymore.


                  
                  Sight, sound, smell 
                  
                

Sight — Oak and green meadow, tidy farms, a stone bridge at Goldshire, and Stormwind’s towers visible over the treeline to the north.
Sound — Birdsong, cart wheels, the Lion’s Pride’s common room through an open door. Kobold squabbling from the mine, if you go that way.
Smell — Cut hay, woodsmoke, horse, and bread from the Goldshire ovens.

Places/Eastern-Kingdoms/Gilneas.title: Gilneas
Places/Eastern-Kingdoms/Gilneas.content:
Gilneas


                  
                  In a sentence 
                  
                

A hundred feet of stone across an entire border, with a nation behind it that stopped answering letters decades ago.


A human kingdom on the peninsula south of Silverpine Forest, ruled by King Genn Greymane.
Greymane withdrew Gilneas from the Alliance during The Interbellum and built the Greymane Wall — a fortification sealing the entire land border. It has been closed ever since.


                  
                  Sight, sound, smell 
                  
                

Sight — A wall across an isthmus, taller than anything reasonable, with no gate open and no one visible on the parapet.
Sound — Sea on both sides. Wind. Nothing at all from beyond the wall, which is what people find hardest.
Smell — Salt and wet stone. Nothing cooking, nothing burning, no smoke on the far side.


Related
Silverpine Forest · The Interbellum · The Second War · Humans · The Alliance

Places/Eastern-Kingdoms/Grim-Batol.title: Grim Batol
Places/Eastern-Kingdoms/Grim-Batol.content:
Grim Batol


                  
                  In a sentence 
                  
                

A dwarven fortress-city carved into a mountain above the water, sealed shut, and nothing has come out of it in fifteen years. People do not sail close.


A Dark Iron fortress in the highlands above the Wetlands, abandoned by them and later used by the orcish Dragonmaw clan for the worst crime of The Second War.
Using the Demon Soul, the Dragonmaw enslaved Alexstrasza, the Aspect of Life, and chained her here — forcing her to breed her own children into war-mounts for the Horde. She was freed when the Demon Soul was destroyed. The fortress was sealed afterwards, and has stayed sealed.
This is not secret history. It was twenty years ago, both sides know it, and it is the single hardest thing for an orc to answer for.


                  
                  Sight, sound, smell 
                  
                

Sight — A fortress gate set into a dead-end valley, sealed and unmarked by weather, with nothing growing on the approach road.
Sound — Nothing. No wind reaches the valley floor and no birds cross it — the silence is the thing every account mentions first.
Smell — Cold dry stone, and underneath it something faintly metallic that visitors describe as the smell of old blood without being able to say why.


Related
Alexstrasza · Demon Soul · The Second War · Wetlands · Dragonmaw · Red Dragonflight · Dark Iron Dwarves

Places/Eastern-Kingdoms/Hillsbrad-Foothi.title: Hillsbrad Foothills
Places/Eastern-Kingdoms/Hillsbrad-Foothi.content:
Hillsbrad Foothills


                  
                  Arrival 
                  
                

Gentle farmland, apple orchards, and two towns twenty minutes apart that have been killing each other for four years over nothing either can articulate.


Continent: Eastern Kingdoms · Levels: 20–30 (tabletop 5–7) · Held by: Split — Southshore (Alliance) and Tarren Mill (Horde)
The Alliance–Horde cold war’s ugliest, most pointless front.
Southshore is a human fishing town. Tarren Mill is a Forsaken settlement. They are close enough to walk between, and the road between them is a killing ground. Neither side has an objective. Neither side can stop.
Durnholde Keep is here in ruins — where Thrall was raised in captivity by Aedelas Blackmoore, and from which he escaped to found the New Horde. It is now held by Syndicate and feral orcs. Thrall has never come back.


                  
                  Sight, sound, smell 
                  
                

Sight — Green farmland that still looks prosperous, Southshore’s fishing boats, and Tarren Mill’s smoke on the northern horizon.
Sound — Livestock, church bells at Southshore, and — most days — fighting somewhere between the two towns that nobody has declared.
Smell — Cut hay and sea air near the coast; closer to Tarren Mill, apothecary chemicals and something under them.

Places/Eastern-Kingdoms/Loch-Modan.title: Loch Modan
Places/Eastern-Kingdoms/Loch-Modan.content:
Loch Modan


                  
                  Arrival 
                  
                

A great lake in a bowl of hills, held back by a dam that is the finest piece of engineering in the Eastern Kingdoms — and there is a crack in it.


Continent: Eastern Kingdoms · Levels: 10–20 (tabletop 3–5) · Held by: Ironforge
Dwarven heartland: green, ordered, and prosperous in a way almost nowhere else on the continent manages.
The Stonewrought Dam holds the loch and is a genuine dwarven achievement. It has also been sabotaged by Dark Iron Dwarves, and the crack is spreading.
Ironband’s Excavation has hit troggs. The Mo’grosh ogres are pressing from the east. It is a comfortable zone with three problems that could all get much worse.


                  
                  Sight, sound, smell 
                  
                

Sight — A great green loch ringed by dwarven stonework, a broken dam leaking down the valley, and dig sites flagged in every direction.
Sound — Water through a breach nobody has patched. Blasting charges up at the quarry. Troggs in the rocks, always somewhere behind you.
Smell — Wet stone, cut pine, and blackpowder from the Explorers’ League camps.

Places/Eastern-Kingdoms/Lordaeron.title: Lordaeron
Places/Eastern-Kingdoms/Lordaeron.content:
Lordaeron


                  
                  In a sentence 
                  
                

The greatest human kingdom of the age. Present tense would be inaccurate.


The northern human kingdom, ruled by King Terenas Menethil II and the heart of the Alliance of Lordaeron in The Second War.
Beneath the ruined Capital City, the Forsaken built Undercity — and Sylvanas Windrunner made the entrance pass through the throne room where Terenas died.


                  
                  Everyone remembers it 
                  
                

Lordaeron fell four years ago. Half the human NPCs a party meets are Lordaeron refugees. Every Forsaken was a Lordaeron citizen.




                  
                  Sight, sound, smell 
                  
                

Sight — A capital with its walls largely intact and nothing living in it — gardens gone to seed, a throne room open to the sky, and a stain on the floor nobody has cleaned.
Sound — Wind through halls. Crows. Below ground, faintly, industry — because the city is not as empty as it looks.
Smell — Cold stone, rot, and a chemical sourness rising from beneath the ruins.


Related
The Third War · Arthas Menethil · Undercity · Forsaken · Scourge · Tirisfal Glades · Eastern Plaguelands · Western Plaguelands · Humans

Places/Eastern-Kingdoms/Menethil-Harbor.title: Menethil Harbor
Places/Eastern-Kingdoms/Menethil-Harbor.content:
Menethil Harbor


                  
                  In a sentence 
                  
                

A fortified port in a permanent drizzle, and the only way for most of the Alliance to reach Kalimdor.


The Alliance’s principal western port, in the Wetlands. Ships run from here to Auberdine in Darkshore and Theramore Isle in Dustwallow Marsh.
It is small, damp, constantly under low-grade threat from murlocs and Dark Iron Dwarves at Dun Modr, and absolutely essential — cut Menethil and the Alliance’s two continents come apart.


                  
                  Sight, sound, smell 
                  
                

Sight — A stone keep and a working quay in permanent drizzle, ships at anchor, and the marsh pressing right up to the walls.
Sound — Rain on water and slate. Rigging, gulls, the harbourmaster shouting. Murlocs on the mudflats after dark.
Smell — Wet rope, tar, fish, and bilge — the standard smell of a port that never gets to dry out.


Related
Wetlands · Theramore Isle · Darkshore · Ironforge · Travel and Downtime · The Alliance

Places/Eastern-Kingdoms/Nethergarde-Keep.title: Nethergarde Keep
Places/Eastern-Kingdoms/Nethergarde-Keep.content:
Nethergarde Keep


                  
                  In a sentence 
                  
                

A fortress built to watch a door, garrisoned by people who have been watching it for thirty years, and nothing has ever come through.


A Kirin Tor-founded fortress in the Blasted Lands, established after The Second War to watch the Dark Portal.
The garrison has been on station for a generation. They have never been rotated out. They are still watching.
Their supply line is currently unreliable, and Stormwind has not noticed.


                  
                  Sight, sound, smell 
                  
                

Sight — A Kirin Tor fortress on a ridge in dead red country, lights in every window, watching a hole in the world.
Sound — Wind and grit. Watch bells on rotation. Very little conversation — a garrison thirty years into a siege that never came.
Smell — Scorched rock, lamp oil, and a dry burnt-metal smell off the Portal on a bad day.


Related
Blasted Lands · Dark Portal · Kirin Tor · The Second War · The Alliance

Places/Eastern-Kingdoms/Quel'Thalas.title: Quel'Thalas
Places/Eastern-Kingdoms/Quel'Thalas.content:
Quel’Thalas


                  
                  In a sentence 
                  
                

A golden forest kingdom with a black scar cut straight through it, from the border to the heart, and nothing grows in the scar.


The High Elves’ kingdom, founded ~6,800 years before the Dark Portal by the Highborne exiled from Kalimdor. Its heart was the Sunwell, created from a stolen vial of the Well of Eternity.


                  
                  Sight, sound, smell 
                  
                

Sight — Gold forest under an unnaturally clear sky, and a scar cut straight through it — a dead corridor of blighted ground running to the north.
Sound — Wind in leaves either side of the scar. Nothing at all within it.
Smell — Warm resin and gold leaf-litter, cut across by cold rot along the dead swathe.


Now
The survivors are split: Blood Elves under Kael’thas Sunstrider went through the Dark Portal; a remnant of High Elves stayed with the Alliance.
Related
High Elves · Blood Elves · Sylvanas Windrunner · Arthas Menethil · Kel’Thuzad · Kael’thas Sunstrider · The Third War · Arcane Magic and the Well of Eternity

Places/Eastern-Kingdoms/Redridge-Mountai.title: Redridge Mountains
Places/Eastern-Kingdoms/Redridge-Mountai.content:
Redridge Mountains


                  
                  Arrival 
                  
                

Red stone, a long blue lake, and a bridge town that has been fortifying itself for two years because nobody is coming to help.


Continent: Eastern Kingdoms · Levels: 15–25 (tabletop 4–6) · Held by: Kingdom of Stormwind, barely
Lakeshire sits on Lake Everstill with a broken bridge, a nervous militia, and a mayor who has written to Stormwind eleven times.
To the east, the Blackrock orcs have taken Stonewatch Keep — a Stormwind fortress — and are massing in Render’s Valley. To the north, gnolls. To the south, more gnolls. The town is surrounded and the crown’s answer has been silence.


                  
                  Sight, sound, smell 
                  
                

Sight — Red rock, a long blue lake, and a bridge with a span missing that everyone steps around like a bad tooth.
Sound — Hammering from the militia’s barricades. Gnolls laughing somewhere upslope. Nothing at all from the east, which is worse.
Smell — Lake water, pine resin, and woodsmoke from a town burning more fires than it needs for warmth.

Places/Eastern-Kingdoms/Searing-Gorge.title: Searing Gorge
Places/Eastern-Kingdoms/Searing-Gorge.content:
Searing Gorge


                  
                  Arrival 
                  
                

A strip-mined wound in the earth, filled with slag and smoke and the noise of industry that never stops.


Continent: Eastern Kingdoms · Levels: 43–56 (tabletop 13–16) · Held by: Dark Iron Dwarves; Thorium Brotherhood at Thorium Point
The Dark Iron Dwarves’ open-cast operation — a whole zone converted into a mine and a furnace. The Cauldrons here are Twilight’s Hammer projects poisoning the land for reasons the Dark Iron do not care to investigate.
Thorium Point is the exception: the Thorium Brotherhood, Dark Iron defectors who rejected Ragnaros and just want to forge. They are neutral, they are the best smiths alive, and they are the only realistic source of fire-worked gear on the continent.
The Venture Company is also here at the Grimesilt Dig Site, because of course they are.


                  
                  Sight, sound, smell 
                  
                

Sight — Ash falling like slow snow, slag terraces, and a sky the colour of a bruise that never resolves into weather.
Sound — Industry — pumps, hammers, the deep intermittent boom of the Cauldrons. No birds and no insects.
Smell — Sulphur, hot iron, and burnt air that dries the back of your throat within a minute.

Places/Eastern-Kingdoms/Silverpine-Fores.title: Silverpine Forest
Places/Eastern-Kingdoms/Silverpine-Fores.content:
Silverpine Forest


                  
                  Arrival 
                  
                

Grey pines, permanent overcast, and a wall to the south that has been sealed for so long people have stopped wondering what’s behind it.


Continent: Eastern Kingdoms · Levels: 10–20 (tabletop 3–5) · Held by: Forsaken, contested


                  
                  Dungeon 
                  
                

Shadowfang Keep (22–30 / tabletop 5–7)


The Forsaken’s southern approach, and a zone where three separate problems overlap.
Shadowfang Keep stands above Pyrewood Village, where the archmage Arugal — driven mad after summoning worgen to fight the Scourge — now presides over a castle full of the things he called. The villagers of Pyrewood transform at nightfall.
Rot Hide gnolls have been deliberately infected with the plague by Scourge necromancers. Ambermill holds out as a Dalaran mage enclave. And to the south stands the Greymane Wall, behind which the kingdom of Gilneas sealed itself off decades ago and has not been heard from since.


                  
                  Sight, sound, smell 
                  
                

Sight — Dense grey-green pine in permanent overcast, abandoned farmsteads, and Shadowfang Keep on its ridge above Pyrewood.
Sound — Wolves — a great many, and organised. Wind in the pines. Pyrewood goes silent at dusk, all at once.
Smell — Wet pine, mould, and old woodsmoke from chimneys nobody is lighting.
