Places/Eastern-Kingdoms/Stormwind-Cathed.title: Stormwind Cathedral
Places/Eastern-Kingdoms/Stormwind-Cathed.content:
Stormwind Cathedral



                  
                  In a sentence 
                  
                

The largest building in the human world, built by masons who were never paid for it.


The Cathedral of Light in Cathedral Square, Stormwind City — the seat of the Church of the Holy Light under Archbishop Benedictus, and the human world’s spiritual centre.
Priests and paladins train here. The Order of the Silver Hand was headquartered here before Arthas disbanded it.


                  
                  The irony is structural 
                  
                

This building was raised by the Stonemasons’ Guild, who were then refused payment and became the Defias Brotherhood. Every service held here happens inside a monument to a debt the crown will not acknowledge.




                  
                  Sight, sound, smell 
                  
                

Sight — Pale stone rising above every roofline in the city, tall windows throwing coloured light across the floor, and scaffolding on the north face that has not moved in two years.
Sound — Bells on the hour. Footsteps carrying a very long way. Singing at the offices, thin now, because there are fewer voices than there were.
Smell — Cold stone, beeswax, incense, and damp wool from the people sheltering inside.


Related
Stormwind City · The Holy Light · Order of the Silver Hand · Defias Brotherhood · Kingdom of Stormwind · Humans

Places/Eastern-Kingdoms/Stranglethorn-Va.title: Stranglethorn Vale
Places/Eastern-Kingdoms/Stranglethorn-Va.content:
Stranglethorn Vale


                  
                  Arrival 
                  
                

Heat like a wet blanket. Panthers you hear once. Troll ruins swallowed by fig roots, and somewhere south of all of it, a pirate town where the war doesn’t apply.


Continent: Eastern Kingdoms · Levels: 30–45 (tabletop 8–11) · Held by: Contested — nobody, Steamwheedle Cartel in Booty Bay
A vast jungle covering the southern tip of the continent, and the closest thing to genuinely neutral ground on Azeroth.
The Gurubashi empire ruled here and left ziggurats everywhere. Its remnant is fractured: some tribes serve Hakkar the Soulflayer, others fight them. Zul’Gurub stands sealed in the north.
Booty Bay at the southern tip is the Steamwheedle Cartel’s crown jewel: a goblin port where Alliance and Horde drink at the same bar because Baron Revilgaz’s bruisers will throw anyone who fights into the sea.


                  
                  Sight, sound, smell 
                  
                

Sight — Canopy so thick the floor stays twilit, troll stonework swallowed by roots, and a goblin port at the southern tip painted in colours no jungle produces.
Sound — Insects at a volume that becomes weather. Tigers coughing. Drums from the Gurubashi ruins, which stop when you listen for them.
Smell — Wet rot, flowers past their turn, and — near Booty Bay — tar, fish and gunpowder.

Places/Eastern-Kingdoms/Stromgarde.title: Stromgarde
Places/Eastern-Kingdoms/Stromgarde.content:
Stromgarde


                  
                  In a sentence 
                  
                

A walled city on cliffs, held by a garrison fighting on three fronts, which was not invited back into the Alliance and has stopped asking.


The last surviving kingdom of Arathor, the original human empire, in the Arathi Highlands.
Prince Galen Trollbane commands what is left, fighting the Syndicate for the ruins of his own city and the Boulderfist ogres for everything outside it.
Stromgarde effectively left the Alliance after The Second War and its most famous son, Danath Trollbane, went through the Dark Portal with the Expedition and never returned.


                  
                  Sight, sound, smell 
                  
                

Sight — A great walled city with its gates broken, half of it held and half of it not, and banners still flying over towers with nobody in them.
Sound — Wind through empty streets. Fighting on three sides, most days. No market noise, because there is no market.
Smell — Old smoke, cold stone, and the particular staleness of a city with more buildings than people.


Related
Arathi Highlands · Syndicate · The Second War · Humans · The Invasion of Draenor · The Alliance

Places/Eastern-Kingdoms/Swamp-of-Sorrows.title: Swamp of Sorrows
Places/Eastern-Kingdoms/Swamp-of-Sorrows.content:
Swamp of Sorrows


                  
                  Arrival 
                  
                

Standing water that hasn’t moved in thirty years. The air tastes of iron. Everything here has been sick since the day the Portal opened.


Continent: Eastern Kingdoms · Levels: 35–45 (tabletop 9–11) · Held by: Contested — Horde at Stonard


                  
                  Dungeon 
                  
                

Sunken Temple (50–60 / tabletop 15–16)


The swamp was ordinary marshland until the Dark Portal opened next door and thirty years of fel energy soaked into the water table.
Stonard is an orcish outpost, one of the Horde’s few Eastern Kingdoms holdings — a Second War remnant that Thrall has kept. The Lost Ones — degenerate, broken draenei — huddle at Fallow Sanctuary, and nobody in 2004 knows what they used to be.


                  
                  Sight, sound, smell 
                  
                

Sight — Standing black water, drowned trees, and the temple’s broken roof breaking the surface of the lake like a wreck.
Sound — Frogs, flies, and the slow suck of mud. Occasionally, from the water, something much larger turning over.
Smell — Sulphur, stagnant water, and rotting vegetation. Near the Portal, a dry burnt-metal smell that does not belong here.

Places/Eastern-Kingdoms/The-Hinterlands.title: The Hinterlands
Places/Eastern-Kingdoms/The-Hinterlands.content:
The Hinterlands


                  
                  Arrival 
                  
                

Ancient hardwood forest on high ground, gryphons circling above the canopy, and troll drums somewhere south that do not stop at night.


Continent: Eastern Kingdoms · Levels: 40–50 (tabletop 12–14) · Held by: Contested — Wildhammer Clan, forest trolls
Highland forest held by the Wildhammer Clan from Aerie Peak, and contested by two forest troll tribes who were here first and say so loudly.
The Vilebranch hold Jintha’Alor, a terraced troll city built up a mountainside, where they are conducting sacrifices to something. The Witherbark press from the south.
Quel’Danil Lodge shelters High Elves — a rare visible remnant of a people who mostly left.
Seradane in the north is a green dragon portal to The Emerald Dream, guarded and increasingly troubled.


                  
                  Sight, sound, smell 
                  
                

Sight — Enormous old-growth pine, gryphon shapes over the crags, and troll terraces cut into hillsides centuries before anyone else arrived.
Sound — Wind in high branches, gryphon calls, and Vilebranch drums that carry further than they should.
Smell — Pine sap, cold rain, and woodsmoke from Aerie Peak.

Places/Eastern-Kingdoms/Tirisfal-Glades.title: Tirisfal Glades
Places/Eastern-Kingdoms/Tirisfal-Glades.content:
Tirisfal Glades


                  
                  Arrival 
                  
                

The sky here is the wrong colour — a sickly amber that never resolves into day or night. And on the northern horizon, a ruined palace, and beneath it, a city of the dead.


Continent: Eastern Kingdoms · Levels: 1–10 (tabletop 1–3) · Held by: Forsaken


                  
                  Dungeon 
                  
                

Scarlet Monastery (34–45 / tabletop 9–11)


The Forsaken homeland. What used to be Lordaeron’s fair northern province is now a blighted, amber-lit country where the crops have failed and the dead walk to work.
Undercity lies in the catacombs beneath the ruins of Lordaeron’s Capital City — directly under the throne room where Arthas Menethil murdered his father, which Sylvanas Windrunner chose deliberately.
The Scarlet Crusade holds the Scarlet Monastery to the east and considers every Forsaken an abomination. They are at war permanently.


                  
                  Sight, sound, smell 
                  
                

Sight — Sickly yellow-grey light through dead trees, tidy fields with nothing growing right, and the ruined spires of the old capital to the south.
Sound — Crows. Wind through bare branches. The occasional distant crack of Scarlet Crusade musketry.
Smell — Cold damp earth, rot under leaf-litter, and a chemical tang carrying up from Brill on the wrong wind.

Places/Eastern-Kingdoms/Western-Plaguela.title: Western Plaguelands
Places/Eastern-Kingdoms/Western-Plaguela.content:
Western Plaguelands


                  
                  Arrival 
                  
                

The grass is grey. The trees are grey. Everything here died standing up and was not permitted to fall over.


Continent: Eastern Kingdoms · Levels: 46–57 (tabletop 13–16) · Held by: Scourge, with Scarlet Crusade at Hearthglen


                  
                  Dungeon 
                  
                

Scholomance (58–60 / tabletop 18)


Where the plague began. Andorhal was the distribution point — Kel’Thuzad’s Cult of the Damned poisoned the grain here and shipped it across Lordaeron. The lich Araj the Summoner holds the ruins now.
Hearthglen to the north is Scarlet Crusade-held, commanded by Highlord Taelan Fordring — son of the disgraced paladin Tirion Fordring — who is a genuinely good man slowly realizing what he’s part of.
Caer Darrow in the south holds Scholomance, a necromantic academy in the old Barov crypts. It is recruiting, which is the part that frightens people.
Uther’s Tomb stands in Sorrow Hill. Tirion Fordring cannot bring himself to visit it.


                  
                  Sight, sound, smell 
                  
                

Sight — Grey grass, orchards in permanent blossom-rot, and farmhouses standing intact with the doors open.
Sound — Very little. Crows that do not call. Bells in Andorhal ringing on no schedule anyone has worked out.
Smell — Sweet decay — the specific smell of fruit gone over — laid across cold earth and old smoke.

Places/Eastern-Kingdoms/Westfall.title: Westfall
Places/Eastern-Kingdoms/Westfall.content:
Westfall


                  
                  Arrival 
                  
                

Dust. Abandoned farmhouses with the doors standing open. Scarecrows that turn out to be harvest golems, and harvest golems that turn out to be hostile. Somewhere out here the kingdom stopped.


Continent: Eastern Kingdoms · Levels: 10–20 (tabletop 3–5) · Held by: Defias Brotherhood — in practice


                  
                  Dungeon 
                  
                

The Deadmines (17–26 / tabletop 4–5)


Westfall was Stormwind’s breadbasket. Now the fields are dust, the farms are empty, and the crown has not sent soldiers in years.


                  
                  Sight, sound, smell 
                  
                

Sight — Wheat gone to seed in fields nobody has cut, windmills turning with nobody minding them, and red bandannas on the road at dusk.
Sound — Sail-arms creaking. Harvest golems clanking through the stubble on routes their dead owners set. Long silences where farm noise should be.
Smell — Dry grass, dust, and the sour smell of a grain store left too long. Nearer the coast, salt and murloc.

Places/Eastern-Kingdoms/Wetlands.title: Wetlands
Places/Eastern-Kingdoms/Wetlands.content:
Wetlands


                  
                  Arrival 
                  
                

It rains. It has been raining for as long as anyone can remember. Raptors call to each other across the fens and the road is the only thing not underwater.


Continent: Eastern Kingdoms · Levels: 20–30 (tabletop 5–7) · Held by: Contested — Alliance at Menethil, everything else feral
Marshland between the dwarven highlands and the northern coast. Menethil Harbor is the Alliance’s main port for Kalimdor and Theramore Isle, and it is the only reason anyone comes here.
Dun Modr to the north is a ruin held by Dark Iron Dwarves. Whelgar’s Excavation has been overrun by raptors. And to the northwest, across the water, stands Grim Batol — sealed, silent, and the site of one of the worst things that ever happened to a dragon.


                  
                  Grim Batol 
                  
                

Where the Horde chained Alexstrasza with the Demon Soul during The Second War and bred her children into war-mounts. She is free now. The fortress is sealed and nobody goes near it. It is inaccessible at launch and it should stay that way — it’s a piece of dread, not a dungeon.




                  
                  Sight, sound, smell 
                  
                

Sight — Standing water everywhere, mud roads on causeways, raptor tracks in the silt, and the shipwreck coast north of Menethil.
Sound — Rain on water. Frogs by the thousand. Raptors calling across the marsh, which is the sound that stops conversation.
Smell — Brackish water, rot, tar from the harbour, and wet rope.

Places/Kalimdor/Ashenvale.title: Ashenvale
Places/Kalimdor/Ashenvale.content:
Ashenvale


                  
                  Arrival 
                  
                

Old forest, blue-green light, and the sound of axes. Not woodcutting axes. Well — yes, woodcutting axes. That’s the problem.


Continent: Kalimdor · Levels: 18–30 (tabletop 5–7) · Held by: Contested — Night Elves vs. Warsong Horde


                  
                  Dungeon 
                  
                

Blackfathom Deeps (24–32 / tabletop 6–7)


The night elves’ ancestral forest, and the hottest front of the faction war — because the Horde is logging it.
The Warsong Outriders cut timber at the Warsong Lumber Camp to build Orgrimmar. The Silverwing Sentinels kill them for it. Neither Thrall nor Tyrande Whisperwind has been able or willing to stop it.


                  
                  Demon Fall Canyon 
                  
                

This is where Grom Hellscream killed Mannoroth and broke the orcish blood curse forever — dying in the act. It is the single most sacred site in orcish history and it is in night elf territory, which neither side has worked out how to handle.


Also here: Blackfathom Deeps on the coast, a sunken temple of Elune now occupied by naga and the Twilight’s Hammer, who serve a thing called Aku’mai.


                  
                  Sight, sound, smell 
                  
                

Sight — Blue-black forest under permanent half-light, moonwells glowing in clearings, and clear-cut scars widening on the eastern edge.
Sound — Wind in old canopy. Sentinel horns answering each other. From the east, axes and Warsong drums, which carry a long way in still air.
Smell — Cedar and wet moss. Where the logging is, cut sap and engine oil.

Places/Kalimdor/Azshara.title: Azshara
Places/Kalimdor/Azshara.content:
Azshara


                  
                  Arrival 
                  
                

Overgrown terraces and broken marble columns descending to a coast of blue coves, and in the water, things with too many arms watching you walk past.


Continent: Kalimdor · Levels: 45–55 (tabletop 13–16) · Held by: Nobody — naga, satyrs, and a small Horde outpost
The far north-east: the overgrown outskirts of the ancient Highborne capital, named for the queen who destroyed it.
Naga have returned to these coasts in force — the drowned descendants of Queen Azshara’s court, coming home after ten thousand years. Nobody knows why now.
Satyrs hold the Legash Encampment. Blue dragonkin are at the Bay of Storms. And Duke Hydraxis of the Hydraxian Waterlords holds a stretch of coast, offering an alliance to anyone willing to fight Ragnaros.


                  
                  Ruins with names 
                  
                

Eldarath, the Ruins of Arkkoran, the Ravencrest Monument — this is pre-Sundering kaldorei architecture, and it is the largest concentration of it anywhere accessible. Night elf PCs are walking through their own lost empire.




                  
                  Sight, sound, smell 
                  
                

Sight — Gold and violet forest on cliffs above the sea, ruined highborne terraces sliding into the water, and naga on every beach.
Sound — Surf on rock, constantly. Wind. Occasionally, from offshore, something singing — which everyone agrees they have heard and nobody discusses.
Smell — Salt, kelp rot, and a cold mineral smell near the ruins that does not belong to the sea.

Places/Kalimdor/Cenarion-Hold.title: Cenarion Hold
Places/Kalimdor/Cenarion-Hold.content:
Cenarion Hold


                  
                  In a sentence 
                  
                

A fortified druid outpost in the ash desert, staring at a wall that has held for a thousand years.


The Cenarion Circle’s forward base in Silithus, from which they monitor the Scarab Wall, the Silithid hives, and the Twilight’s Hammer excavation.


                  
                  Sight, sound, smell 
                  
                

Sight — A walled druidic outpost of grown timber and stone, incongruously green, planted in rust-coloured waste.
Sound — Wind carrying grit against the palisade. Chanting at set hours. Beneath everything, faint chitinous clicking from underground.
Smell — Dust and chitin outside; cut herbs, water and living wood within the walls.

Places/Kalimdor/Darkshore.title: Darkshore
Places/Kalimdor/Darkshore.content:
Darkshore


                  
                  Arrival 
                  
                

Grey surf, driftwood, and the bones of something enormous half-buried in the sand — and someone has built a shrine inside its ribcage.


Continent: Kalimdor · Levels: 10–20 (tabletop 3–5) · Held by: Night Elves, contested
A storm-battered coast scattered with the ruins of the pre-Sundering Kaldorei empire. Ameth’Aran and Bashal’Aran are ten thousand years old and full of restless night elf spirits.
Auberdine is the port and the only real settlement.


                  
                  Sight, sound, smell 
                  
                

Sight — Grey beach and drowned ruins, huge fallen trees, and the wrecks of ships along a coast that eats them.
Sound — Surf, constantly. Wind off the water. Furbolg somewhere inland, and gulls that sound wrong.
Smell — Salt, kelp, wet rot, and cold sand.

Places/Kalimdor/Desolace.title: Desolace
Places/Kalimdor/Desolace.content:
Desolace


                  
                  Arrival 
                  
                

Grey scrub, bleached bone, and a coastline of black sand. The name is not poetic. It is a description.


Continent: Kalimdor · Levels: 30–40 (tabletop 8–10) · Held by: Nobody — Centaur khanates at war


                  
                  Dungeon 
                  
                

Maraudon (46–55 / tabletop 14–15)


The most barren land on Kalimdor, and it did not used to be. Something killed it.
Five Centaur khanates fight each other across it; only the Gelkis Clan and Magram Clan will deal with outsiders, and only against each other.
The Kodo Graveyard is where the great beasts go to die, and something there is not letting them.


                  
                  Sight, sound, smell 
                  
                

Sight — Grey scrub over cracked ground, centaur camps on every rise, and the bones of something enormous half-buried in the middle distance.
Sound — Wind, and hooves — always hooves, somewhere, moving. Very little else.
Smell — Dust, dry dung from the centaur herds, and a faint sourness off the ground itself.

Places/Kalimdor/Durotar.title: Durotar
Places/Kalimdor/Durotar.content:
Durotar


                  
                  Arrival 
                  
                

Red rock, hard sun, and canyons that funnel a wind full of grit. And built into the largest canyon, a city of timber and iron that was not here five years ago.


Continent: Kalimdor · Levels: 1–10 (tabletop 1–3) · Held by: The Horde


                  
                  Dungeon 
                  
                

Ragefire Chasm (13–18 / tabletop 3–4) — beneath Orgrimmar


Thrall chose this land because nobody else wanted it. It is arid, it is hostile, and it is theirs — no prior claim, no displaced people, nobody to owe.
Orgrimmar is raw and new and enormous. Razor Hill and Sen’jin Village are the outposts.
The Echo Isles off the coast belong to the Darkspear Trolls and are held by Zalazane, a witch doctor who went mad and enthralled his own tribe.
Tiragarde Keep on the coast is full of shipwrecked Kul Tiran marines — survivors of Daelin Proudmoore’s fleet, still fighting a war that ended three years ago.


                  
                  Sight, sound, smell 
                  
                

Sight — Red rock and hardpan, sparse thorn scrub, and a canyon city of raw timber and iron in the middle distance.
Sound — Wind and grit. Scorpid and raptor. Drums and hammering from Orgrimmar, audible for miles.
Smell — Hot dust, dry vegetation, woodsmoke, and hot metal.

Places/Kalimdor/Dustwallow-Marsh.title: Dustwallow Marsh
Places/Kalimdor/Dustwallow-Marsh.content:
Dustwallow Marsh


                  
                  Arrival 
                  
                

Waist-deep water, hanging moss, and mosquitoes. To the east, a human city on an island. To the south, a bog where nothing goes, and something very large is sleeping under it.


Continent: Kalimdor · Levels: 35–45 (tabletop 9–11) · Held by: Split — Theramore, Horde, ogres, and a dragon


                  
                  Dungeon 
                  
                

Onyxia’s Lair (60 raid / tabletop 19–20) — uncleared


A hot southern marsh containing two of the most important things on Kalimdor.
Theramore Isle is Jaina Proudmoore’s human city — the Alliance’s foothold on the Horde’s continent, and the only functioning diplomatic channel between the factions. It exists because she and Thrall both decided it should, and it cost her her father.
Brackenwall Village is an ogre settlement allied to the Horde, which is exactly as strange as it sounds and entirely canonical.


                  
                  Sight, sound, smell 
                  
                

Sight — Grey standing water and drowned trees, a walled human city flying blue on an island, and dragonkin circling a bog to the south.
Sound — Insects. Bog gas surfacing. Theramore’s harbour bell, and further off, wingbeats too large to be birds.
Smell — Rotting reed and sulphur, cut with salt and tar near the city walls.

Places/Kalimdor/Felwood.title: Felwood
Places/Kalimdor/Felwood.content:
Felwood


                  
                  Arrival 
                  
                

The trees are green. Not leaf-green — a sick, luminous, wrong green, and it comes off on your hands. Nothing here smells like a forest should.


Continent: Kalimdor · Levels: 48–55 (tabletop 14–16) · Held by: Nobody — corruption, satyrs, and the Shadow Council
Formerly a healthy part of Ashenvale. Then Archimonde died at Mount Hyjal just north of here and the demonic residue soaked into everything.
Jaedenar — the Shadow Council’s major stronghold — sits beneath Shatter Scar Vale, where satyrs and warlocks work at something ongoing.
The Deadwood and Winterfall Furbolg have been corrupted. The Timbermaw Hold furbolg have not, and hold the tunnels, and do not trust anyone.
The Cenarion Circle maintains Emerald Sanctuaries — small, embattled outposts trying to cleanse the ground a few square yards at a time.


                  
                  Sight, sound, smell 
                  
                

Sight — Trees the colour of old bruises, ground slick with green residue, and corruption that stops at a visible line where the Circle has been working.
Sound — Almost nothing alive. Wind that carries no birdsong. Furbolg somewhere, in distress rather than in threat.
Smell — Chemical sweetness over rot — the specific wrongness of a forest being poisoned rather than dying.

Places/Kalimdor/Feralas.title: Feralas
Places/Kalimdor/Feralas.content:
Feralas


                  
                  Arrival 
                  
                

Rainforest that has never been cut. Ancient trees, hanging vines, and two mountains on the western coast so tall they hold up the weather.


Continent: Kalimdor · Levels: 40–50 (tabletop 12–14) · Held by: Contested — night elves, Horde, ogres, and something older
Kalimdor’s great southern jungle, and the last place the old Kaldorei empire’s outer provinces survive.
Feathermoon Stronghold is Sentinel-held, commanded by Shandris Feathermoon, Tyrande Whisperwind’s adopted daughter and the finest soldier the night elves have. Camp Mojache is the Horde’s answer.
The Gordunni ogres hold the ruins of Eldre’Thalas — a Highborne city where the Shen’dralar, arcane-addicted night elf survivors, have been hiding for ten thousand years.


                  
                  Sight, sound, smell 
                  
                

Sight — Enormous rainforest with light coming down in shafts, high elf ruins under moss, and ogre banners on ancient towers.
Sound — Constant water — rain, or runoff, or both. Birds in the canopy. Ogres, once you are close enough that it matters.
Smell — Wet green growth, flowering vines, and old wet stone.

Places/Kalimdor/Gadgetzan.title: Gadgetzan
Places/Kalimdor/Gadgetzan.content:
Gadgetzan


                  
                  In a sentence 
                  
                

A walled goblin town in the middle of a desert, selling water at prices that would be criminal anywhere with a government.


The Steamwheedle Cartel’s Tanaris holding. Neutral, expensive, and the only reliable source of water, supplies, and transport in the southern desert.
Same rule as Booty Bay: no fighting in town. The bruisers are just as serious about it.
Useful for: reaching Zul’Farrak, Un’Goro Crater, and Silithus; hiring mercenaries; buying things that are not legal elsewhere.


                  
                  Sight, sound, smell 
                  
                

Sight — A walled goblin town shimmering in heat, corrugated iron and scaffolding, with an airfield full of things that should not fly.
Sound — Engines being run up. Auction chatter. Wind moving sand against the walls, constantly.
Smell — Hot metal, engine oil, dust, and spiced food frying somewhere.


Related
Steamwheedle Cartel · Tanaris · Goblins · Zul’Farrak · Silithus · Un’Goro Crater

Places/Kalimdor/Jaedenar.title: Jaedenar
Places/Kalimdor/Jaedenar.content:
Jaedenar


                  
                  In a sentence 
                  
                

A town in a poisoned forest, built by a demon cult, named after a demon, and operating openly because nobody has the strength to stop it.


The Shadow Council’s principal stronghold on Azeroth, beneath Shatter Scar Vale in Felwood — named for Kil’jaeden.
Satyrs, warlocks, and summoned demons work here on something that has been running for four years, since Archimonde died at Mount Hyjal just north and the fel residue soaked into the ground.


                  
                  Sight, sound, smell 
                  
                

Sight — An actual town with streets and lit windows, built in a poisoned forest by people who were not hiding.
Sound — Work — carts, hammering, orders being given. It sounds like any other town, which is the unsettling part.
Smell — Chemical sweetness over rot, woodsmoke, and something rendered.


Related
Shadow Council · Felwood · Satyr · The Burning Legion · Kil’jaeden · Cenarion Circle · Timbermaw Hold

Places/Kalimdor/Moonglade.title: Moonglade
Places/Kalimdor/Moonglade.content:
Moonglade


                  
                  Arrival 
                  
                

A perfect valley. Still water, silver light, and a silence that is not empty but attentive. Alliance and Horde druids pass each other on the path and nod.


Continent: Kalimdor · Levels: 55 (tabletop 17) · Held by: Cenarion Circle — neutral, inviolate
The Cenarion Circle’s seat, and the best neutral ground in the setting.
Druids of both factions train, sleep, and argue here, and the peace is absolute — not enforced by guards but by the fact that nobody who reaches Moonglade wants to break it.
Nighthaven is the settlement. Lake Elune’ara is the centre. The Stormrage Barrow Dens hold sleeping druids, including Malfurion Stormrage — whose body lies here while his spirit is trapped in The Emerald Dream.
Fandral Staghelm presides in his absence, and does not appear to be looking very hard.


                  
                  Sight, sound, smell 
                  
                

Sight — A high sheltered valley of silver birch and still water, untouched by any war, with a great moonwell at its centre.
Sound — Water, wind in leaves, and long silences. The quietest inhabited place on either continent.
Smell — Clean water, cut grass, night-blooming flowers. No smoke, anywhere.

None. That is the point.

Places/Kalimdor/Mount-Hyjal.title: Mount Hyjal
Places/Kalimdor/Mount-Hyjal.content:
Mount Hyjal


                  
                  In a sentence 
                  
                

The mountain where the world was saved, four years ago, and nobody has been allowed back up since.


The highest peak in Kalimdor, holding a second Well of Eternity and the World Tree Nordrassil grown over it. How that second Well came to be is something the kaldorei do not discuss with outsiders.


                  
                  The Battle of Mount Hyjal 
                  
                

The climax of The Third War. Humans under Jaina Proudmoore, orcs under Thrall, and night elves under Tyrande Whisperwind and Malfurion Stormrage fought together — the only time in history — to hold the mountain against Archimonde.
They lost the battle and won the war: Nordrassil’s power was detonated as Archimonde reached it, destroying him utterly.
The night elves lost their immortality. That was the price and they paid it knowingly.




                  
                  Sight, sound, smell 
                  
                

Sight — A peak above the cloud line, the slopes below it scarred and regrowing unevenly, and a treeline that stops where the fighting stopped.
Sound — Wind at altitude. Sentinel horns on the approaches. Nothing from the summit.
Smell — Cold thin air, pine, and burnt ground that four years of rain has not finished washing out.


Now
Nordrassil is damaged. The mountain is inaccessible — closed off and guarded, and the kaldorei turn back anyone who climbs. It is the founding memory of the present era, and everyone old enough to remember it, does.
Related
The Third War · Nordrassil · Archimonde · Night Elves · Thrall · Jaina Proudmoore · Tyrande Whisperwind · Illidan Stormrage · The Four Years After

Places/Kalimdor/Mulgore.title: Mulgore
Places/Kalimdor/Mulgore.content:
Mulgore


                  
                  Arrival 
                  
                

Golden grassland under an enormous sky, herds of kodo moving slowly across it, and four mesas rising out of the plain with rope bridges strung between them.


Continent: Kalimdor · Levels: 1–10 (tabletop 1–3) · Held by: Tauren / Thunder Bluff
The tauren homeland — and it has only been the tauren homeland for four years.
They were nomads hunted across the Barrens by Centaur until Thrall’s orcs helped Cairne Bloodhoof drive them off. Mulgore is what they settled, and Thunder Bluff on its mesas is the most peaceful capital in the world.
The Venture Company is already trying to mine it, which the tauren regard as roughly equivalent to grave-robbing.


                  
                  Sight, sound, smell 
                  
                

Sight — Gold grassland to every horizon, four mesas rising out of it, and kodo herds moving slowly across the middle distance.
Sound — Wind through long grass. Wind chimes and drums from the bluffs. Kodo bells. Almost nothing else.
Smell — Sun-warmed grass, kodo, drying hides, and woodsmoke from cooking fires.

Places/Kalimdor/Nordrassil.title: Nordrassil
Places/Kalimdor/Nordrassil.content:
Nordrassil


                  
                  In a sentence 
                  
                

The first World Tree, grown over a stolen well by three dragons, and it is not what it was.


The original World Tree, grown by the Dragon Aspects atop Mount Hyjal over the second Well of Eternity that Illidan Stormrage created.
It granted the Night Elves immortality and bound them to guard it. That bargain held for ten thousand years.
Fandral Staghelm grew Teldrassil as a replacement.


                  
                  Sight, sound, smell 
                  
                

Sight — A World Tree the size of a mountain range, damaged — bark scorched in a band around the trunk, whole limbs dead and still standing.
Sound — Wind at enormous scale through leaves. Water. Almost nothing else; the kaldorei who tend it work quietly.
Smell — Green sap, wet bark, and old char where the fire reached.


Related
Mount Hyjal · Night Elves · Teldrassil · The Dragon Aspects · The Sundering · Fandral Staghelm · The Third War

Places/Kalimdor/Northrend.title: Northrend
Places/Kalimdor/Northrend.content:
Northrend


                  
                  In a sentence 
                  
                

A frozen continent at the top of the world with a citadel on it, and everything wrong with the present age started there.


The frozen northern continent. Arthas Menethil sailed here, burned his ships, took up Frostmourne, and lost his soul. Ner’zhul crashed here as the Lich King and was frozen into the Icecrown Glacier.
Also here: Ulduar (a Titan complex, rumored only), the Nexus (Malygos’s seat), the Frozen Throne, and Naxxramas — which is still hovering here, not over the Plaguelands.


                  
                  Sight, sound, smell 
                  
                

Sight — A white coastline seen from the deck of a ship that will not put in, ice shelf to the horizon, and something built on the highest point that is too regular to be rock.
Sound — Wind off ice. Pack ice grinding. Sailors report a sound from inland they decline to describe twice.
Smell — Cold, salt, and nothing else — no smoke, no vegetation, no animal.


Related
The Lich King · Arthas Menethil · Ner’zhul · Scourge · Naxxramas · Kel’Thuzad · Malygos · Ulduar

Places/Kalimdor/Silithus.title: Silithus
Places/Kalimdor/Silithus.content:
Silithus


                  
                  Arrival 
                  
                

Ash-coloured sand, a permanent low wind, and dune after dune of nothing. Then, on the southern horizon, a wall — and it is not a natural formation.


Continent: Kalimdor · Levels: 55–60 (tabletop 17–18) · Held by: Nobody — Twilight’s Hammer and the Silithid
The southernmost desert, and the site of the campaign’s slowest apocalypse.
Nothing has happened yet. The gates are shut. That is the entire tension.


                  
                  Sight, sound, smell 
                  
                

Sight — Flat rust-coloured waste under a bleached sky, silithid mounds pushing up through the crust, and a wall on the southern horizon.
Sound — Wind carrying grit. Underneath it, a chitinous clicking from below ground that never entirely stops.
Smell — Dry dust, chitin, and a faint acrid sweetness on the wind from the direction of the wall.

Places/Kalimdor/Stonetalon-Mountains.title: Stonetalon Mountains
Places/Kalimdor/Stonetalon-Mountains.content:
Stonetalon Mountains


                  
                  Arrival 
                  
                

Terraced peaks and hanging valleys, and in the middle of it a canyon full of stumps and machinery where a forest used to be.


Continent: Kalimdor · Levels: 15–27 (tabletop 4–6) · Held by: Contested — and the Venture Company is winning
Highlands between Ashenvale and the Barrens, being actively destroyed by the Venture Company at Windshear Crag — clear-cutting on an industrial scale, with goblin machinery, for profit.
Night elves at Stonetalon Peak and Horde at Sun Rock Retreat both object, which makes this one of the few places both factions have a shared enemy and occasionally admit it.
The Charred Vale to the south was burned during the Third War and has never recovered.


                  
                  Sight, sound, smell 
                  
                

Sight — Terraced peaks, dying pine on the lower slopes, and goblin cutting operations working around the clock in the valleys.
Sound — Saws. Constant, from three directions. Harpies above the ridgelines, and the occasional crack of a whole tree going over.
Smell — Cut pine and sawdust laid over engine smoke. Higher up, clean cold air and the difference is startling.

Places/Kalimdor/Tanaris.title: Tanaris
Places/Kalimdor/Tanaris.content:
Tanaris


                  
                  Arrival 
                  
                

Heat that bends the air. Dunes to the south, a wrecked coastline to the north, and a walled goblin town in the middle charging for water.


Continent: Kalimdor · Levels: 40–50 (tabletop 12–14) · Held by: Steamwheedle Cartel at Gadgetzan; Sandfury trolls


                  
                  Dungeon 
                  
                

Zul’Farrak (44–54 / tabletop 13–14)


A vast desert. Gadgetzan is the Steamwheedle Cartel’s neutral town, and it makes its money selling water at rates that would be criminal anywhere with a government.
Zul’Farrak is the Sandfury troll city. They sacrifice at a great step-pyramid, and caravan drivers who camp within earshot say the tribe is keeping something alive down there.
The Wastewander bandits hold the Abyssal Sands. The Gaping Chasm in the south is a silithid hive — one of several, and they are connected to Ahn’Qiraj.


                  
                  Sight, sound, smell 
                  
                

Sight — White dune and hardpan under a hard sky, a goblin port shimmering in heat haze, and a step-pyramid on the eastern horizon.
Sound — Wind moving sand. Very little else in daylight. After dark, drums from Zul’Farrak that carry across the whole basin.
Smell — Hot dry dust, salt from the coast, and engine oil and cooking grease in Gadgetzan.

Places/Kalimdor/Teldrassil.title: Teldrassil
Places/Kalimdor/Teldrassil.content:
Teldrassil


                  
                  Arrival 
                  
                

Violet leaves the size of sails, moss underfoot, and everything lit as though by moonlight even at midday. You are standing in a tree that is also a country.


Continent: Kalimdor · Levels: 1–10 (tabletop 1–3) · Held by: Darnassus / Night Elves
The second World Tree, grown by Fandral Staghelm four years ago in an attempt to restore what was lost at Mount Hyjal — night elf immortality.


                  
                  Sight, sound, smell 
                  
                

Sight — A whole landscape growing in the branches of one tree — violet leaf-litter, glowing motes in the air, and no horizon that is not canopy.
Sound — Wind through leaves at an enormous scale. Water. Owls. Nothing mechanical anywhere.
Smell — Green sap, night-blooming flowers, and clean water.

Places/Kalimdor/The-Barrens.title: The Barrens
Places/Kalimdor/The-Barrens.content:
The Barrens


                  
                  Arrival 
                  
                

Yellow grass to the horizon in every direction, scattered acacia, and a road. The road goes on for a very long time.


Continent: Kalimdor · Levels: 10–25 (tabletop 3–6) · Held by: The Horde, loosely


                  
                  Dungeon 
                  
                

Wailing Caverns (17–24 / tabletop 4–5) · Razorfen Kraul (30–40 / 8–9) · Razorfen Downs (37–46 / 10–11)


Kalimdor’s spine — an enormous savanna that connects everything and is bigger than it has any right to be.
The Crossroads is the Horde’s central waypoint and the most attacked settlement in the world, because it sits at the junction every Alliance raiding party passes through.
Ratchet on the east coast is a neutral Steamwheedle Cartel port — the gateway between Kalimdor and Booty Bay.
Northwatch Hold in the south is a Theramore garrison whose aggression Jaina Proudmoore does not fully control.
Beneath it all: Wailing Caverns.


                  
                  Sight, sound, smell 
                  
                

Sight — Flat dry savannah, widely spaced acacia, and a road running through it that you can see for a very long way in both directions.
Sound — Wind. Zhevra and plainstrider. Quilboar somewhere in the thickets, and caravan wheels long before you see the caravan.
Smell — Dust, dry grass, animal dung on the road, and woodsmoke from the Crossroads.

Places/Kalimdor/Theramore-Isle.title: Theramore Isle
Places/Kalimdor/Theramore-Isle.content:
Theramore Isle



                  
                  In a sentence 
                  
                

A walled human city on an island in a Kalimdor swamp, flying Alliance colours a day’s sail from Orgrimmar, and somehow still standing.


Founded by Jaina Proudmoore from the refugees she led west during The Third War on Medivh’s warning. It sits in Dustwallow Marsh and exists because Jaina and Thrall both decided it should.


                  
                  Sight, sound, smell 
                  
                

Sight — A compact walled city on a marsh island — blue banners, a lighthouse, and a mage tower taller than anything for fifty miles.
Sound — Harbour bell, gulls, drill on the walls. Marsh insects beyond them. Quieter than a city this size should be.
Smell — Salt and tar, marsh rot past the walls, and lamp oil in the tower district.


Sites
Foothold Citadel (Jaina’s tower) · the docks (ships to Menethil Harbor) · the barracks · Northwatch Hold in the southern Barrens, a Theramore garrison whose aggression Jaina does not fully control

Places/Kalimdor/Thousand-Needles.title: Thousand Needles
Places/Kalimdor/Thousand-Needles.content:
Thousand Needles


                  
                  Arrival 
                  
                

A maze of red rock spires rising hundreds of feet out of a dry canyon floor, with rope bridges strung between them and a salt flat glittering at the eastern end.


Continent: Kalimdor · Levels: 25–35 (tabletop 6–8) · Held by: Contested — tauren, centaur, goblins
Mesa country. Freewind Post sits on top of a pillar and is reachable only by the Great Lift, a tauren-built elevator that is the zone’s defining landmark.
The Galak centaur contest the canyon floor. Highperch in the north is wyvern territory.
To the east, the Shimmering Flats — a salt pan where the goblins of the Mirage Raceway hold rocket-car races, because two rival cartels decided the best way to settle a business dispute was motorsport. It is the single silliest thing in vanilla and it is wonderful.


                  
                  Sight, sound, smell 
                  
                

Sight — Red rock spires with sheer sides, rope bridges strung between them, and a dry seabed floor a thousand feet below.
Sound — Wind through the columns, which sounds like several people humming out of tune. Kodo bells. Racing engines from Mirage Raceway.
Smell — Hot dry stone, kodo, and engine exhaust where the goblins have set up.

Ulduar


                  
                  In a sentence 
                  
                

A Titan complex in Northrend that nobody has reached, mentioned in fragments recovered from another Titan complex that nobody understands.


A Titan installation in Northrend, referenced obliquely in records recovered from Uldaman by the Explorers’ League.


                  
                  Sight, sound, smell 
                  
                

Sight — Referenced, never seen. The recovered plates depict a walled complex on a scale that makes Uldaman look like an outbuilding.

Places/Kalimdor/Un'Goro-Crater.title: Un'Goro Crater
Places/Kalimdor/Un'Goro-Crater.content:
Un’Goro Crater


                  
                  Arrival 
                  
                

You come over the crater rim and the temperature jumps twenty degrees. Below you is jungle — real, primeval, steaming jungle — with a volcano in the middle of it and something very large moving through the canopy.


Continent: Kalimdor · Levels: 48–55 (tabletop 14–16) · Held by: Nobody. It has never been settled.
A vast volcanic crater containing an intact prehistoric ecosystem. Devilsaurs. Diemetradons. Things that should have died out with the Titans and evidently did not, because the Titans kept them.


                  
                  It is a terrarium 
                  
                

Un’Goro is Titan machinery. Six elemental pylons ring the crater, still functioning, still doing something. The Explorers’ League at Marshal’s Refuge is trying to work out what. The crystals scattered across the crater floor are part of the mechanism.


The Slithering Scar in the south is a Silithid hive, which is the crater’s genuine problem — and it links to Silithus.


                  
                  Sight, sound, smell 
                  
                

Sight — A ringwall of cliffs enclosing dense green jungle, geysers venting white, and animals that should not exist walking around in daylight.
Sound — Steam. Insects at volume. Something very large moving through undergrowth, regularly, in the middle distance.
Smell — Wet heat, sulphur from the vents, crushed vegetation, and a heavy animal musk.

Places/Kalimdor/Winterspring.title: Winterspring
Places/Kalimdor/Winterspring.content:
Winterspring


                  
                  Arrival 
                  
                

Snow, black pines, and a silence so complete you can hear your own pulse. Then, somewhere in the trees, a frostsaber coughs.


Continent: Kalimdor · Levels: 55–60 (tabletop 17–18) · Held by: Nobody — Steamwheedle Cartel at Everlook
High alpine forest in Kalimdor’s north-east. Everlook is the Steamwheedle Cartel’s coldest and most expensive town.
Mazthoril is a Blue Dragonflight cave — one of the few places blue dragons are visible in the world, and they are not friendly, because Malygos has been insane for ten thousand years and nobody is minding the flight.
The Winterfall Furbolg are corrupted, drinking something the Timbermaw Hold furbolg want stopped. Darkwhisper Gorge in the south-east is a demon encampment. And the frostsaber pride at Frostsaber Rock can, with enormous patience, be befriended.


                  
                  Sight, sound, smell 
                  
                

Sight — Deep snow under black pine, ice caves lit blue from inside, and a goblin town with its lights on in the middle of nowhere.
Sound — Snow deadening everything. Wind at altitude. Frostsabers calling, which sounds close and is not.
Smell — Cold — which has its own smell — plus pine, woodsmoke from Everlook, and hot machine oil.

Player-Primer-—-Azeroth-in-Year-29.title: Player Primer — Azeroth in Year 29
Player-Primer-—-Azeroth-in-Year-29.content:
Player Primer — Azeroth in Year 29


                  
                  Safe to share 
                  
                

This is the only document in the vault written for players. Send it before session zero. It contains no secrets, no twists, and nothing a character wouldn’t plausibly know. Everything genuinely hidden has been left out on purpose.



What This Is
A Dungeons & Dragons campaign set in the world of Warcraft — specifically, Azeroth as it stood in 2004, at the moment the original game began. Not the version from the last twenty years of expansions. The early one, when the map was smaller and almost nothing had been settled yet.
You don’t need to have played Warcraft. Genuinely. Roughly half of what a longtime player “knows” about this era was written years later and doesn’t apply here anyway, so everyone starts closer to level than you’d expect.

Where We Are
Four years ago, the world nearly ended.
A demonic army called the Burning Legion invaded. Orcs, humans, and night elves — three peoples with every reason to hate each other — fought together on the slopes of a mountain called Hyjal and stopped it. The night elves spent ten thousand years of immortality to do it. It worked.
Then everyone went home, and nobody agreed what came next.
That’s where we start. Not in a golden age and not in a ruin — in the messy, underfunded, badly-organised aftermath, four years on, where the heroes have scattered and the paperwork was never done.
Some things you’d know if you lived there:

The kingdom of Lordaeron is gone. Not conquered — destroyed from within by an undead plague. Its survivors are refugees. Its capital is a graveyard.
Stormwind still stands, ruled by a ten-year-old king and a regent doing his best. It is broke, and its outlying provinces have noticed that nobody is coming to help them.
Ironforge is rich, stable, and quietly running most of the Alliance because nobody else can afford to.
The orcs have a homeland. For the first time. A red desert on another continent that nobody else wanted, with a city built out of raw timber and iron four years ago.
The night elves are mortal now, for the first time in ten millennia, and they are not handling it well.
There is no war and there is no peace. Alliance and Horde raid each other over lumber, land, and old grudges, in three or four places, constantly, while both leaderships insist it isn’t a war.



                  
                  Want the longer version? 
                  
                

A Short History of Azeroth covers how the world got here — the myths everyone half-believes, the wars your grandparents fought, and the six years everyone lived through. It also flags the places where the Alliance and the Horde remember the same event completely differently, which is most of them.
It is written for players and contains no secrets. Read it if you want more; skip it if you don’t.



The Two Sides
The Alliance isn’t an alliance. It’s seven governments that won a war together, never signed anything afterward, and are currently held together by habit and by Ironforge’s money. Humans, dwarves, gnomes, and — recently and uneasily — night elves.
The Horde isn’t the Horde you may have heard of. The old one was a demon-poisoned war machine. This one is four years old, led by a young shaman who freed his people from prison camps and is trying to build a country out of them. Orcs, trolls, tauren, and the undead who broke free of the plague that made them.
Neither side is the villain. Both have people in them doing indefensible things and people in them trying very hard. If the campaign works, you should at some point find yourself agreeing with someone you’re supposed to be fighting.

Who You Can Be
Human, dwarf, gnome, or night elf on the Alliance side. Orc, troll, tauren, or Forsaken — the free-willed undead — on the Horde side.
Each of those has its own page with history, leadership, current conflicts, what they want, and how they talk — start at Peoples MOC and pick yours. They are written for players too.
We’re using D&D 5.5E, plus the official Warcraft sourcebook when it releases. Bring a character concept to session zero rather than a finished sheet; we’ll settle species, class, and the mechanical details together, and some of it depends on what the book says.
Come with an idea of where your character is from and what they want. That’s more useful than a build.

What Kind Of Game This Is
You start small. Level one, in one place, with local problems — a mine, a missing patrol, a farm that can’t pay its taxes. The world’s larger disasters are all happening, but they’re happening somewhere else for now, and you’ll hear about them long before you can do anything about them.
Violence is one tool. Several of the campaign’s genuine problems can’t be solved by winning a fight — and at least one gets actively worse if you try. Expect documents, negotiations, and people with legitimate grievances alongside the monsters.
Your relationships are your resources. The people you help early will matter later. So will the ones you don’t.
Death is real. No respawns, no running back to your body. Resurrection exists but it’s rare, expensive, and someone will want something for it.

One Request
If you already know Warcraft well: please don’t look things up mid-campaign, and don’t tell the others what’s coming. Several plot threads depend on nobody at the table knowing the answer yet, and a wiki tab will flatten them.
If you know some of it, come tell the DM privately what you know. Being trusted with a secret is much more fun than accidentally spoiling one.

Bring To Session Zero

A character concept — species, rough class idea, and one sentence about what they want
Anything you’d rather the game avoid, or handle carefully. This gets asked properly at the table too.
Questions. Any of them. There’s no such thing as a dumb Warcraft question here — half the table is learning it fresh.

Rules/Classes-of-Azeroth.title: Classes of Azeroth
Rules/Classes-of-Azeroth.content:
Classes of Azeroth
The hub. Twelve of the thirteen WoW classes are playable. Each has its own page with lore, level-1 identity, every specialization graded against a 2024 subclass, and species pairings worth stealing.


                  
                  Decided 
                  
                

All classes are open except the Evoker. The faction and species locks stay. Those rules do different jobs — the class list is about what a player can be, the locks are about what Azeroth in Year 29 can explain.
The three post-vanilla classes are open as rarities: you are not joining an order, you are one of a handful. Each page gives concrete origins to pick from at session zero.




                  
                  The campaign starts after the book 
                  
                

Nothing here describes how to play before 17 November, because we are not starting before then. Character choices get made against the sourcebook, not against a stopgap.
I get early access on 3 November, so there are two weeks to confirm all of this and fix whatever I got wrong.




                  
                  Flavour first, mechanics second 
                  
                

Where a WoW spec has no clean 5.5E equivalent, the flavour is the thing worth preserving and the rotation is not. A Protection Warrior is the one who steps in front and shouts; whether the system has a taunt button is a separate and less interesting question.
The gradings below exist to set expectations honestly at session zero — not to talk anyone out of a character. Nothing on this page is a “don’t play this”.



Availability
































































































ClassAvailable ToChassisRarityPageWarriorAll eight speciesFighter / BarbarianEverywhereWarriorPaladinAlliance only — human, dwarfPaladinUncommon, and leaderlessPaladinHunterDwarf, night elf, orc, tauren, trollRangerCommonHunterRogueAll but taurenRogueCommonRoguePriestHuman, dwarf, night elf, Forsaken, trollClericCommonPriestShamanHorde only — orc, tauren, trollDruid / Cleric / BarbarianRevivingShamanMageHuman, gnome, Forsaken, trollWizardScattered exilesMageWarlockHuman, gnome, orc, ForsakenWarlockIllegal everywhereWarlockDruidNight elf, taurenDruidHalf of them asleepDruidDeath KnightAny speciesPaladinThe one who got outDeath KnightMonkAny species, local traditionMonkUncommon, undocumentedMonkDemon HunterNight elf or blood elfRangerOne of a dozen aliveDemon Hunter
Not available


                  
                  Evoker is cut 
                  
                

The class is species-locked to the dracthyr, and dracthyr are Neltharion’s hidden experiment — a PC hands the table a piece of his laboratory at level one and The Dragon in the Court depends on that staying buried.
It is also the worst-supported class in 5.5E: Devastation converts cleanly and Preservation and Augmentation have no equivalent at all, which the WoW sourcebook does not fix. Cutting it costs one spec that worked and removes two that never would.
A player who wants dragon magic takes Sorcerer (Draconic Sorcery) with a Red Dragonflight or Blue Dragonflight blessing in their bloodline. Same mechanics, no spoiled secret, and it plugs into Alexstrasza and Malygos.




                  
                  Three rulings worth reading before session zero 
                  
                

Death knights are not Ebon Blade — that order is founded four years from now. You broke free of the Scourge on your own, and Death Knight gives three ways that could have happened.
Demon hunters are night elf or blood elf. There are three specific routes in and one of them is homebrew. See Demon Hunter — and note the blood elf route is a deliberate, narrow exception to the no-blood-elf rule.
Monks need a local tradition rather than a monastery. Kaldorei Warden discipline, tauren wrestling, troll fighting-forms. Do not say “chi” at the table.



Books In Play


                  
                  Everything below is available at the table 
                  
                

All of these are in hand by the time we start. Nothing on this page depends on a book I do not have.





































BookUnlocksPlayer’s Handbook 2024The twelve core classes and 48 subclassesDungeon Master’s Guide / Monster ManualNo subclassesRavenloft: The Horrors WithinGrave Domain, Undead Patron, Phantom, Shadow Sorcery, Hollow Warden, College of SpiritsForgotten Realms: Heroes of FaerûnBanneret, Winter Walker, Spellfire, Bladesinger, Scion of the ThreeArcana UnleashedArcane Archer, Necromancer, Conjurer, Vestige PatronD&D: World of Warcraft6 new + 3 updated subclasses. Early access 3 Nov, general 17 Nov.Eberron: Forge of the ArtificerNot bought — see the Artificer note below




                  
                  One subclass you own but cannot use 
                  
                

Reanimator is in Ravenloft, but it is an Artificer subclass — and the Artificer is not in the 2024 Player’s Handbook. It lives only in Eberron: Forge of the Artificer.
So Reanimator, and the whole Artificer chassis, are off the table unless I buy that book too. Worth knowing before a player finds it in Ravenloft and asks. No WoW class maps to Artificer anyway — it is the gnomish-engineer build, not a spec conversion.



The Master Mapping Table
Every WoW specialization graded against a 2024 (5.5E) subclass.


                  
                  Fit key 
                  
                

✅ Direct — the subclass does the thing; flavour is the only difference
🔄 Shared — reuses a subclass another spec already uses, differentiated by spell list, weapon, or flavour. This is fine and not a downgrade.
🟡 Close — playable, loses something specific. Named in each row.
🔴 Thin — no subclass does this. Playable on flavour; the mechanics will not carry it.




                  
                  Source key 
                  
                

PHB = Player’s Handbook 2024 · RHW = Ravenloft: The Horrors Within · HoF = Heroes of Faerûn · AU = Arcana Unleashed · WoW = D&D World of Warcraft Sourcebook










































































































































































































































































WoW ClassSpecBest SubclassFitSourceWarriorArmsFighter — Battle Master✅PHBFuryBarbarian — Path of the Berserker🟡PHBProtectionFighter — Banneret🟡HoFPaladinHolyPaladin — Oath of the Holy✅WoWProtectionPaladin — Oath of Glory🟡PHBRetributionPaladin — Oath of Vengeance✅PHBHunterBeast MasteryRanger — Beast Master✅PHBMarksmanshipFighter — Arcane Archer✅AUSurvivalRanger — Gloom Stalker🟡PHBRogueAssassinationRogue — Assassin✅PHBCombat / OutlawRogue — Swashbuckler✅WoWSubtletyRogue — Phantom🟡RHWPriestDisciplineCleric — Discipline Domain✅WoWHolyCleric — Life Domain✅PHBShadowCleric — Shadow Domain✅WoWShamanElementalDruid — Circle of the Sea🟡PHBEnhancementBarbarian — Path of the Elements✅WoWRestorationCleric — Life Domain🟡PHBMageArcaneWizard — Evoker🔄PHBFireWizard — Evoker✅PHBFrostWizard — Abjurer🟡PHBWarlockAfflictionWarlock — Fiend + Tome🔴PHBDemonologyWarlock — Fiend + Pact of the Chain🔴PHBDestructionWarlock — Fiend + Agonizing Blast✅PHBDruidBalanceDruid — Circle of the Stars✅PHBFeralDruid — Circle of the Moon✅PHBGuardianDruid — Circle of the Moon (bear)🔄PHBRestorationDruid — Circle of the Land🟡PHBDeath KnightBloodPaladin — Oath of the Ebon Blade✅WoWFrostPaladin — Oath of the Ebon Blade🔄WoWUnholyPaladin — Oath of the Ebon Blade🔄WoWMonkBrewmasterMonk — Warrior of Mystic Brews✅WoWMistweaverMonk — Warrior of Mercy✅PHBWindwalkerMonk — Warrior of the Open Hand✅PHBDemon HunterHavocRanger — Demon Hunter✅WoWVengeanceRanger — Demon Hunter🔄WoW
Tally across 35 specs: 17 direct · 5 shared · 11 close · 2 thin. Twenty-two need nothing but flavour, and only two are genuinely thin — both of them Warlock.


                  
                  Nine of these rows are predictions, not readings 
                  
                

Every row marked WoW is inferred from an announced subclass name. The book is not out. Nobody outside WotC has seen the mechanics.
What is actually known: the nine subclass names, which class each attaches to, and which WoW spec each is obviously aimed at. That is genuinely a lot — Oath of the Ebon Blade on a Paladin chassis is not ambiguous.
What is not known: what any of them actually do. Whether Discipline Domain really implements absorb-healing. Whether the Demon Hunter Ranger solves mobility. Whether the 13 class skins contain useful guidance or a paragraph of flavour text. Whether the official species rules match the stand-ins on Playable Species at Launch. Whether professions replace Professions and Crafting outright.
Verification date: 3 November. Two weeks before general release and well before session one. Anything that contradicts this page goes in the reconciliation table on D&D World of Warcraft Sourcebook, and this page gets corrected rather than argued with.



The Four Systemic Differences


                  
                  These are not problems to solve 
                  
                

Four things WoW does that 5.5E structurally does not. Knowing them stops you trying to convert something that was never going to convert, and tells you what to say at session zero.


1 · No threat, no aggro
Affects: Protection Warrior · Protection Paladin · Guardian Druid · Blood DK · Brewmaster Monk
Nothing in 5.5E makes an enemy attack you. 5e assumes positioning and the Sentinel feat do the work that threat does in WoW, and the WoW sourcebook adds nothing here either.
What to do: play the flavour. Stepping in front, shouting, and refusing to move are all roleplay, and Banneret (Heroes of Faerûn) makes the shouting mechanical. Nobody at the table will miss a threat meter.
Caveat: the book could ship a threat mechanic inside a class skin. If it does, this section is wrong and that is a good outcome. Recheck 3 November.
2 · No stacking timers
Affects: Affliction Warlock · Restoration Druid · Restoration Shaman
WoW is built on applying and maintaining damage- and healing-over-time. 5.5E has perhaps three such spells and no management game around them. Healing here is burst and reactive rather than pre-emptive.
What to do: say it at session zero. An Affliction warlock who curses people and watches them rot plays fine as a character; they just resolve their damage immediately. Undead Patron (Ravenloft) gets closer to the decay theme than Fiend does.
Caveat: 60+ new spells ship with the book and some may well be damage-over-time. Recheck 3 November.
3 · One pet, not six
Affects: Demonology Warlock
Pact of the Chain gives you a single familiar. 5e limits summoning deliberately — six pets is six extra turns and the table crawls.
What to do: your imp is the whole pact, and it gets nastier as you level. If the player wants a horde, they want a different game, and steering them to Destruction is kinder than homebrewing it.
4 · No resource meters
Affects: every class, slightly
Rage, combo points, runes, chi, and mana-as-a-bar all refresh per-second; 5e refreshes per-rest. There is no equivalent and building one makes the conversion worse, not better. Reflavour freely and do not build a subsystem.

What the Sourcebook Adds


                  
                  The shape of the list is informative 
                  
                

6 new subclasses — Oath of the Ebon Blade, Oath of the Holy, Demon Hunter (Ranger), Shadow Domain, Discipline Domain, Path of the Elements.
3 updated — Swashbuckler (Rogue), Path of the Spiritual Guardian (Barbarian), Warrior of Mystic Brews (Monk).
13 class skins — reflavouring guidance for every WoW class.
WotC built new subclasses only where the 2024 PHB had a genuine hole — death magic, absorb-healing, void damage, fel mobility, elemental weapons. What the list does not include is any warrior, mage, druid or warlock subclass, which is why threat, stacking timers and mass summoning are likely to stay unsolved.
That inference is drawn from the announced list. It could be wrong — a class skin or a new spell could cover any of it. Recheck 3 November.


The classes with no WoW equivalent
Bard has no WoW class. The nearest thing Azeroth has is a troll drummer or a Tauren storyteller — a background, not a class conflict. College of Spirits (Ravenloft) is an excellent troll voodoo build, and College of the Moon (Heroes of Faerûn) suits a priestess of Elune better than any cleric domain does.
Artificer would be the gnomish engineer, and it is not available — the class lives only in Eberron: Forge of the Artificer, which I have not bought. See the books table above.


What Your Class Means Here


                  
                  The thing every class has in common in Year 29 
                  
                

The people who would have trained you properly are dead. The Silver Hand is leaderless, Dalaran is a crater, orcish shamanism was nearly lost to the Legion, Gnomeregan is sealed, and half the Cenarion Circle is still asleep. You are not the inheritor of a proud unbroken tradition. You are what’s left, taught in a hurry by someone who was themselves taught in a hurry.
At level 1 you are competent at one thing and untested at everything else. Nobody has heard of you. That is the point — this campaign starts in a village with a local problem, and the first person who trusts you will do so because you were standing there.



Quick Concept Table


                  
                  For a player who wants to be told what to play 
                  
                

Pick a line. Every one of these connects to something already happening in the world.























































































ConceptSpecies · ClassBuildThe one who was there when it went wrongGnome rogueThiefRelearning what was stolen from your peopleOrc shamanPath of the ElementsFirst of your kind, with nobody to askTauren druidCircle of the MoonWoke up into a world that had moved onNight elf druidCircle of the StarsServing an order that lost its wayHuman paladinOath of DevotionRemembers being alive, and being cleverForsaken mageEvokerOwes the Horde everything, personallyTroll hunterBeast MasterApproaches the sacred like a machineDwarf paladinOath of GloryMade one bargain and is still payingHuman warlockFiend PatronHolds the line because someone has toAny warriorBattle MasterThe Light burns you and you use it anywayForsaken priestDiscipline DomainDied, woke up, and nobody has a word for youAny death knightOath of the Ebon BladeSent back through the Portal, barely trainedBlood elf demon hunterDemon Hunter (Ranger)Taught by one person, copying them stillAny monkWarrior of the Open HandTen thousand years hunting alone, on nobody’s ledgerNight elf demon hunterHollow Warden, then Demon Hunter

If a Player Just Wants It To Work


                  
                  The five smoothest conversions 
                  
                

Every one of these is buildable from the core Player’s Handbook today, with no gaps and nothing to buy.
Fire Mage (Wizard, Evoker) · Retribution Paladin (Oath of Vengeance) · Feral or Balance Druid (Circle of the Moon / Stars) · Beast Mastery Hunter (Beast Master) · Destruction Warlock (Fiend + Agonizing Blast)
And the two the mechanics will not carry: Affliction Warlock and Demonology Warlock. Both are still playable on flavour — see Warlock — but tell the player before they build, not after.

Rules/Classes/Death-Knight.title: Death Knight
Rules/Classes/Death-Knight.content:
Death Knight


                  
                  Open, but you are an anomaly 
                  
                

Death knights exist in Year 29 as Scourge commanders. What does not exist is a free-willed one — the Knights of the Ebon Blade are not founded for another four years.
So you are not a member of an order. You are the first one who got out. Nobody has a name for what you are, both factions would kill you on sight if they understood it, and there is no one to train you.




                  
                  At a glance 
                  
                






























Available toAny species — the Scourge raised everyoneFactionNeither. You are a defector from a third thing.5e chassisPaladinSourcebookOath of the Ebon Blade (new, 17 Nov)RarityThe only one anyone has met


In the World
Two generations of death knight precede you.
The first were orcish warlocks of the Shadow Council, their souls stuffed into the corpses of fallen Knights of the Silver Hand during The Second War. Gul’dan built them. Teron Gorefiend was the first, and he is dead.
The second is Arthas Menethil’s, and it is the one that matters. Rune-blade wielders raised by The Lich King in Northrend and seeded through the Plaguelands as officers. The Argent Dawn exists specifically because of them.
You are the crack in the second generation. How the crack happened is your character — pick one at session zero.

The Three Origins


                  
                  All three are mine, not Blizzard's 
                  
                

The free-willed death knight is a 2008 story. These are three ways to get one four years early without breaking anything downstream.


1 · The binding failed
The runeblade took less than it should have. Whatever Arthas does to bind a will did not fully take on you — because the ritual was rushed, because the blade was flawed, or because you were more stubborn than he budgeted for.
Nobody knows this happened, including the Scourge. You spent some time pretending, and then you ran.
Plays as: paranoia. Every death knight you meet might notice. Best for a player who likes the tension of passing.
2 · The Lich King let go
The Lich King’s attention is not infinite, and in Year 29 he is spending nearly all of it on Northrend, rebuilding after the Third War. Control at range degrades. Some of the officers he seeded in the Plaguelands have been running on old orders for years.
You are one whose orders ran out. Nobody released you. You were simply forgotten long enough to become someone again.
Plays as: dread. He has not lost you. He has not looked. Sooner or later he will look.
3 · Somebody cut you loose
The Argent Dawn has been trying to sever Scourge bindings since it formed, mostly unsuccessfully. They have had exactly one success, or think they have.
You were captured, worked on for months by people who were not sure it would work and did it anyway, and woke up owing a debt to an organisation that still is not certain you are safe.
Plays as: obligation. You have a faction, a handler, and a leash you agreed to.


                  
                  Which to pick 
                  
                

1 for a lone-wolf character, 2 for horror, 3 for a player who wants somewhere to belong from session one. Three is the friendliest to a new player and the easiest to fold into a party.



At Level 1
You died. You remember dying. You have been walking for somewhere between a month and a year and you have not yet met anyone who knows what to do with you.
Your body does not tire and does not warm. The runeblade is louder when you are angry. You are not sure whether the hunger is yours.
Specializations


                  
                  Fit key 
                  
                

✅ Direct — the subclass does the thing · 🔄 Shared — same subclass as another spec, differentiated by flavour and gear · 🟡 Close — works, loses something · 🔴 Gap — nothing in 5.5E does this































WoW SpecSubclassFitWhyBloodPaladin — Oath of the Ebon Blade (WoW book)✅ DirectSelf-healing tank. Death Strike is the whole spec and it needed a purpose-built feature.FrostPaladin — Oath of the Ebon Blade, dual-wield🔄 SharedSame oath, two weapons and cold damage. Obliterate and Howling Blast.UnholyPaladin — Oath of the Ebon Blade, with a ghoul🔄 SharedSame oath plus the raised minion.


                  
                  These features are not confirmed yet 
                  
                

The sourcebook’s subclass names are announced. Its mechanics are not. Everything in the table above is a reasonable prediction from a name and a WoW spec, not a reading of the book.
Early access is 3 November. Confirm on the day, and log anything that surprises you in the D&D World of Warcraft Sourcebook reconciliation table.




                  
                  All three specs, one oath 
                  
                

Blood, Frost and Unholy are the same subclass with different weapons and a different minion. That is how WoW does it too — the specs share a resource and a chassis and diverge on what they point it at.


Species Pairings
Anyone the Scourge could reach, which in The Third War was nearly everyone.

Human — Lordaeron. You were in the levies, or the clergy, or you were nobody, and Arthas came through anyway.
Forsaken — you are the only being in Azeroth who has been raised twice, and the Royal Apothecary Society would very much like to know how
Night elf — taken at Mount Hyjal. The kaldorei have no word for what you are and they have had four years to invent one.
Dwarf — an Explorers’ League dig that went into the wrong barrow in the Western Plaguelands
Orc — the first generation’s inheritance, and the Shadow Council would like it back
Tauren — Lordaeron is a long way from Mulgore. How you got there is the character.

Playing One Here
The death knight’s problem is not power. It is that there is nowhere to put you.
The Argent Dawn hunts your kind and might make an exception. The Scourge wants you back and does not consider your opinion relevant. The Forsaken are the only people in Azeroth who would recognise your situation, and joining them means joining the Horde.
