Rules/Classes/Demon-Hunter.title: Demon Hunter
Rules/Classes/Demon-Hunter.content:
Demon Hunter


                  
                  Open — night elf or blood elf, and you are one of a handful 
                  
                

There is no Illidari. The order is founded twelve years from now, Illidan Stormrage is beyond the Dark Portal, and nobody on Azeroth is taking students.
So you got here by one of three specific routes, and which one is the character. Pick at session zero.




                  
                  At a glance 
                  
                






























Available toNight elf or blood elf — see the three originsFactionNight elf: nominally Alliance, hunted anyway. Blood elf: nobody’s — but drifting Horde-ward, because nothing else opens.5e chassisRangerSourcebookDemon Hunter Ranger (new, 17 Nov)RarityPerhaps a dozen alive, and most are on another world


In the World
Illidan Stormrage is the demon hunter. He burned out his own eyes with Sargeras’s fire, drank from the Skull of Gul’dan, and his brother put him in a barrow prison under Mount Hyjal for ten thousand years because of it.
He was released four years ago to fight Arthas, and he is now beyond the Dark Portal, having taken Outland from Magtheridon. Altruis and Varedis went with him. So did most of what remained of his order.
You are one of the ones who didn’t.

1 · Released, and stayed behind (night elf)
You took the fire before The Sundering and the Wardens put you under with him. When the doors opened four years ago you walked out — and did not follow him a second time.
What this costs you. You went into the ground before the Sundering and came out after The Third War. Everything is wrong. Your people are mortal, Nordrassil has burned, Cenarius is dead, and there is an alliance with a species called humans that you have never heard of.
This is the same shock the awakened druids carry, except they are welcomed home and you are not.
2 · Never sealed (night elf — homebrew)


                  
                  This one is mine, not Blizzard's 
                  
                

Canon says the Wardens took all of them. I am saying they took all but one, because it makes a better character and nothing downstream breaks.


The Wardens came for Illidan’s followers ten thousand years ago and you were not there — out hunting, or already hiding, or simply missed in a chaotic night. Maiev Shadowsong’s records show your name on the list of the interred. The records are wrong.
You have spent ten thousand years alone, hunting demons nobody knew were there, staying ahead of an order that thinks you are already in a cell. You have no allies, no home, and no one who can confirm you exist.
What this costs you. Nothing about the world surprises you — you watched all of it happen. What you have instead is ten thousand years of solitude and the certainty that the moment a Warden gets a good look at you, the paperwork problem becomes your problem.


                  
                  This is the best fit for a first-time player 
                  
                

Origin 1 requires roleplaying total cultural displacement every session. Origin 3 requires knowing Kael’thas lore. Origin 2 just requires being tired. It is the least homework and the most immediately playable.


3 · Trained in Outland, and sent back (blood elf)
Kael’thas Sunstrider took the sin’dorei through the Dark Portal a year ago and threw in with Illidan. Illidan needed demon hunters and had a supply of desperate, fel-addicted elves who had already lost everything.
You are from the first blood elf intake, and you are barely trained. A year of Illidan’s methods, which are not gentle and not long. Then you were sent back through the Portal for a reason you were told once and did not fully understand.
What this costs you. You are the newest demon hunter alive and it shows. You also came back to an Azeroth where your people are a rumour — the sin’dorei are offscreen, Quel’Thalas is a ruin, and the Alliance still thinks of your kind as high elves who went quiet.


                  
                  Where this leaves you politically 
                  
                

Nowhere, and that is the point. The Alliance imprisoned your people for treason at the end of the last war and you have not forgotten it. The sin’dorei are offscreen beyond the Portal. There is no blood elf delegation anywhere on Azeroth.
The Horde is the only door that opens — not by treaty, just by being the one group with no reason to hate you on sight. That drift is where canon goes a few years from now, and you are early to it.




                  
                  This is a deliberate exception to the species rule 
                  
                

Playable Species at Launch says no blood elf PCs, and that stands for everyone else. This origin is the one door through it, because it is the only one where the character has to be sin’dorei — Illidan’s blood elf intake is the only demon hunter recruitment happening anywhere in 2004.
It does not open blood elves generally, and it does not put Quel’Thalas or Silvermoon on the map. You came back alone.



At Level 1
Blindfolded, fel-scarred, and carrying something in you that is not you. You see demons other people cannot. You have never met another practitioner who was not also a prisoner.
Specializations


                  
                  Fit key 
                  
                

✅ Direct — the subclass does the thing · 🔄 Shared — same subclass as another spec, differentiated by flavour · 🟡 Close — works, loses something · 🔴 Gap — nothing in 5.5E does this

























WoW SpecSubclassFitWhyHavocRanger — Demon Hunter (WoW book)✅ DirectMovement-as-aggression. Fel Rush and Eye Beam need purpose-built features, which is why this subclass exists.VengeanceRanger — Demon Hunter (WoW book), defensive picks🔄 SharedSame subclass, defensive options. Demon Spikes is a named spell in the new book.


                  
                  These features are not confirmed yet 
                  
                

The sourcebook’s subclass names are announced. Its mechanics are not. Everything in the table above is a reasonable prediction from a name and a WoW spec, not a reading of the book.
Early access is 3 November. Confirm on the day, and log anything that surprises you in the D&D World of Warcraft Sourcebook reconciliation table.




                  
                  Play the flavour, not the rotation 
                  
                

Fel Rush, Eye Beam, and Metamorphosis may not convert cleanly even with the book, and that is fine. What makes a demon hunter at the table is fel sight, glaives, a blindfold, and the fact that something is riding along inside you — none of which needs a subclass feature.
If the book’s Demon Hunter turns out not to scratch the itch, Ranger (Hollow Warden) is the closest alternative in any other book: Wrath of the Wild is a transformation with a fear aura, on the same Ranger chassis.


Species Pairings

Night elf — origins 1 and 2. Ten thousand years old, blind, fel-scarred, in a world that buried the people who put you under.
Blood elf — origin 3. A year of training, a world you barely recognise, and a prince who sent you back without explaining why.

Playing One Here
Two questions to settle at session zero, and both are good:
Did you take the fire willingly? All of Illidan’s followers were volunteers, in every generation. Whether you still think it was worth it is the character’s spine.
Who is looking for you? The Wardens imprisoned your order and consider the release an escape rather than a pardon. Maiev Shadowsong is currently chasing Illidan through the Dark Portal; she has deputies, and they are less busy.
Related

Rules/Classes/Druid.title: Druid
Rules/Classes/Druid.content:
Druid



                  
                  At a glance 
                  
                






























Available toNight elf, taurenFaction lockNone — but the only two traditions sit on opposite sides5e chassisDruidSourcebookClass skin onlyResource fantasyYou have been asleep, or you have no elders. Either way, you are behind.


In the World
The Cenarion Circle, taught by Cenarius, who is dead — killed by Grom Hellscream in Ashenvale four years ago.
For ten thousand years kaldorei druids slept in the Barrow Dens while the Sentinels kept watch above them. They are only now waking up, into a world where Nordrassil has burned, their immortality is gone, and the kaldorei have joined an alliance with humans. Nobody warned them. There was no way to.
And four years ago the night elves did something genuinely unprecedented: they taught outsiders. The first Tauren druids are alive right now, and the eldest of them is younger than the war that made them possible.
At Level 1
You are either newly awake or newly taught. In practice these mean the same thing: everyone assumes you know more than you do, and you are not going to correct them.
Specializations


                  
                  Fit key 
                  
                

✅ Direct — the subclass does the thing · 🔄 Shared — same subclass as another spec, differentiated by flavour · 🟡 Close — works, loses something · 🔴 Gap — nothing in 5.5E does this





































WoW Spec2024 SubclassFitWhyBalanceDruid — Circle of the Stars✅ DirectStarry Form is Moonkin Form — a non-beast combat shape with a caster’s damage. Moonfire and Starfire in one feature.FeralDruid — Circle of the Moon✅ DirectCat Form. Wild Shape as your primary combat mode rather than a utility button.GuardianDruid — Circle of the Moon, bear forms🔄 SharedSame subclass as Feral, tankiest beast at each tier. Hits the no-threat-mechanic wall — you can be a bear, you cannot make anything attack the bear.RestorationDruid — Circle of the Land🟡 CloseThe healing spell list is there. Stacking heal-over-time is not — Rejuvenation, Lifebloom and Wild Growth are a HoT-management game that 5.5E has no vocabulary for.


                  
                  Druid is the second-best-served class after Mage
                  
                

Balance and Feral are exact matches, and both come free in the core Player’s Handbook. The WoW sourcebook adds no druid subclass because none was needed.


Alternate builds

Guardian, as pure durability — Barbarian (Path of the Wild Heart). Bear Form as a rage rather than a Wild Shape. The best tauren guardian build, and it needs no spell slots.
Balance, as a moon-priest — Cleric (Light Domain) reflavoured to Elune. Blurs into Priest, which is arguably correct for a kaldorei.
Restoration, sea-flavoured — Druid (Circle of the Sea) for a druid trained near Darkshore rather than inland.
Feral, without spellcasting — Monk (Warrior of the Open Hand) reskinned as an unarmoured shapeshifter. Unusual, fast, and mechanically clean.



                  
                  Forms are the class 
                  
                

WoW druids swap shape mid-fight. 5e Wild Shape is a limited resource until Circle of the Moon fixes it. Set expectations at session zero: at level 1 you get two Wild Shapes per rest, not a rotation.


Species Pairings

Night elf — you went to sleep before The Third War and woke after it. Your people are mortal. Nobody warned you.
Tauren — you are among the first druids your people have ever produced. There is no elder to ask. You are the elder now, at nineteen.

Playing One Here
Both druid species carry the same wound from opposite directions: there is nobody above you who has done this before. The Cenarion Circle is a leaderless institution running on the authority of a dead demigod, and half its membership is still asleep.

Rules/Classes/Hunter.title: Hunter
Rules/Classes/Hunter.content:
Hunter



                  
                  At a glance 
                  
                






























Available toDwarf, night elf, orc, tauren, trollFaction lockNone — but no human, gnome, or Forsaken tradition exists5e chassisRangerSourcebookClass skin onlyResource fantasyA partnership, not a toolkit.


In the World
Not a job — a relationship. The bond with a companion beast is the entire discipline, and every people comes to it from a completely different direction.
Dwarven hunters are Explorers’ League escorts with bears and rifles. Kaldorei hunters ride nightsabers bred in Teldrassil and have done for ten thousand years. Orcish hunters take wolf-brothers, a practice that survived the Legion because it never depended on magic. Tauren hunt as a rite of adulthood in Mulgore. Darkspear hunters take raptors, which is less taming than negotiation.
Humans, gnomes, and Forsaken have marksmen and trappers — but no beast tradition. A human who wants a companion animal is a ranger, not a hunter, and should be built as one.
At Level 1
You are a tracker with one animal that has decided you are acceptable. It is not obedient. It is present, which is different.
Specializations


                  
                  Fit key 
                  
                

✅ Direct — the subclass does the thing · 🔄 Shared — same subclass as another spec, differentiated by flavour · 🟡 Close — works, loses something · 🔴 Gap — nothing in 5.5E does this











































WoW Spec2024 SubclassFitWhyBeast MasteryRanger — Beast Master✅ DirectYour companion is a character, not a spell effect. Nothing lost in translation.MarksmanshipFighter — Arcane Archer (Arcana Unleashed)✅ DirectThe Marksmanship build. Arcane Shot is Aimed Shot: a limited pool of big, named arrows.MarksmanshipRanger — Hunter🟡 CloseThe available-today version. Colossus Slayer is Aimed Shot, but the subclass is generic and 5e rangers do not do ranged burst.SurvivalRanger — Gloom Stalker🟡 CloseGets the ambush and the melee-from-a-ranged-class oddity. Traps have no 5.5E mechanic — Freezing Trap and Explosive Trap are reflavoured spells at best.SurvivalRanger — Winter Walker (Heroes of Faerûn)🟡 CloseFreezing Trap and Chimaera Shot as an entire subclass. Better than Gloom Stalker if the character is cold-flavoured; worse if they are a jungle troll.
Alternate builds

Survival, as a trapper — Ranger (Fey Wanderer) reskinned. Charm and misdirection instead of shadow.
Marksmanship, frost-flavoured — Ranger (Winter Walker, Heroes of Faerûn). Freezing Trap and Chimaera Shot as a whole subclass.
Beast Mastery, without spellcasting — Fighter (Champion) with an animal companion granted as a background feature. Cleanest for a player who wants a bow and a bear and nothing else.



                  
                  The pet is a party member 
                  
                

Give the companion a name at character creation and use it in narration. A hunter whose beast is a stat block is playing a ranger; a hunter whose beast has opinions is playing a hunter.


Species Pairings

Night elf — a nightsaber born the same night you were, in a people who no longer live long enough for that to be a small thing
Dwarf — Explorers’ League escort. You have shot things that came out of holes your employers dug.
Troll — a raptor. It is not tame. This is understood by both of you.
Tauren — you hunt for the herd, and you have never once killed for sport
Orc — a wolf out of Durotar, from a line that predates the Legion and outlasted it

Playing One Here
The hunter’s story is almost always the beast’s story. Where did it come from, what did it cost, and what happens the first time the party asks you to send it somewhere it will not come back from?

Rules/Classes/Mage.title: Mage
Rules/Classes/Mage.content:
Mage



                  
                  At a glance 
                  
                






























Available toHuman, gnome, Forsaken, trollFaction lockNone5e chassisWizardSourcebookClass skin onlyResource fantasyA discipline with no institution left to enforce it.


In the World
Arcane magic came to humanity from Quel’Thalas by way of Arathor, taught by high elves paying a debt, and its great institution was the Kirin Tor of Dalaran.
Dalaran was pulled down four years ago. Archimonde destroyed it during The Third War and what remains is a crater under a purple dome. The survivors are scattered — exiles teaching in back rooms in Stormwind City and Ironforge, arguing about who has the authority to certify anyone. Forsaken mages remember the same curriculum from the other side of dying.
Troll mages exist and are almost entirely self-taught, which the surviving Kirin Tor consider impossible and which the trolls consider none of their business.
At Level 1
You are a student whose academy no longer exists, holding notes from a teacher who may or may not still be alive. Nobody will certify you. Nobody is left who can.
Specializations


                  
                  Fit key 
                  
                

✅ Direct — the subclass does the thing · 🔄 Shared — same subclass as another spec, differentiated by flavour · 🟡 Close — works, loses something · 🔴 Gap — nothing in 5.5E does this































WoW Spec2024 SubclassFitWhyFireWizard — Evoker✅ DirectPyroblast, Fireball, Scorch — 5e gives you all three by name, and Sculpt Spells solves friendly fire.ArcaneWizard — Evoker🔄 SharedSame subclass as Fire, force-weighted spellbook. Arcane Blast and Arcane Missiles are raw force. Loses the mana-management identity, which 5e’s slot system cannot express.FrostWizard — Abjurer🟡 CloseArcane Ward is Ice Barrier and Mana Shield. But Frost’s control — slows, roots, Frost Nova — comes from spell selection rather than the subclass, so the build is mostly your prepared list.


                  
                  Mage is the best-served class in the conversion 
                  
                

Wizard is the one 5e class that already works the way a WoW class does: pick a school, prepare a list, throw damage. All three specs are buildable from the core Player’s Handbook with no purchases and no homebrew. If a player wants a guaranteed-smooth character, this is it.
Conjurer, Enchanter, Necromancer and Transmuter from Arcana Unleashed complete the school set — Conjurer is the summoner-mage build if anyone wants it.


Alternate builds

Frost, damage-first — Wizard (Evoker) with cold spells. Simpler, hits harder, loses the barrier fantasy.
Arcane, as innate talent — Sorcerer (Spellfire Sorcery, Heroes of Faerûn). Power drawn straight from the Weave with no academy behind it. The best build for a troll or a self-taught human.
A battlemage — Wizard (Bladesinger, Heroes of Faerûn). Not a WoW spec, but it is the Quel’Thalas spellblade tradition and it fits a high elf perfectly.
Arcane, as a diviner — Wizard (Diviner). Nothing in WoW matches it, but Kirin Tor scrying is very much a thing and it plays beautifully in an investigation campaign.



                  
                  Portals and Conjured Food 
                  
                

The two things every WoW player expects a mage to do. Teleportation Circle is 5th level and Create Food and Water is 3rd — both are a long way from level 1. Tell players this at session zero so nobody plans a campaign around free travel.


Species Pairings

Human — a Dalaran refugee, or a Stormwind apprentice taught by one
Gnome — you approach spellwork as engineering, document everything, and are baffled that others don’t
Forsaken — you remember being a Kirin Tor apprentice. You remember the whole thing.
Troll — self-taught and unaffiliated, which most mages consider impossible

Playing One Here
Your teacher is the hook. Alive, dead, or missing — pick one at session zero and the campaign will find them.

Rules/Classes/Monk.title: Monk
Rules/Classes/Monk.content:
Monk


                  
                  Open, and the easiest of the four to justify 
                  
                

There is no monastic chi tradition in Year 29 and Pandaria is behind the mist. But the monk needs no cosmic permission — only a teacher, and every people in Azeroth has an unarmed fighting tradition nobody has written down.
Do not use the word “chi” at the table. Everything else about this class survives the translation intact.




                  
                  At a glance 
                  
                






























Available toAny species, with a local tradition to hang it onFactionNone5e chassisMonkSourcebookWarrior of Mystic Brews (updated, 17 Nov)RarityUncommon, not unique — people have always fought with their hands


In the World
Pandaren exist in 2004 as a Warcraft III easter egg. Chen Stormstout was a hero unit, and that is the complete published canon. Pandaria will not surface for eight years, there is no Shado-Pan, and no Order of the Broken Temple.
But nobody in Azeroth needed pandaren to invent punching. The traditions that already exist:

Kaldorei Wardens — night elf jailers trained in unarmed restraint, ten thousand years old and unbroken. The closest thing Azeroth has to a martial order.
Tauren wrestling — a rite in Thunder Bluff and Mulgore, practised for status and settled without weapons
Troll fighting-forms — surviving fragments of the Gurubashi and Amani empires, taught in the Darkspear Tribe alongside the drums
Shen’dralar discipline — the exiled highborne in Dire Maul have had ten thousand years and nothing to do
Pandaren brewing — one traveller, if a player wants it. See Species of the Sourcebook.

Pick one at session zero. Mechanically Monk, narratively local.
At Level 1
You were taught by one person and you are still copying them. You have never met another practitioner outside your teacher’s household, and you assume the discipline is more widespread than it is.
Specializations


                  
                  Fit key 
                  
                

✅ Direct — the subclass does the thing · 🔄 Shared — same subclass as another spec, differentiated by flavour · 🟡 Close — works, loses something · 🔴 Gap — nothing in 5.5E does this































WoW SpecSubclassFitWhyWindwalkerMonk — Warrior of the Open Hand✅ DirectThe default monk is Windwalker. Flying Serpent Kick, Fists of Fury, Touch of Death — all of it is Open Hand technique, feature for feature.MistweaverMonk — Warrior of Mercy✅ DirectHands of healing and harm. Hand of Mercy is Soothing Mist. Best healer-monk mapping in either system.BrewmasterMonk — Warrior of Mystic Brews (WoW book)✅ DirectStagger, Purifying Brew, and the stumbling-tank identity. The 2014 Drunken Master brought forward.


                  
                  These features are not confirmed yet 
                  
                

The sourcebook’s subclass names are announced. Its mechanics are not. Everything in the table above is a reasonable prediction from a name and a WoW spec, not a reading of the book.
Early access is 3 November. Confirm on the day, and log anything that surprises you in the D&D World of Warcraft Sourcebook reconciliation table.


Alternate builds

Windwalker, elemental — Monk (Warrior of the Elements). 🔄 Shared chassis, storm-and-fire flavour instead of pure martial. Excellent for a Shaman-adjacent concept.
A Warden — Monk (Warrior of Shadow). Shadow Step and Darkness. No WoW spec matches it, but it is the single best mechanical fit for a kaldorei Warden and it is sitting in the core Player’s Handbook.
Arcane-flavoured — Monk (Warrior of the Mystic Arts, Arcana Unleashed). Not a WoW spec, but it exists and it is good.

Species Pairings

Night elf — a Warden’s discipline, which is a real ten-thousand-year-old tradition and the least homebrew option on this page
Tauren — Thunder Bluff wrestling. Powerful Build and Unarmoured Defence agree with each other.
Troll — Darkspear fighting-forms, half-remembered from an empire that fell
Human — a monastery in the Redridge Mountains that predates Stormwind and has nine members
Pandaren — if allowed as an exotic pick. The only character on this page who would recognise the word “monk”.

Playing One Here
The monk’s story is the teacher, same as the Mage’s. The difference is that a mage’s academy was destroyed and a monk’s never existed in the first place.
Related

Rules/Classes/Paladin.title: Paladin
Rules/Classes/Paladin.content:
Paladin



                  
                  At a glance 
                  
                






























Available toHuman, dwarfFaction lockAlliance only5e chassisPaladinSourcebookOath of the Holy (new)Resource fantasyThe Light answers, whether or not you deserve it.


In the World
The Order of the Silver Hand was the finest institution the Alliance ever built and it is broken. Uther is dead, killed by his own student. Tirion was excommunicated for sparing an orc who saved his life. Arthas — the Order’s brightest — became the precise thing it existed to destroy.
What remains trains initiates at Northshire Abbey and in Ironforge, and nobody has replaced the Highlord. There is no central authority, no unified doctrine, and no agreement about what went wrong. Ask three paladins why Arthas fell and you will get three answers, all of them defensive.
The lock is lore, not balance. The Silver Hand is a human institution founded by Stormwind and Lordaeron clergy, and the Light came to the dwarves through Ironforge’s contact with humanity. No Horde tradition of Light-wielding exists in Year 29. See Classes of Azeroth for what to do when a player wants one anyway.
At Level 1
You are an initiate who took vows from an Order that cannot currently define what it stands for. The Light answers you anyway, which is either reassuring or unsettling depending on the day and how much you have thought about it.
Specializations


                  
                  Fit key 
                  
                

✅ Direct — the subclass does the thing · 🔄 Shared — same subclass as another spec, differentiated by flavour · 🟡 Close — works, loses something · 🔴 Gap — nothing in 5.5E does this































WoW Spec2024 SubclassFitWhyHolyOath of the Holy (WoW book)✅ DirectThe purpose-built healing paladin. It exists because 5.5E paladins are otherwise not healers at all — Lay on Hands is a pool, not a rotation.ProtectionOath of Glory🟡 CloseInspiring Smite is Word of Glory and the aura reads as Devotion Aura. Runs into the same no-threat-mechanic wall as Protection Warrior.RetributionOath of Vengeance✅ DirectVow of Enmity is Avenging Wrath in everything but name. The single cleanest spec-to-subclass match in this whole vault.


                  
                  These features are not confirmed yet 
                  
                

The sourcebook’s subclass names are announced. Its mechanics are not. Everything in the table above is a reasonable prediction from a name and a WoW spec, not a reading of the book.
Early access is 3 November. Confirm on the day, and log anything that surprises you in the D&D World of Warcraft Sourcebook reconciliation table.


Alternate builds

Protection, as a bulwark — Oath of the Ancients. 🟡 Close. Aura of Warding is the most defensive thing in the class. Reflavour the fey imagery as Light and it works.
The Silver Hand as written — Oath of Devotion. 🟡 Close. Sacred Weapon and Protection from Evil are the Order’s actual liturgy. The most institutional paladin, if the character cares more about the Order than about a spec.
Retribution, for a lapsed one — Oath of Vengeance taken after a broken oath rather than instead of one. Tirion’s arc, played forward.



                  
                  Oath of the Ebon Blade is a different class 
                  
                

The sourcebook’s other new paladin oath is the Death Knight, not a paladin variant. Same chassis, opposite character.


Species Pairings

Human — Northshire-trained, and old enough to remember when the tabard meant something uncomplicated
Dwarf — the Light came to Ironforge late and practically; you approach it like engineering rather than mystery

Playing One Here
Every paladin at this table carries the same unanswered question: if the Light chose Arthas, what is choosing me?
There is no institution above you to settle it. Uther is dead. The Abbey writes to the crown and gets no reply. Whatever you decide the Light means, you are deciding it yourself, at level one, with no one to check your work.

Rules/Classes/Priest.title: Priest
Rules/Classes/Priest.content:
Priest



                  
                  At a glance 
                  
                






























Available toHuman, dwarf, night elf, Forsaken, trollFaction lockNone — but Light and Shadow split along faction lines in practice5e chassisClericSourcebookShadow Domain and Discipline Domain (both new)Resource fantasyTwo doors into the same room, and the other clergy will not use yours.


In the World
Two traditions that barely acknowledge each other.
Light. Stormwind Cathedral and Northshire Abbey, the halls of Ironforge, and the kaldorei Sisterhood of Elune — who would object to being grouped with the other two, since Elune is a goddess and the Light is a philosophy. All three heal, and all three are currently short-staffed.
Shadow. Forsaken and troll practice, drawing on the same source from the other side. The Light’s clergy regard it as an illness rather than a heresy, which is somehow worse. Forsaken shadow priests will tell you, without much patience, that the Light physically burns them and Shadow does not.
At Level 1
You are an acolyte. You can close a wound and steady a frightened person. You have not yet been asked to do anything harder than that, and you have opinions about what you would do if you were.
Specializations


                  
                  Fit key 
                  
                

✅ Direct — the subclass does the thing · 🔄 Shared — same subclass as another spec, differentiated by flavour · 🟡 Close — works, loses something · 🔴 Gap — nothing in 5.5E does this































WoW Spec2024 SubclassFitWhyDisciplineCleric — Discipline Domain (WoW book)✅ DirectPrevention over repair — shields, absorbs, damage that heals.HolyCleric — Life Domain✅ DirectDisciple of Life and Blessed Healer are Renew and Circle of Healing.ShadowCleric — Shadow Domain (WoW book)✅ DirectVoid damage, mind-affecting, self-sustaining.


                  
                  These features are not confirmed yet 
                  
                

The sourcebook’s subclass names are announced. Its mechanics are not. Everything in the table above is a reasonable prediction from a name and a WoW spec, not a reading of the book.
Early access is 3 November. Confirm on the day, and log anything that surprises you in the D&D World of Warcraft Sourcebook reconciliation table.


Alternate builds

Holy, as a priestess of Elune — Cleric (Light Domain). 🔄 Shared role, different god. Radiant and moonlight are the same colour at the table.
Shadow, as something that happened to you — Sorcerer (Shadow Sorcery, Ravenloft). 🟡 Close. For a Forsaken whose Shadow is innate rather than studied — they did not choose it and cannot put it down. Different character from a Shadow Domain priest, not a worse one.
Shadow, as an outside voice — Warlock (Great Old One). 🟡 Close. Mind Flay and Vampiric Touch as Dissonant Whispers and Mind Sliver, and the Old One framing fits troll and Forsaken practice more honestly than anyone in-world would admit.



                  
                  Which door you use is a character choice, not a mechanical one 
                  
                

A Forsaken can be a Holy priest. It hurts. That is a fantastic character and the pain should be in the fiction, not the stat block.


Species Pairings

Forsaken — the Light burns you now. Shadow doesn’t. You have had to build an entire theology around that fact.
Night elf — a Priestess of Elune, whose goddess has been notably quiet since Nordrassil burned
Human — Northshire, and increasingly aware that your Abbey’s letters to the crown go unanswered
Troll — voodoo, which the other priests call superstition and which works
Dwarf — Ironforge’s clergy are few, practical, and extremely hard to shock

Playing One Here
The priest is the only class that has to decide what it believes before level three. Light or Shadow is a mechanical choice in WoW and a theological one here.

Classes of Azeroth · The Holy Light · Elune · Forsaken · Magic Schools and Damage Types · Rules MOC

Rules/Classes/Rogue.title: Rogue
Rules/Classes/Rogue.content:
Rogue



                  
                  At a glance 
                  
                






























Available toAll but taurenFaction lockNone5e chassisRogueSourcebookSwashbuckler (updated to 2024)Resource fantasyYou were never there.


In the World
Three respectable careers and one disreputable one.
Stormwind Assassins — the crown’s intelligence service, which does not exist and has an office. Ravenholdt — an assassins’ school in the Hillsbrad Foothills that trains anyone who can pay and asks no questions about faction. Goblin work — smuggling out of Booty Bay for the Steamwheedle Cartel, which is technically neutral and practically whoever is paying. And then simple theft, which pays worst and gets you hanged.
Tauren are excluded for physics rather than lore. A nine-foot shorthorn does not do subtle. If a player wants the concept, build it as a scout or tracker instead — see Classes of Azeroth.
At Level 1
You are a scout, a burglar, or a runner for someone who does not use your real name. You have not killed for money yet, or you have and it did not go the way you expected.
Specializations


                  
                  Fit key 
                  
                

✅ Direct — the subclass does the thing · 🔄 Shared — same subclass as another spec, differentiated by flavour · 🟡 Close — works, loses something · 🔴 Gap — nothing in 5.5E does this































WoW Spec2024 SubclassFitWhyAssassinationRogue — Assassin✅ DirectPoisons, opening burst, advantage on the surprised. Assassinate is Ambush and Cheap Shot in one feature.Combat (later Outlaw)Rogue — Swashbuckler (WoW book)✅ DirectToe-to-toe duelling with a rogue’s toolkit. Updated to 2024 by the sourcebook.SubtletyRogue — Arcane Trickster, reskinned as shadow🟡 CloseCall Misty Step “Shadowstep” and Invisibility “Vanish” and it plays right. But there is no shadow rogue in 5.5E — see below.


                  
                  These features are not confirmed yet 
                  
                

The sourcebook’s subclass names are announced. Its mechanics are not. Everything in the table above is a reasonable prediction from a name and a WoW spec, not a reading of the book.
Early access is 3 November. Confirm on the day, and log anything that surprises you in the D&D World of Warcraft Sourcebook reconciliation table.




                  
                  Subtlety's signature move lives on the wrong class 
                  
                

The 2024 PHB does have a shadow-teleporting subclass — Warrior of Shadow, and it is a Monk. Shadow Step, Darkness, and shadow-arts are all there, on a chassis with no Sneak Attack.
Phantom (Rogue, Ravenloft) is the closest actual rogue and it is worth a look: death-echoes rather than shadow-magic, but Wails from the Grave is a second Sneak Attack every turn, which plays exactly like a Subtlety rogue’s burst. Scion of the Three (Heroes of Faerûn) is the other option, and it drags in a patron.
If the player wants Subtlety by name, Arcane Trickster reskinned is still the cleanest. If they want it to feel right in play, take Phantom.


Alternate builds

Subtlety, without spells — Rogue (Assassin) leaning entirely on Stealth expertise and Cunning Action. Simpler; loses the teleport.
Combat, as a brawler — Rogue (Thief) with Fast Hands. Sap, pickpocket, and improvised weapons.
Assassination, as a cultist — Rogue (Scion of the Three, Heroes of Faerûn) reflavoured to the Shadow Council or the Royal Apothecary Society. Only with DM buy-in, since it drags in a patron.
A rogue who is really a spy — Rogue (Soulknife) reskinned as a Stormwind Assassins operative with trained mental discipline rather than psionics. Works better than it sounds.



                  
                  Poisons are a subsystem here 
                  
                

Rogue poisons are more available in Azeroth than in default 5e — Ravenholdt sells them and the Royal Apothecary Society gives them away. See Consumables and Reagents.


Species Pairings

Gnome — sabotage and locks. Everything you know was learned in a city that no longer exists.
Forsaken — nobody watches a corpse walk past. It is the single greatest professional advantage in Azeroth and you have made your peace with why you have it.
Human — Westfall made you. You are one bad winter from having been a Defias instead.
Troll — you move through jungle the way other people move through a corridor
Night elf — a Sentinel scout, which is an honourable version of this and you know it
Orc — the Burning Blade has assassins and so does Thrall; you have probably worked for one of them
Dwarf — Ironforge does not produce many, and the ones it produces are very good

Playing One Here
Rogues are the class most likely to have a former employer who wants a word. Give yours a name at session zero — it is the cheapest campaign hook in this vault.
Related

Rules/Classes/Shaman.title: Shaman
Rules/Classes/Shaman.content:
Shaman



                  
                  At a glance 
                  
                






























Available toOrc, tauren, trollFaction lockHorde only5e chassisDruid, Cleric, or Barbarian depending on specSourcebookPath of the Elements Barbarian (new)Resource fantasyNothing you do is a command. Everything you do is a request.


In the World
Communion with the elements, and the most quietly remarkable story in the young Horde.
The orcs lost shamanism entirely when they drank Mannoroth’s blood — a whole tradition gone inside a single generation, the elements refusing to answer a people who had sold themselves. Thrall rebuilt it almost from nothing after Durnholde, and the tauren taught him, because their line never broke. Four years on, orcish shamanism is a revival, not an inheritance, and everyone practising it knows exactly how close it came to being lost.
Troll shamanism is a third thing again — sea, storm, and the loa, which is a different conversation with the elements than either of the others is having.
The Alliance has no tradition of it. Not a prohibition, an absence. Nobody in Ironforge or Stormwind City knows how to listen. See Classes of Azeroth for the arc if a player wants to be the first.
At Level 1
You are an apprentice who has been heard once. Not obeyed — heard. The elements are not servants and every elder you meet will remind you of this, at length.
Specializations


                  
                  Fit key 
                  
                

✅ Direct — the subclass does the thing · 🔄 Shared — same subclass as another spec, differentiated by flavour · 🟡 Close — works, loses something · 🔴 Gap — nothing in 5.5E does this































WoW Spec2024 SubclassFitWhyElementalDruid — Circle of the Sea🟡 CloseWrath of the Sea is Lightning Shield. But the 2024 PHB dropped Tempest Domain and has no Storm Sorcery — there is no lightning-caster subclass in the core rules at all. Circle of the Sea is an aura, not a nuker.EnhancementBarbarian — Path of the Elements (WoW book)✅ DirectElemental weapon enchantments on a melee rage chassis. Windfury as a subclass.RestorationCleric — Life Domain, or Druid — Circle of the Land🟡 CloseThroughput is there; stacking heal-over-time is not. Riptide and Healing Rain have no 5.5E analogue, and Chain Heal has no bouncing-heal mechanic.


                  
                  These features are not confirmed yet 
                  
                

The sourcebook’s subclass names are announced. Its mechanics are not. Everything in the table above is a reasonable prediction from a name and a WoW spec, not a reading of the book.
Early access is 3 November. Confirm on the day, and log anything that surprises you in the D&D World of Warcraft Sourcebook reconciliation table.


Alternate builds

Enhancement, unarmoured — Monk (Warrior of the Elements) with a weapon. 🟡 Close. Elemental strikes on a martial chassis. No armour and no totems, but it moves.
Elemental, fire-focused — Cleric (Light Domain). 🟡 Close. Lava Burst and Flame Shock, and the domain’s radiant damage reads as fire without argument.
Elemental, as a raw conduit — Sorcerer (Spellfire Sorcery, Heroes of Faerûn). 🟡 Close. Power drawn straight from the source with nobody’s permission — the best build for a troll or a self-taught orc, and it hits harder than Circle of the Sea.
Elemental, as a raw conduit — Sorcerer (Spellfire Sorcery, Heroes of Faerûn) reskinned. Better for a troll who was never formally taught.
Restoration, totem-forward — Druid (Circle of the Land) with Spike Growth, Plant Growth, and Wind Wall recast as totems planted in the ground.



                  
                  Totems 
                  
                

Totems are the visual signature of the class and 5e has no native mechanic for them. Reflavouring is free: any concentration spell with a fixed area becomes a totem you set down. A bespoke totem subsystem is under consideration in House Rules.


Species Pairings

Orc — you are part of a revival four years old. Your grandparents would not recognise what you are doing.
Tauren — your tradition is unbroken and you are patient with the orcs relearning theirs, mostly
Troll — the sea and the loa, which is a different conversation than either of the others is having

Playing One Here
The shaman is the class whose power can decline to help. Lean into it. When the elements go quiet in a place, that is worldbuilding, and the party will notice before you have to explain it.

Rules/Classes/Warlock.title: Warlock
Rules/Classes/Warlock.content:
Warlock



                  
                  At a glance 
                  
                






























Available toHuman, gnome, orc, ForsakenFaction lockNone — illegal on both sides, practised on both sides5e chassisWarlock (Fiend Patron)SourcebookClass skin onlyResource fantasyYou made one bargain and have not yet found the bottom of it.


In the World
Fel magic. Illegal in every jurisdiction on Azeroth and practised in all of them.
The Cleft of Shadow beneath Orgrimmar operates openly enough that Thrall must know and has chosen not to look, because the Burning Blade would be worse underground. Quiet cellars in Stormwind’s Mage Quarter do the same work with better manners. The Shadow Council never stopped existing; it simply stopped announcing itself.
Everyone knows it happens. Nobody wants to be the one who says so in a room where it can be minuted.
At Level 1
You are someone who made one bargain, for a reason that seemed sufficient at the time, and has not yet found out what it actually cost. Your imp is insulting and probably smarter than it lets on.
Specializations


                  
                  Fit key 
                  
                

✅ Direct — the subclass does the thing · 🔄 Shared — same subclass as another spec, differentiated by flavour · 🟡 Close — works, loses something · 🔴 Gap — nothing in 5.5E does this































WoW Spec2024 BuildFitWhyDestructionFiend Patron + Agonizing Blast✅ DirectEldritch Blast reskinned as Shadow Bolt is the single cleanest reflavour in this vault. Immolate and Conflagrate exist by name.DemonologyFiend Patron + Pact of the Chain🔴 GapYou get one familiar. Demonology’s fantasy is a field of demons, and 5e deliberately limits summoning for table-speed reasons. Pact of the Chain gets you an imp and nothing else.AfflictionFiend Patron + Pact of the Tome🔴 Gap5.5E has almost no damage-over-time. Corruption, Agony, and Unstable Affliction are a stacking-DoT rotation, and the core rules have perhaps three such spells. Curses and debuffs land; the spec’s engine does not.


                  
                  Destruction is the well-represented spec. Say so at session zero. 
                  
                

Neither Affliction nor Demonology is fixed by the WoW sourcebook — Warlock gets a class skin only. Destruction converts perfectly and the other two do not. That is worth saying out loud before a player builds, not after.
This does not mean the other two are unplayable. It means the flavour carries them and the mechanics will not: an Affliction warlock is a character who curses people and watches them rot, built on a chassis that resolves damage immediately. If the player is happy with that, it plays fine.
Alternatives worth a look: Undead Patron (Ravenloft) is the natural Forsaken warlock and gets closer to Affliction’s decay theme than Fiend does. Vestige Patron (Arcana Unleashed) is a bargain with something dead and specific, which suits a Shadow Council character.


The demons

























WoW5eImpImp (Pact of the Chain)VoidwalkerQuasit, or a reskinned HomunculusSuccubusSprite reskinned, or a Summon Fiend at higher levelsFelhunterPseudodragon reskinned, or a Find Steed variant
The demons

























WoW5eImpImp (Pact of the Chain)VoidwalkerQuasit, or a reskinned HomunculusSuccubusSprite reskinned, or a Summon Fiend at higher levelsFelhunterPseudodragon reskinned, or a Find Steed variant
Alternate builds

A warlock who was corrupted rather than contracted — Great Old One Patron. Better for The Old Gods than the Legion, and it makes the character’s power something that happened to them.
Destruction, as raw output — Sorcerer (Draconic Sorcery) reskinned as fel. Drops the pact fiction entirely; use only if the player wants the damage and not the story.
A warlock who thinks they are a mage — Wizard (Evoker) with the fel-flavoured spells. Excellent for a gnome in denial.



                  
                  Public exposure 
                  
                

A warlock casting in the street is a crime in Stormwind City, Ironforge, Darnassus, and the Undercity. Not a moral judgement — a legal one, with guards attached. Agree with the player at session zero how visible their magic is.


Species Pairings

Orc — your people were enslaved by exactly this power within living memory, and you took it up anyway. Every orc who learns will have an opinion.
Gnome — you did it out of curiosity, which most people find more alarming than desperation
Human — a bargain struck to save something, and you would do it again
Forsaken — you are already damned by most reckonings. It clarifies the risk calculation.

Playing One Here
The warlock is the party’s liability and knows it. That is a role, not a problem — but it works only if the other players are in on it.

Rules/Classes/Warrior.title: Warrior
Rules/Classes/Warrior.content:
Warrior



                  
                  At a glance 
                  
                






























Available toAll eight speciesFaction lockNone5e chassisFighter, or Barbarian for FurySourcebookClass skin only — no new subclassResource fantasyRage. You fight better the longer the fight goes on.


In the World
No institution, no initiation, no secret. Every settlement in Azeroth has someone who holds the line, and none of them call it a calling. Militias in Elwynn Forest, city guards in Ironforge, caravan escorts on the Barrens road, clan warriors in Durotar, mercenaries drinking through their pay in Booty Bay.
That universality is the point. Every other class on this list needs a teacher, an order, a bargain, or a bloodline. The warrior needs a weapon and a reason. In Year 29, both are easy to come by.
At Level 1
You are a volunteer who has survived two or three real fights. You own a weapon and you know what it is for. Nobody trained you formally — someone older showed you how to stand, and the rest you learned from people trying to kill you.
Specializations


                  
                  Fit key 
                  
                

✅ Direct — the subclass does the thing · 🔄 Shared — same subclass as another spec, differentiated by flavour · 🟡 Close — works, loses something · 🔴 Gap — nothing in 5.5E does this





































WoW Spec2024 SubclassFitWhyArmsFighter — Battle Master✅ DirectManeuvers are Mortal Strike, Overpower, and Colossus Smash: a limited pool of decisive strikes rather than a rotation.FuryBarbarian — Path of the Berserker🟡 CloseDual-wielding rage that trades defence for output. Reckless Attack is Recklessness. Loses the building of rage — 5e Rage is a duration you enter, not a meter you fill.ProtectionFighter — Banneret (Heroes of Faerûn)🟡 CloseCommanding Shout and Rallying Cry as real mechanics — a warrior who holds the line by commanding rather than by soaking.ProtectionFighter — Champion, shield and Protection style🟡 CloseThe no-book version. Durable and simple; mechanically just “more crits wearing a shield”.


                  
                  There is no threat mechanic in 5.5E, and that is fine 
                  
                

No taunt, no aggro table, no Shield Slam. The sourcebook adds no warrior subclass — Warrior gets a class skin only — so the book is unlikely to change this. 5e assumes positioning does the job that threat does in WoW.
Play the flavour instead. A Protection Warrior at this table is the one who steps in front, shouts, and does not move. Banneret gives you the shouting, the Sentinel feat and the Protection fighting style give you the stepping-in-front, and Goading Attack from Battle Master covers a ranged pull. That is the whole fantasy without a threat subsystem underneath it.
Barbarian (Path of the World Tree) is the alternative — temporary hit points and yanking allies out of danger reads as Shield Wall and Intervene.


Alternate builds

Arms, without the bookkeeping — Fighter (Champion) with a greatsword. Crits on 19. No maneuver economy to track.
Fury, for a player who wants spell-free complexity — Fighter (Battle Master) with two-weapon fighting, taking the aggressive maneuvers only.



                  
                  Rage at the table 
                  
                

5e has no rage meter, and it does not need one. Barbarian Rage covers Fury and Protection; Fighter’s Second Wind and Action Surge cover Arms. If a player wants the feel of building fury, see House Rules.


Species Pairings

Orc — born free in Durotar, and tired of being told you don’t understand what that cost
Tauren — you have taken the Rite of Strength and killed a Bristleback chief; nothing since has been as frightening
Human — Stormwind Army, either still serving on nine copper a day or resigned over something you won’t discuss
Forsaken — you fought in life. The reflexes came back before the memories did.
Night elf — Sentinel. Four years mortal and still adjusting to what a wound means now.
Dwarf — Ironforge mountaineer, or Explorers’ League muscle who has been down more holes than any scholar
Gnome — small, fast, and furious about Gnomeregan
Troll — Darkspear, and the tribe has been fighting for its life for four straight years

Playing One Here
The warrior is the class with no cosmic problem. Nobody’s god went quiet, nobody’s academy burned, nobody’s bargain came due. That makes you the party’s anchor — and it means your story has to come from what you want, not from what was taken.
Good warrior questions for session zero: Who taught you? Are they alive? What are you being paid, and by whom? What did you do in The Third War, if you were old enough?

Rules/Death-and-Resurrection.title: Death and Resurrection
Rules/Death-and-Resurrection.content:
Death and Resurrection


                  
                  The ruling 
                  
                

No spirit healers. No corpse runs. No graveyard respawns. Death in this Azeroth works the way death works in D&D 5.5E — and that means it is rare, expensive to undo, and permanent when the party cannot pay.
The videogame’s revolving door is held in reserve as a plot device.



Why This Ruling
Every other system in this vault runs on the assumption that loss is real. The Forsaken are a people defined by having died. Start — Deathknell (Forsaken) opens with a character waking in a box. The Doom Clocks work because consequences stick.
A world with spirit healers on every hilltop has none of that. The moment dying is free, the Scourge stops being frightening.

What Death Costs

























LevelRealistic Recourse1–4Almost none. A cleric of the Order of the Silver Hand or a Cenarion Circle druid might be reachable, and will ask for something the party cannot casually give.5–8Revivify exists in the world but is held by named NPCs, not sold. Getting the body to one in time is an adventure.9–14Raise dead is obtainable in a capital. It costs money, a favour, and a debt — and the recipient carries a penalty for weeks of in-world time. Use a time skip.15+Available to those with standing. The question stops being can we and becomes what do we owe now, and to whom.

The Light Does Not Fix Everything
A useful in-world constraint, and it is period-correct:

The Light cannot restore what has been claimed. Anyone killed by the Scourge and raised by it is beyond ordinary resurrection.
Fel damage scars. Death by demonic means complicates every attempt.
Forsaken PCs are already dead. They do not benefit from resurrection magic at all; restoring a destroyed Forsaken is a different, darker, and entirely unsolved problem. Establish this at session zero with any Forsaken player.

Magic Schools and Damage Types
Azeroth runs on six. Everything resistible falls into one.








































SchoolSources5e EquivalentPhysicalSteel, claws, fallingBludgeoning / piercing / slashingFireMages, Ragnaros, the Dark IronFireFrostMages, the Scourge, NorthrendColdNatureDruids, shamans, poison, silithidPoison / lightning / acidShadowWarlocks, shadow priests, the Void, The Old GodsNecrotic / psychicArcaneMages, the Blue Dragonflight, Kirin TorForce


                  
                  The Light is not a school 
                  
                

The Holy Light is its own thing — the province of paladins and priests, opposed to Shadow, and mechanically radiant. It resists nothing and is resisted by little; undead and demons take it badly. This is deliberate. In 2004 the Light is a faith, not a physics.


Resistance Gear
Resistance sets are a defining vanilla ritual. Preserve the idea, not the spreadsheet.

Rules/Playable-Species-at-Launch.title: Playable Species at Launch
Rules/Playable-Species-at-Launch.content:
Playable Species at Launch
Eight, and only eight. Four to a side.


                  
                  "Species", not "race" 
                  
                

The 2024 revision of D&D renamed race to species, and split ability score bonuses out of it entirely — those now come from your background. So a Tauren is not stronger than a gnome on the character sheet; a tauren warrior is stronger than a gnome scholar, because of what they did with their life.
This is a better fit for Azeroth than the old rules were. Nothing about being orcish makes you good at fighting. Being raised in Durotar in Year 29 does.


Alliance



































SpeciesHomeCapitalFlavourHumansElwynn ForestStormwind CityResilient, short-lived, politically fracturedDwarvesDun MoroghIronforgeTitan-forged, archaeologically obsessedNight ElvesTeldrassilDarnassusNewly mortal after ten millenniaGnomesDun Morogh(exiled to Ironforge)Homeless, irradiated, undeterred
Horde



































SpeciesHomeCapitalFlavourOrcsDurotarOrgrimmarFreed from demonic taint, rebuilding honourForsakenTirisfal GladesUndercityUndead, free-willed, morally unresolvedTaurenMulgoreThunder BluffSpiritual, patient, newly settledDarkspear TrollsDurotar(guests in Orgrimmar)Displaced, voodoo-practicing, wry

Mapping to 5.5E
All eight are covered by the D&D World of Warcraft Sourcebook — five as remapped Player’s Handbook species, and Forsaken, Tauren and troll as new ones.


                  
                  Use the book's versions 
                  
                

Character creation happens after the sourcebook ships, so the official species are the ones we use. No stand-ins, no homebrew stat blocks, no “take Human and add these three traits.”

















AzerothSourcebookHumans · Dwarves · Night Elves · Gnomes · Orcs2024 PHB species with WoW-mapping rulesForsaken · Tauren · TrollNew species, built for this




                  
                  What I do not know yet 
                  
                

Whether the book’s Forsaken carry an undead trait package the way the game does — no eating or breathing, poison and disease immunity, and the Light healing them at reduced effect. Whether troll Regeneration made it in at all. Whether species grant a starting Renown Score and how that lands against Reputation as a Mechanic.
I get early access on 3 November. Anything surprising goes in the reconciliation table on D&D World of Warcraft Sourcebook.



❌ Not Available


                  
                  These do not exist as options in 2004 
                  
                

Blood elves and draenei arrive with The Burning Crusade (2007). Blood elves exist in lore — Kael’thas Sunstrider leads them through the Dark Portal — but they are offscreen and not Horde. Draenei as presented in TBC required a full retcon of what “draenei” even meant in 2004; the only draenei on Azeroth at launch are the degenerate Lost Ones in the Swamp of Sorrows.
Worgen, goblins, pandaren, dracthyr, earthen, mechagnomes, nightborne, void elves, vulpera, haranir — all post-launch as playable species. Note this is a species list, and it mostly does not gate classes: the Monk is open without pandaren being available. The one place the two are locked together is dracthyr and the Evoker, and both are cut. Goblins exist as a people and make excellent NPCs and, arguably, neutral-party PCs. Worgen exist as Archmage Arugal’s monsters. Pandaren appear as a Warcraft III easter egg only.



The Exotic Exception


                  
                  Decided 
                  
                

One or two exotic species across the whole party. Not one or two each — one or two total, agreed at session zero, by conversation rather than first-come.
The D&D World of Warcraft Sourcebook adds eight species beyond our eight, and some of them are more defensible in 2004 than people assume. Species of the Sourcebook has the verdict on every one, ranked.


The short version, best to worst for a Year 29 campaign:








































SpeciesWhy1WorgenAlready loose in Silverpine Forest and Duskwood. Play a victim of Archmage Arugal, not a Gilnean. Costs the setting nothing.2PandarenOne traveller from a place nobody can find. No homeland on the map, no contradiction possible.3MechagnomeReskin as a Gnomeregan survivor rebuilt in mechanical parts. Delete Mechagon entirely.4DraeneiOnly as a single castaway who came through the Dark Portal fifteen years ago. Heavy retcon.5EarthenCanon-legal, but it costs the campaign a reveal I want to keep. Ask me; I will probably say no.—Vulpera, dracthyr, haranirNo. Nothing to hang them on in 2004.


                  
                  Why an exception at all 
                  
                

Because a player who is excited about a character will play that character better than one who settled. The canon boundary exists to make the world feel like 2004, not to win an argument.
An exotic PC should be the only one of their kind anyone in the party has met. That is the price of admission and it is also the best thing about it.


High Elves — A Narrow Exception
A handful of High Elves remain Alliance-loyal at launch and are visible in game — Allerian Stronghold’s forebears, the Silvermoon delegation in Stormwind City, Dalaran survivors in the Kirin Tor. Not a playable option in 2004, but the most defensible import if a player wants one, and it does not count against the exotic budget above.
Use Elf (High Elf lineage) from the 2024 PHB. Prestidigitation, Misty Step, and a levelled spell — mechanically the most magical of the elf lineages, which is exactly right.


                  
                  My ruling 
                  
                

A high elf PC is fine. A blood elf PC is not — the sin’dorei are through the Portal with Kael’thas Sunstrider and their arc has not happened yet.




                  
                  One exception, and only one 
                  
                

A blood elf Demon Hunter. Illidan’s first sin’dorei intake is the only demon hunter recruitment happening on any world in 2004, so that character has to be a blood elf — there is no other way to build them.
This does not open blood elves generally. There are no blood elf mages, rogues, or warriors, Quel’Thalas stays a ruin offscreen, and Silvermoon does not go on the map. One character, one route, came back alone. See Demon Hunter.


Choosing a Class To Go With It
Each species suits some classes for reasons rooted in its history, not its stat block. Classes of Azeroth is the hub, with a page for every one of the thirteen — what the class means in Year 29, what a level 1 of it actually looks like, every WoW spec mapped to a 2024 subclass, and specific species pairings worth stealing.


                  
                  The short version 
                  
                

Orc shaman — reviving a tradition the Legion destroyed. Tauren druid — first generation, no elders. Forsaken anything — you remember your living career. Night elf druid — asleep for the whole Third War. Gnome rogue — trained in a city that no longer exists. Forsaken priest — the Light burns you and you use it anyway. Troll hunter — the raptor is not tame, and that is understood by both of you.


Related
Classes of Azeroth · Species of the Sourcebook · Canon Boundary — What Exists at Launch · Peoples MOC · Lore MOC

Rules/Professions-and-Crafting.title: Professions and Crafting
Rules/Professions-and-Crafting.content:
Professions and Crafting
Primary Trades





































ProfessionTabletop HandlingBlacksmithingSmith’s tools. Armorsmith / weaponsmith branch at high skill.LeatherworkingLeatherworker’s tools. Dragonscale, elemental, tribal branches.TailoringWeaver’s tools. Bolt-based; mooncloth and shadowcloth need special sites.EnchantingNo 5e analogue — treat as a downtime activity. Requires disenchanting magic items.EngineeringTinker’s tools. Goblin and gnomish branches are mutually exclusive and both explode.AlchemyAlchemist’s supplies. Potions, elixirs, transmutation.Herbalism / Mining / SkinningGathering. Handle with a check against terrain.
Secondary
First Aid (bandages — a real combat action in vanilla) · Cooking (buff food, campfires) · Fishing (patient, occasionally lucrative)
Rules of Thumb

Specialization is exclusive. Goblin or gnomish engineering, never both. Choosing is characterization.
Recipes are treasure. A pattern from the Thorium Brotherhood is a reward on par with a magic item.
Gathering is a reason to travel. Arcane crystals in Winterspring. Black lotus in Silithus. Thorium in Searing Gorge.
Crafting takes downtime, not a rest. Days, not minutes.

Reputation as a Mechanic
Vanilla’s eight-rank ladder, run as a real subsystem rather than a progress bar.
Hated → Hostile → Unfriendly → Neutral → Friendly → Honored → Revered → Exalted
Running It
Track a simple score per faction, −3 to +4:


















































ScoreRankWhat It Means At The Table−3HatedAttacked on sight. Bounty posted.−2HostileRefused service, followed, reported−1UnfriendlyPrices doubled. No favors.0NeutralTransactional. They don’t know you.+1FriendlyFair prices, minor favors, gossip+2HonoredReal discounts, safehouses, introductions+3ReveredTheir trained members assist. Restricted goods.+4ExaltedYou are one of them. Titles, mounts, secrets.
Shift a rank when the party does something a faction genuinely cares about — not per quest turned in.

Rules/Species-of-the-Sourcebook.title: Species of the Sourcebook
Rules/Species-of-the-Sourcebook.content:
Species of the Sourcebook
The D&D World of Warcraft Sourcebook offers 16 species — 11 new, plus WoW-mapping rules for 5 that already exist in the 2024 Player’s Handbook. This page is the verdict on each, measured against the canon boundary.


                  
                  The short version 
                  
                

All eight launch species are covered by the book. Nothing you need is missing. Eight other species are on offer and seven of them are post-2004.
I will allow one or two exotic species across the whole party, by conversation, at session zero. Not one or two each. See Playable Species at Launch.



Your Eight Are All In There









































Launch SpeciesWhere It Comes FromHumans2024 PHB Human, with WoW-mapping rulesDwarves2024 PHB Dwarf, with WoW-mapping rulesNight Elves2024 PHB Elf, with WoW-mapping rulesGnomes2024 PHB Gnome, with WoW-mapping rulesOrcs2024 PHB Orc, with WoW-mapping rulesForsakenNew speciesTaurenNew speciesTrollNew species
That is a clean fit. The five PHB species get Azeroth-specific rules rather than a reprint, and the three the PHB could not cover are built from scratch.

The Other Eight — Verdicts
Ranked by how little damage they do to a 2004 campaign.
✅ Worgen — the best exception
In the world at launch: yes. This is the one people forget. Worgen are already loose in Year 29 — Archmage Arugal summoned them from the Emerald Dream to fight the Scourge in Silverpine Forest, lost control, and they have spread through Shadowfang Keep and into Duskwood. The Nightbane pack in Duskwood is a live quest chain at launch.
What does not exist yet is Gilneas as a playable homeland. The Greymane Wall is sealed, the nation is silent, and the Gilnean worgen curse story is a Cataclysm plot six years out.


                  
                  The version I would run 
                  
                

A victim, not a nation. Someone from Silverpine or Duskwood who was bitten by Arugal’s pack and did not fully turn. Horror, not heritage. No Gilneas, no Greymane, no worgen society — you are the only one you have met who kept their mind.
That character has a natural enemy (Archmage Arugal), a natural fear (the next full moon), and a reason to travel. It is the strongest exotic pick on this list.


Faction: neither. A worgen PC at launch is an outcast from both, which is a feature.

✅ Pandaren — charming, low damage
In the world at launch: barely. Chen Stormstout was a Warcraft III hero unit and that is the complete canon. Pandaria is behind the mist and will be for eight years.
But “a wandering brewmaster from a land nobody has heard of” costs the setting almost nothing, because nobody in Azeroth can contradict them. The mystery is the character.


                  
                  The version I would run 
                  
                

One traveller, no homeland on any map, no Shado-Pan, no Celestials. When asked where Pandaria is, the honest answer is “I could not find it again if I tried.”
The Monk is open now, so a pandaren brewmaster works exactly as a player would expect. Note that Brewmaster specifically needs the WoW sourcebook — see Monk.


Faction: neutral, which suits a party leaning one way and wanting a bridge.

⚠️ Mechagnome — needs a reskin, then it works
In the world at launch: no, but the parts are. Mechagon is a Battle for Azeroth zone from 2019. However — Gnomeregan fell to radiation four years ago, gnomish prosthetics and clockwork limbs are everywhere in Ironforge’s Tinkertown, and things were done to some of the survivors down there that nobody has catalogued.


                  
                  The version I would run 
                  
                

A Gnomeregan survivor whose irradiated body was rebuilt in mechanical parts — by choice, by necessity, or by someone else’s decision. Use the mechagnome stat block, delete every reference to Mechagon and King Mechagon, and call it what it is: a gnome who was repaired.


Faction: Alliance, Gnomeregan Exiles.

⚠️ Draenei — possible, as a castaway
In the world at launch: no. The Exodar crashes on Azuremyst in 2007. The only draenei on Azeroth in Year 29 are the Lost Ones — degenerate, hostile, and living in the Swamp of Sorrows and Blasted Lands near the Dark Portal.
The playable draenei required a full retcon of what “draenei” meant in 2004. Importing one means importing the retcon.


                  
                  The version I would run 
                  
                

A single uncorrupted exile who came through the Dark Portal with the Horde’s invasion and has been hiding in the Blasted Lands for fifteen years. No Exodar, no Prophet Velen, no naaru — one person from a world that the orcs destroyed, who recognises every orc they meet.
That is a strong character with a real relationship to Draenor’s fall. It is also a lot of retcon to carry.


Faction: would be Alliance, but arrives with no ties to anyone.

⚠️ Earthen — mechanically fine, narratively a landmine
In the world at launch: yes, asleep. Earthen are titan-forged and they are in Uldaman right now, in stasis, at level 35ish. The species itself arrives playable with The War Within in 2024.
The problem is not canon. The problem is that an earthen PC would put a mid-campaign revelation on the character sheet at session zero.
Faction: Alliance by default, but an earthen predates the concept of factions and would find them baffling.

❌ Vulpera — no
Battle for Azeroth, 2018. Vol’dun does not exist, Zandalar is closed, and there is no vulpera presence anywhere in the Eastern Kingdoms or Kalimdor in 2004.


                  
                  If someone loves the concept 
                  
                

Reskin as a small desert-nomad people out of Tanaris with Steamwheedle Cartel ties, mechanically identical, called something else. That is homebrew rather than import, and I would rather do it honestly.



❌ Dracthyr — no, and the Evoker goes with them
Dragonflight, 2022. Asleep in the Forbidden Reach since before The Second War, created by Neltharion, unknown to everyone including the other Aspects.
A dracthyr PC hands the party a walking piece of Neltharion’s laboratory at level one, and The Dragon in the Court depends on the Black Dragonflight’s works staying hidden.


                  
                  Both are cut 
                  
                

Dracthyr are not available, and neither is the Evoker. The two are locked together in WoW and I am keeping them locked together here. This is the one entry on this page with no exception route.
A player who wants dragon magic takes Sorcerer (Draconic Sorcery) with a Red Dragonflight or Blue Dragonflight blessing in their bloodline. Same mechanics, no spoiled secret, and it plugs into Alexstrasza and Malygos instead of a laboratory nobody should know about. See Classes of Azeroth.



❌ Haranir — no
Midnight, 2026. From the Underhold beneath Khaz Algar, a continent that has not been discovered. There is not enough published lore for me to reskin it into 2004 honestly, and no in-world hook to hang it on.

Summary Table



























































SpeciesIn 2004?VerdictReskin NeededWorgenYes, as Arugal’s victimsBest exceptionDrop GilneasPandarenWarcraft III cameo onlyAllowedDrop Pandaria as a placeMechagnomeParts, not the speciesAllowed with reskinGnomeregan, not MechagonDraeneiLost Ones onlyDM approvalCastaway, not ExodarEarthenAsleep in UldamanDM approval — spoiler costNone; that’s the problemVulperaNoNoWould be full homebrewDracthyrNoNo — and the Evoker is cut with them—HaranirNoNo—

Renown
The sourcebook ties species to a starting Renown Score with one of its 20+ factions, built on the Dungeon Master’s Guide renown rules. That is close to what Reputation as a Mechanic already does here.


                  
                  How I am handling the overlap 
                  
                

My eight-rank reputation ladder came first and is tuned to this campaign’s factions. When the book ships I will map its renown values onto my ladder rather than run two systems. Logged in D&D World of Warcraft Sourcebook.
The species-grants-starting-renown idea is good and I am keeping it: a Darkspear troll should not start at zero with the Darkspear Tribe.

Rules/Travel-and-Downtime.title: Travel and Downtime
Rules/Travel-and-Downtime.content:
Travel and Downtime


                  
                  Decided at the table 
                  
                

Hearthstones exist, once per week. Flight paths exist and are expensive. Ground mounts are the normal way to cover distance. No spirit healers and no corpse runs — see Death and Resurrection.



Getting Around


















































MethodAvailabilityCost & LimitsFootEveryoneDefault. Small zone: half a day. Large zone: 2–3 days.Ground mountPurchasable from ~tabletop level 4Horse, ram, mechanostrider, saber, wolf, kodo, raptor, skeletal steed. Faction-locked and culturally specific — a dwarf on a kodo is a story.Flight pathBetween known, allied roosts onlyExpensive. Gryphon (Alliance), wyvern (Horde), hippogryph, bat. See pricing below.ShipFixed routes, fixed schedulesMenethil ↔ Theramore ↔ Auberdine ↔ Darnassus · Booty Bay ↔ Ratchet. Days at sea, weather, naga.ZeppelinOrgrimmar ↔ Undercity ↔ Grom’golGoblin-built. This should worry passengers.Deeprun TramStormwind ↔ IronforgeTwo hours, beneath the sea, free. A genuine marvel.HearthstoneOne per character, bound to one innOnce per week. See below.Mage portalMage PCs, or hiredCapitals only. Ruinous if hired at low level.

The Hearthstone
Every character may attune one hearthstone to one inn. Rebinding takes an hour with the innkeeper and can be done anywhere with a bound inn.
Usage: once per seven days. Track it on the character sheet, not in your head — the players will.
Good reasons the stone fails, established in advance and telegraphed:

Deep beneath Blackrock Mountain — the ley interference is audible as a hum
Inside Ahn’Qiraj’s walls or a Titan vault
Aboard a ship at sea, or anywhere in The Emerald Dream
Anywhere the Twilight’s Hammer have prepared ground on purpose


Flight Path Costs
Flight is fast and it should hurt to use. Price it as a real budget decision at levels 1–8, and a convenience by level 12.

























DistanceRough CostFeels LikeOne zone hopSmall but noticeable”Do we need to?”Cross-continent, 3–4 legsA meaningful chunk of party fundsA planned expenseEmergency, unlinked roostRefused at any priceRoosts must be visited on foot first

Time Skips and Artificial Breaks


                  
                  The scheduling tool 
                  
                

The world in The Doom Clocks and World Events Calendar needs time to pass for its consequences to land. The party will not naturally take year-long breaks. So build them in.


Legitimate reasons to skip weeks or months, in rough order of usefulness:








































BreakLengthFictionWinter6–10 weeksPasses close in Dun Morogh. Seas unsafe. Campaigning stops because campaigning does stop.Training2–6 weeksA new tier of ability requires a trainer, a capital, and time. Cover for a level-up.Recovery2–8 weeksA serious wound, a curse, a resurrection debt. See Death and Resurrection.Crafting or commission3–12 weeksResistance gear, a forged weapon, a chartered shipWaiting on the worldanyA trial date, a thaw, a shipment, a birth, a siegePolitical delay4–12 weeksThe Senate votes in spring. The hearing is set for autumn. Nothing the party does moves it.
During a skip, always:

Advance the relevant clocks and read the World Events Calendar for the months crossed.
Give each PC one downtime action (below).
Deliver one piece of bad news the party could have prevented had they been there. Not a punishment — physics.
Change one price. Every clock has an economic shadow.


Downtime Activities
One per character per skip, unless the skip is long.

Craft — see Professions and Crafting
Curry favour — advance a faction’s regard (Reputation as a Mechanic)
Research — libraries in Ironforge, Darnassus, the Kirin Tor in exile, the Explorers’ League
Train — new abilities require a trainer in a capital. This is the usual cover for levelling.
Carouse — Goldshire, the Pig and Whistle, Thelsamar. Roll on Rumor Tables twice and let them keep both.
Work a trade — mercenary contracts, caravan guard, bounties. Pays, and generates hooks.
Tend a relationship — an NPC from Characters MOC. Genuinely the highest-value option and players under-use it. Say so.

index.title: The Booty Bay Chronicle
index.content:
Printed in Booty Bay, where we sell to anyone who pays and ask nobody their
business. Year 29 since the opening of the Dark Portal.


New here? Start with the Player Primer.
It covers the world, the two factions, and what kind of game this is — about
five minutes, no prior Warcraft knowledge assumed.


Browse





























Humans · Orcs · Dwarves · Night Elves · Tauren · Trolls · Gnomes · ForsakenThe peoples of AzerothThe Alliance · The HordeWho’s who, and why they don’t trust each otherElwynn Forest · Durotar · Teldrassil · Mulgore · Dun Morogh · Tirisfal GladesWhere you might beginIronforge · Orgrimmar · Thunder Bluff · DarnassusThe great citiesPlayable Species at Launch · Classes of Azeroth · Death and ResurrectionRules that affect your character
Search is top left. Everything is cross-linked — follow a name and you’ll
usually end up somewhere useful.

The state of things
Lordaeron is gone. Destroyed from within by an undead plague. Its survivors
are refugees; its capital is a graveyard.
Stormwind stands, barely. A ten-year-old king, a regent doing his best, an
empty treasury, and provinces that have noticed nobody is coming to help.
The orcs have a homeland for the first time — a red desert nobody else
wanted, with a city four years old built out of raw timber and iron.
The night elves are mortal now, after ten thousand years, and they are not
handling it well.
There is no war and there is no peace. Alliance and Horde raid each other
over lumber and old grudges while both leaderships insist it isn’t a war.


A note on our editorial standards. The Chronicle prints what walks in off
the docks and what our correspondents can verify. We do not print rumour, we
do not print what the Steamwheedle Cartel would rather we didn’t, and we
certainly do not print anything a paying customer hasn’t yet earned the right
to know.
If a page you expect is not here, that is not an oversight. Ask your DM.
